Detail: Operation Romeo commenced, an organised police crackdown in the Maoist heartland of Rolpa. Reportedly aimed at rooting out the Maoists and their sympathisers, the operation resulted in mass human rights abuses, 132 arrested, 6000 displaced, and the arbitrary detention, torture, execution and enforced disappearance of hundreds.
Keywords: security offensive, Nepal police, Rolpa, pre-conflict, human rights violations, state, police

Detail: and 2006, the Government of Nepal and the Communist Party of Nepal (Maoist) fought a war that killed at least 13,000 people, forcibly disappeared over 1,300, and displaced and tortured thousands more. Reports and documentation from survivors, human rights organizations, international organizations, the United Nations, media, and national bodies record atrocities committed by both sides.
Maoists attack a police post in Holeri, Rolpa, announcing the launch of their 'people's war'.
Keywords: conflict onset, Maoist offensive, Holeri, Rolpa,  Maoist

Detail: Launch of Armed Insurgency
Maoists Claim Responsibility
Government Hardline Response
Prime Minster Deuba convenes an all-party meeting concerning the conflict, but the issue is largely substantively dismissed.
Keywords: political dialogue, lack of political commitment, state

Detail: Dil Bahadur Ramtel (11/12), a student from Pandung, Gorkha, is shot and killed by police during protests against the arrest of a school headmaster. He is widely regarded as the first martyr of Nepal's Maoist insurgency.
Keywords: police shooting, civilian killing, school, student, Gorkha, violence, civilian, protests

Detail: First Recorded Conflict Death: Dil Bahadur Ramtel
Maoist leader Baburam Bhattarai submitted a 40-point demand to Prime Minister Sher Bahadur Deuba, who dismissed it and traveled to India for a state visit.
Keywords: 40-point demand, ultimatum to government, state rejection of demands, Singha Durbar Kathmandu, Maoist, state

Detail: The state launches a harsh police crackdown in the midwestern hills. However, police violence against civilians feeds the Maoist insurgency with fresh recruits.
Keywords: security offensive, human rights violations, civilian affected, insurgent recruitment, Rolpa, Rukum, Mid-western, state, Maoist

Detail: Maoists boycott local elections, eight people are killed in campaign violence. The government forms a taskforce to find a political solution to the conflict.
Keywords: election, political dialogue initiative, non-military response, nationwide, violence, Maoist, state

Detail: Local Election Boycott and Violence

The government attempts to introduce anti-terrorism legislation through the Terrorist and Disruptive Activities (Control and Punishment) Act ('TADA'), but the proposed Act is withdrawn following widespread opposition from civil society groups.
Keywords: legislative attempt, civil society opposition, anti-terrorism, state

Detail: Anti-Terror Law Debate

As part of the negotiation of TADA , the government publicly characterises the Maoist Insurgency as a 'terrorist' and 'disruptive' movement, signaling a shift from treating the conflict solely as a law-and-order issue toward a national security concern.
Keywords: anti-terrorism, counterterrorism, conflict securitization, Kathmandu, state

Detail: By this time, more than 50 Village Development Committees ('VDC') in Rolpa alone are under Maoist control.
Expansion Beyond the Mid-West

Operation Kilo Sierra II: Girija Prasad (G.P.) Koirala-led government expands police counter-insurgency operations across 18 districts, marking a major escalation of the conflict. By the end of 1998, 500 people have been killed under suspicion of holding Maoist sympathies.
Keywords: security offensive, human rights violations, civilian affected, state, Maoist, civilian killing, nationwide

Detail: Police arrested Gopal Siwakoti Chintan, Executive Director of INHURED and Secretary General of the Nepal Concern Society, from the Nepal Concern Society office, and confiscated audio and video materials of human rights victim interviews and seminars, amid the intensified police campaign against alleged Maoist supporters.
Keywords: civil society, human rights defender, arbitrary detention, INHURED, Nepal Concern Society, police, 1998
Organizations: Nepal Police; INHURED; Nepal Concern Society

Detail: The Maoists expand out of the midwestern hills for the first time into central Nepal and the eastern hills.
CPN–UML leader Yadu Gautam is assassinated by Maoist insurgents.
Maoist Urban Bombings in Kathmandu
Maoist insurgents start a campaign under which select enemies would be physically eliminated.
Keywords: targeted killing, violence, campaign, military campaign, maoist

Detail: Maoists strike in Kathmandu, detonating bombs at the offices of the Election Commission and Gorkhapatra, the largest circulated Nepali newspaper.
Keywords: Maoist offensive, media, state, bomb attack, violence, Maoist

Detail: Parliamentary elections are held and the Maoists call for a boycott. Krishna Prasad Bhattarai becomes prime minister and he appoints Sher Bahadur Deuba to lead a committee tasked with finding a solution to 'the Maoist problem'.
Keywords: election, conflict resolution, legislative attempt, committee,

Detail: Parliamentary Elections Held

Anti-Terror Legislation Fails to PassThe government introduces amendments to internal security law like Terrorist and Disruptive (TADO) aimed at strengthening measures against terrorism and insurgency. The proposal faces political opposition and does not pass Parliament.

The Government introduces Nepal Laws Relating to Internal Administration (Amendment) Bill to Parliament, aimed at strengthening powers to bring 'terrorist activities' under control. Opposition Members of the House of Representatives reject the Bill on September 21.
Keywords: counterterrorism, legislative attempt, state, parliament, Kathmandu

Detail: Opposition Members of the House of Representatives reject the Bill.

At the end of Amnesty International’s Kathmandu visit led by Secretary General Pierre Sané, Nepali authorities released Suresh Ale Magar and Pawan Shrestha, who had been re-detained (“disappeared”) by police immediately after a Supreme Court-ordered release from Kathmandu Central Jail on 23 December 1999. Amnesty urged investigation of remaining disappearance cases it had raised with the government.
Keywords: enforced disappearance, Amnesty International, secret detention, Suresh Ale Magar, Pawan Shrestha, civil society pressure, Kathmandu
Organizations: Amnesty International; Nepal Police; Supreme Court of Nepal

Detail: Maoists waylay a bus in Dolakha district carrying Polish tourists and rob them of about US$ 5,000 in cash. This is the first major incident by Maoists targeting foreign visitors.
Keywords: Maoist, Maoist offensive, civilian, Central, Dolakha

Detail: During commemorations of the fourth anniversary of the 'People's War', Maoist leader Pushpa Kamal Dahal 'Prachanda' issues a press statement saying the Maoists may now be willing to negotiate with the government to end violence, killings and abductions, if the government agrees to certain conditions.
Maoists Signal Possible Negotiation

Amnesty International Secretary General Pierre Sané issued a public statement in Kathmandu during an AI delegation visit, urging Nepali political leaders to place human rights at the centre of efforts to end the “people’s war,” condemning abuses by both state security forces and the CPN (Maoist), and joining Nepali human rights defenders in demanding accountability for disputed “encounter” killings and secret detention.
Keywords: Amnesty International, Pierre Sané, civil society, human rights advocacy, Kathmandu, people's war, accountability

Detail: Maoists use the chaos in Kathmandu to continue attacks on police posts and government offices. Police start pulling out of rural areas in the Midwest.
Keywords: Maoist offensive, violence, Nepal police, Maoist, state, Mid-western

Detail: G.P. Koirala again becomes Prime Minister after Krishna Prasad Bhattarai resigns following pressure for his inability to contain the Maoist insurgents.

Nepal’s National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) was formally established under the Human Rights Commission Act 1997, after years of delay and following a Supreme Court mandamus directing the government to constitute the Commission. It began operating as an independent statutory body to investigate and monitor human rights violations amid the escalating armed conflict.
Keywords: NHRC, National Human Rights Commission, institutional monitoring, Supreme Court mandamus, civil society, Kathmandu
Organizations: National Human Rights Commission of Nepal; Government of Nepal; Supreme Court of Nepal

Detail: Maoist insurgents surround a police post manned by 53 police personnel in Jajarkot district and attack with mortars and bombs. Nine policemen, seven civilians and 21 insurgents are killed in the incident.
Keywords: security offensive, human rights violations, civilian, insurgent recruitment, Rolpa, Rukum, Mid-western, state, Maoist/

Detail: Maoist leadership rejects an offer of negotiations made by the government as, in their opinion, the government failed to create the minimum favorable environment for negotiations.

Hundreds of Maoist guerrillas stormed Dunai, Dolpa district headquarters, on the night of 25 September 2000, attacking the police office and jail, freeing prisoners, looting Nepal Bank, and killing about 14 policemen — the first Maoist assault on a district headquarters. Home Minister Govinda Raj Joshi later resigned amid criticism that the army failed to reinforce the police.
Keywords: Maoist offensive, violence, Nepal police, Maoist, Dolpa

Detail: Deputy PM Ram Chandra Poudel meets Maoist leader Rabindra Shrestha in Kathmandu to attempt to negotiate a solution to the conflict.
Keywords: Political dialogue, dialogue initiative, Maoist, state

Detail: Government establishes the Armed Police Force, a paramilitary force tasked with counter-insurgency operations.
Keywords: Armed Police Force, counterterrorism, counterinsurgency, state

Detail: Government forms special tribunal under the State Offences and Punishment Act, to prosecute crimes against the state, particularly those committed by Maoists.

Unified Command Structure EstablishedFollowing the collapse of peace talks and declaration of the State of Emergency, the Royal Nepal Army, Nepal Police, and Armed Police Force are brought under a unified counter-insurgency command. The move marks the transition from a police-led response to a nationwide military campaign and the beginning of the conflict's most violent phase.
Keywords: Nepal Army, APF, police, peace process
Organizations: Royal Nepal Army, Nepal Army, Armed Police Force, Nepal Police

Detail: Former King promulgates the Armed Police Ordinance intended to activate the Armed Police Force (APF) and make arrangements for its deployment against the Maoist insurgents.
Keywords: Armed Police Force, counterterrorism, counterinsurgency, state

Detail: Maoist insurgents ambush the convoy of the country's Chief Justice, Keshav Prasad Upadhyay, who narrowly escapes the attack, in Chhyasatti, Surkhet, 500km west of Kathmandu. Six others, including a judicial officer, are killed in the attack.
Keywords: Mid-western, Maoist offensive, violence, targeted killing, state, Maoist

Detail: The eve of the fifth anniversary of the commencement of the 'People's War' brings about an escalation in insurgent activities. Maoists use the anniversary to announce the Prachanda Path doctrine, the ideological line of the Maoist party drawn from Marxism-Leninism-Maoism.

Maoists set all documents on fire at the Bahrabise bazaar police station. They also set the Samdu police post, near Mayanglung, on fire. In another attack on security forces, the Maoists injure a policeman at the Madhumalla police station and cut off the limbs of a school teacher in Shantipur, near Gulmi.
Keywords: Maoist, Nepal police, Maoist offensive, school, human rights violations

Detail: The government and Maoist insurgents unofficially consider peace talks.
Keywords: Maoist, state, political dialogue, dialogue initiative

Detail: Prime Minister G.P. Koirala makes a fresh initiative to end the five-year old insurgency and offers to hold talks with the Maoists. Human Rights activist Tuladhar and others also involve themselves in working out the mechanism to bring the Maoist insurgents and the government to the negotiating table.
In a wave of attacks in Rukum and Dailekh, Maoists kill 70 policemen in a week and loot weapons. The paramilitary Armed Police Force is set up.
Keywords: Maoist offensive, Maoist, Nepal police, Armed Police Force, Mid-western, Far-western

Detail: In a nation-wide address, Prime Minister G.P. Koirala appeals to the Maoists to end violence and surrender weapons, while assuring them of a general amnesty.
CPN-UML calls for a three-day nation-wide general strike, which turns violent. All ten leftist parties in the country extend support to the strike.
The royal massacre occurs, resulting in the deaths of nine members of the royal family. A government-appointed inquiry confirmed Crown Prince Dipendra as the perpetrator.
The royal massacre, three kings in four days.
Prince Gyanendra, brother of Birendra is crowned King after late King Birendra's son, Dipendra––who had been declared King on June 2––succumbs to injuries sustained during the palace shooting.
Maoists begin attacks against public schools and declare war on alcohol.
Nine Maoist insurgents, including five women cadres, are killed in attacks on three police outposts in Lamjung, Gulmi, and Nuwakot.
Keywords: Maoist offensive, security offensive, Nepal police, Central

Detail: Maoist insurgents set off explosions near the residence of Prime Minister G.P. Koirala at Biratnagar. However, no one is killed or injured in the incident.
Keywords: State, bomb attack, Maoist, Maoist offensive

Detail: Deputy Prime Minister and Home Minister Ram Chandra Paudel resigns from the Cabinet, saying democracy in Nepal is in crisis.
Prime Minister G.P. Koirala resigns. He is replaced by Sher Bahadur Deuba.
Maoist insurgents declare cease-fire.
Maoist Ceasefire Declared
The government holds first talks with the Maoists.

Madhab Kumar Nepal and Bamdev Gautam meet Prachanda in Siliguri in India. At the first round of talks between the Maoists and the government, the Maoists demand abolition of constitutional monarchy, rewriting of the Constitution, and establishing an interim government to facilitate transition to a republic.
Keywords: Dialogue initiative, political dialogue, state rejection of demands, Maoist, state, ultimatum to government

Detail: First Round of Talks

A second round of talks between the government and the insurgents ends inconclusively as the Maoists insist on the formation of a Republic and setting up of a Constituent Assembly to review the Constitution.
Keywords: Dialogue initiative, political dialogue, state rejection of demands, ultimatum to government

Detail: Armed Police Force Formally EstablishedThe Armed Police Force (APF) is formally established as a specialized paramilitary force to strengthen internal security and support counter-insurgency operations.
The Defence Ministry announces that the US government has made a commitment to supply Nepal with 10 modern, fully armed military helicopters to 'fight terrorism'.

A third round of talks between the government and Maoist insurgents ends in deadlock. Government insists on making changes to the Constitution now in force to accommodate Maoist demands, but refuses to abrogate it. The Maoists stick to their demand that a Constituent Assembly be convened to further ensure people’s rights. Significantly, the Maoists drop their demand for a Republic.
Keywords: Dialogue initiative, political dialogue, state rejection of demands, ultimatum to government

Detail: Third Round of Talks Deadlocks

Maoist insurgents trash the ongoing truce and during the night, attack the Army barracks in Ghorai, Dang district, killing 14 soldiers and injuring 30 more. Insurgents announce the formation of a central People’s Revolutionary Government with Babu Ram Bhattarai as Chief Convenor of the Maoist parallel government. Insurgents attack the airport in Surkhet and blow up a privately-owned helicopter, damaging two more.
Keywords: Maoist offensive, military campaign, Moist, state, violence, bomb attack, Mid-Western

Detail: Ghorahi/Dang Attack and Collapse of Ceasefire
The king declares a state of emergency in the country and orders the deployment of troops against the Maoists.
State of Emergency and Army Deployment
Terrorism Ordinance 2001 passed, expanding government powers to declare and address terrorism.
Keywords: Legislative attempt, counterterrorism, conflict securitisation, state

Detail: Terrorism and Disruptive Ordinance (TADO) Passed
Tourism collapsed, investment fell sharply, and industries were hit by Maoist extortion and threats, deepening the economic hardship of ordinary civilians across Nepal.
48 Royal Nepal Army troops and 49 police were killed in Maoist attacks in Mangalsen, Acham district, marking one of the deadliest single incidents of the conflict for security forces.
Keywords: Nepal Army, police, Maoist, Acham, killing, clash

Detail: The United States designated the Communist Party of Nepal (Maoist) a terrorist organization, internationalizing the conflict and influencing Nepal's counter-insurgency strategy.
Five female prisoners escaped from Gorkha prison, including Kamala Naharki, Anjila BK, Sanju Aryal, Mina Marahatta, and Uma Bhujel, a section commander of the Maoist People's Liberation Army.

According to UN Human Rights Committee findings in Fulmati Nyaya v. Nepal, a 14-year-old indigenous Tharu girl (pseudonym Fulmati Nyaya) from Kailali District was arrested by security forces in April 2002, sexually assaulted during transfer, then detained and repeatedly raped and otherwise sexually tortured by Armed Police Force / army personnel at Banbehda, Kailali. (Committee Views adopted 18 March 2019 — already in mastersheet.)
Keywords: Fulmati Nyaya, conflict-related sexual violence, child rape, Tharu, Kailali, Armed Police Force, Royal Nepal Army, detention
Organizations: Armed Police Force; Royal Nepal Army

Detail: TADO Becomes Law (TADA Act)The TADO is converted into the Terrorist and Disruptive Activities (Prevention and Punishment) Act, providing expanded legal powers for counter-insurgency operations.

Conflict Intensifies NationwideParliament is dissolved, the state of emergency continues, and military operations expand across the country. International military support from India, the United States, and the United Kingdom increases.
Security forces threatened the parents of Bipin Bhandari at gunpoint, demanding his whereabouts, illustrating the direct targeting of civilian families by security forces.

During intensified conflict and Deuba’s outreach to Western partners (including a meeting with US President George W. Bush), the United States pledged on the order of US$20 million in emergency/supplemental assistance related to Nepal’s campaign against the Maoist insurgency, and the United Kingdom announced substantial military-related support (later detailed as about £6.5 million for hardware/helicopters/training). India separately offered support (already in mastersheet as 18 May 2002).
Keywords: United States, United Kingdom, military aid, counter-insurgency, Deuba, internationalisation
Organizations: United States; United Kingdom; Government of Nepal

Detail: 32 Maoist insurgents were killed in a security forces operation on the Dang-Kailali border.

Nepal’s Defence Ministry reported that security forces killed about 90 Maoist fighters in overnight fighting in western Nepal — roughly 40 at Lisne, Rolpa, and about 50 at Bhagal on the Doti–Kailali border (figures are government claims; some later statements raised Rolpa tolls dramatically and were not independently confirmed). Two security personnel were also reported killed.
Keywords: Rolpa, Doti, Kailali, Lisne, security forces, casualty claims, counter-insurgency
Organizations: Royal Nepal Army / security forces; CPN-Maoist

Detail: India offered support to Nepal in its fight against the Maoist insurgency, further internationalizing the conflict.

Facing defeat on extending the state of emergency, Prime Minister Sher Bahadur Deuba recommended dissolution of the House of Representatives; King Gyanendra accepted. Deuba announced November elections and defended the move in a 24 May national address; the Nepali Congress later expelled him from the party for dissolving parliament without consultation.
Keywords: Deuba, parliament dissolved, House of Representatives, state of emergency, elections, Gyanendra, political crisis

Detail: The state of emergency was extended for three months through executive order, continuing the suspension of civil liberties for ordinary Nepalis.
100 Maoist insurgents were killed in a failed attack on the Army camp in Rukum district.

Bipin Bhandari Forcibly DisappearedBipin Bhandari, a 21-year-old student leader from Salyan associated with the Maoist student movement, is arrested by security forces from a hideout in Kathmandu and subsequently disappears. His whereabouts remain unknown. The case becomes one of Nepal's most emblematic enforced disappearance cases and symbolizes the suffering of hundreds of families affected by disappearances during the conflict.
28 Maoist insurgents were killed in separate security force operations.
Police killed a senior Maoist leader at Sukdhev Chowk, Rautahat district.
A high-intensity bomb exploded at the headquarters of Prime Minister Deuba's Nepali Congress faction in Kathmandu, injuring 10 civilians.
Maoist insurgents killed a former police officer in Dang district, targeting an ex-security force member living as a civilian.
RNA troops killed a Maoist area committee member in Jumla district.
Eight Maoist insurgents were killed in countrywide counter-insurgency operations.
The government issued a red corner notice against Maoist supreme commander Prachanda.
Maoist insurgents killed a Rashtriya Praja Party activist and injured a CPN-UML sympathizer, continuing the pattern of targeting political party members.
Maoist insurgents abducted a Nepali aid worker employed with a British charity near the Rolpa-Pyuthan border, demonstrating the targeting of humanitarian workers.
15 Maoist insurgents were killed in counter-insurgency operations in Dolkha district. A security force member and two local residents were also injured.
60 Maoist insurgents surrendered in Okhaldhunga and 19 more in Nuwakot district.
86 Maoist insurgents surrendered across Kavre, Bhaktapur, and Khotang districts.
Pro-Maoist students detonated a blast at a college in Kathmandu, injuring six civilians including students.
Prachanda offered peace talks; the government rejected negotiations until the Maoists laid down arms, illustrating the early pattern of failed dialogue.
10 insurgents were killed in Banke district. Interpol issued red notices for senior Maoist leaders including Prachanda and Baburam Bhattarai.
The Army reported over 2,290 Maoist deaths since the resumption of the conflict in November 2001, reflecting the scale of casualties in under a year of renewed fighting.
30 Maoist insurgents were killed in Thawang village, Rolpa district, in the largest Army operation since May 2002.
Home Minister Devendra Raj Kandel survived a Maoist ambush, demonstrating the targeting of senior government officials.
Nine insurgents were killed in a separate Army operation in Dolpa district.
Maoist insurgents robbed Nepal Bank in Rautahat district.
Two insurgents and one police officer were killed and three people injured.
33 insurgents surrendered in Sindhupalchowk.
Five Nepali Congress activists and one CPN-UML activist were massacred by insurgents in Ramechap district, continuing the pattern of targeting political party members.
State of Emergency EndsThe state of emergency declared after the breakdown of peace talks formally expires.
The state of emergency, originally declared on 27 November 2001, expired.
Bhimad Police Post AttackOne of the deadliest attacks on police during the conflict results in heavy casualties among both police personnel and Maoist combatants.
At least 50 insurgents were also killed and 11 policemen reported missing.
Nine policemen were killed in a Maoist ambush near the Mahendra Highway in Siraha district.
Six troops were injured in a separate ambush in Dang district.
A nationwide general shutdown called by Maoist insurgents disrupted civilian life across Nepal including Kathmandu, affecting livelihoods and freedom of movement.
Gopal Bishwakarma, president of the Bardia Nepal Dalit Sangh, a Dalit rights organization, was killed by Maoists, illustrating the targeting of marginalized community leaders.
17 insurgents were killed in clashes with troops in Rolpa district.
55 insurgents were killed in Rukum and 14 in Rolpa. Prachanda and Baburam Bhattarai offered a conditional ceasefire pending peace talks.
Keywords: Prachanda, Rukum, Rolpa, killing, peace process

Detail: At least 74 insurgents were killed in a major Army operation in Rolpa district.
Deuba proposes postponing elections because of the security situation. King Gyanendra dismisses him, assumes executive authority and sets up a government of technocrats.
Royal Takeover of Executive AuthorityKing Gyanendra dismisses Prime Minister Sher Bahadur Deuba and assumes executive authority, deepening Nepal's political crisis.
Lokendra Bahadur Chand assumed charge as caretaker Prime Minister.

Maoist insurgents attacked Rumjatar airport in Okhaldhunga district. One Army captain and two soldiers were killed alongside 42 insurgents, illustrating the conflict's reach into civilian infrastructure.
Insurgents killed four policemen at a post near Butwal.
Insurgents beheaded three soldiers found in civilian dress in Nuwakot district.
Five journalists detained on alleged Maoist affiliations were released.
At least 20 more journalists remained in detention, reflecting the widespread suppression of press freedom during the conflict.

Jumla Attack — Major Maoist attacks targeted Jumla airport and security posts; Chief District Officer Damodar Pant was among those killed, along with two civilians, and security-force casualty claims reported large police and soldier losses (SATP attributing roughly 33 police and 4 soldiers among SF deaths that night). Attacks also damaged airport and police infrastructure in Jumla district headquarters.
Keywords: Maoist, clash, Damodar Pant, CDO, Jumla airport

Detail: At least 55 insurgents were also killed. In separate clashes in Gorkha district, 23 policemen and at least 63 Maoist insurgents were killed. Former Member of Parliament Chakra Bahadur Chaudhary of CPN-UML was killed at his residence in Dhangadhi, continuing the pattern of targeting elected officials.
At least 50 Maoist insurgents were killed in ground and aerial attacks in Lamjung district.
Maoist insurgents offered peace talks with the interim government, reiterating demands for a round table conference, an interim government, and a constituent assembly.
Insurgents attacked Lahan in Siraha district, killing three policemen and looting NR 30 million in cash and jewelry.
First State Rehabilitation PlanningThe National Security Council prepares an early concept paper on disarmament, rehabilitation, and support for conflict victims.
Lok Bahadur Thapa, advisor of the Maoist parallel government, surrendered to authorities in Kaski district.
Six policemen were injured in a Maoist ambush in Bara district.
Maoists released 18 school children previously kidnapped in Kailali and Doti districts.
Maoist insurgents killed five security force personnel at Gawar, 350 kilometers west of Kathmandu.

Maoists abducted 150 children from a school in Bajura district. 140 of the 250 students previously kidnapped from schools in Dang district were released. 17 suspected Maoist insurgents held for nearly a year in Nuwakot were freed.
Security forces killed 11 Maoist insurgents in operations across Bardia, Rukum, Accham, Kanchanpur, and Jajarkot districts.
Maoist insurgents abducted six CPN-UML activists, including former Member of Parliament Dhanharka Rai, from a public meeting in Bhojpur district.
Inspector General of Police Krishna Mohan Shrestha and his wife were murdered in Kathmandu.
Maoists abducted a policewoman, Sudha Rana, in Dhangadi district — the first reported abduction of a policewoman. She was released the following day.
Four CPN-UML activists, including former Member of Parliament Dhana Harka Rai, previously abducted in Bhojpur, were also released.
The Nepal Maoist Victims Association announced a three-phase campaign to pressure the government for relief for conflict victims.
Armed Police Force Chief Inspector General Krishna Mohan Shrestha, his wife, and his bodyguard were killed in a Maoist attack in Kathmandu.
Keywords: APF, police, Maoist, Kathmandu, killing, clash

Detail: Maoists also abducted 36 students from Milan Pokhari Lower Secondary School in Gulmi district.
Maoist leader Prachanda announced a ceasefire.

The government reciprocated, announcing a truce and appointing Minister Narayan Singh Pun as coordinator for peace talks. 16 Maoist insurgents were killed in separate security force operations across the country.
CPN-UML leader Madhav Kumar Nepal called on the Maoists to clarify the modalities of their demands for a round table conference and constituent assembly.
The Maoists announced a five-member dialogue committee headed by Baburam Bhattarai for peace talks.
The government sent an official invitation to the Maoists for dialogue.
Maoists attacked Dang and Khotang districts, violating the ceasefire.
The Defence Ministry accused Maoists of resuming abductions and extortion and sent a draft code of conduct for their comments.

Two school students were killed and one injured when Maoist insurgents opened fire at a school in Baglung district. The insurgents later claimed they had been conducting a firing demonstration for children.
Maoist leaders asked human rights activists Padma Ratna Tuladhar and Daman Nath Dhungana to act as facilitators in peace talks.
The killers of Armed Police Inspector General Krishna Mohan Shrestha, his wife, and bodyguard were identified as Krishna Hari Sainju, Kamala Bista, Gopal Krishna Nagarkoti, and Sita Karanjit.
Two Maoist insurgents were killed in an encounter with security forces in Bajhang district.
Government coordinator Narayan Singh Pun announced peace talks would be held in the second week of March.
Police in Bihar, India, uncovered a Maoist hideout and recovered a large cache of arms and ammunition.
A Maoist insurgent was arrested in Birgunj after extorting NR 100,000 from a businessman.
Cases were filed at the Patan Appeals Court against Maoist leaders Prachanda, Baburam Bhattarai, and others for their role in the killing of 49 policemen in Sindhuli.
Maoist leaders expressed anger at the cases filed against them, warning the move undermined the government's commitment to dialogue.
Army personnel arrested four insurgents during an extortion attempt in Lalitpur. Several more were arrested in Kathmandu.
14 insurgents detained at Mahendranagar jail beat up guards and escaped.
Maoists damaged a telecommunications repeater station in Accham district, violating the ongoing truce.
Government chief negotiator Narayan Singh Pun and Maoist parallel government head Baburam Bhattarai signed a 22-point code of conduct to govern the peace process.
Kamal Thapa was appointed as a monitoring team member from the government side to oversee ceasefire violations.
Maoists abducted Nepali Congress (Democratic) Pyuthan district chairman Shalikram Pandit and another local leader.
Maoist leader Mahara set preconditions for peace talks, demanding the release of five central-level leaders and withdrawal of cases against Prachanda and Baburam Bhattarai.
The Supreme Court ordered the release of pro-Maoist journalists Ram Karki and Maheshwore Dahal. Several Maoist insurgents were released from different jails, though some were rearrested.
Insurgents abducted two policemen from Parsa district.
Government chief negotiator Pun announced peace talks would commence on 1 April.
Maoist chief negotiator Bhattarai came overground in Kathmandu along with other members of the rebel negotiating team.
Maoist chief negotiator Bhattarai met Prime Minister Lokendra Bahadur Chand at a public meeting in Kathmandu, calling for fresh elections to resolve the political crisis.
Bhattarai discussed peace talks with Rashtriya Prajatantra Party chief Pasupati SJB Rana.
Maoists suspended peace talks, citing the government's failure to withdraw cases against Prachanda and Bhattarai.
Bhattarai admitted Maoist involvement in the killing of Armed Police Force Inspector General Krishna Mohan Shrestha, his wife, and bodyguard on 26 January.
Government negotiator Narayan Singh Pun stated the government would not release all Maoist prisoners.
Bhattarai demanded the immediate release of Maoist prisoners, or at least five central committee members, to resume peace talks.
Maoist negotiator Dev Gurung said insurgents were ready to withdraw their demand for a new Constituent Assembly.
Nuwakot District Security Committee freed eight imprisoned Maoist insurgents.
Two Maoist central committee members, Krishna Dhoj Khadka and Rekha Sharma, were released from prison. Bhattarai met government negotiator Narayan Singh Pun for talks.
The government announced a six-member team for peace negotiations with Maoists.
Government negotiator Pun announced the first round of goodwill talks would be held on 21 April.
The 21 April preliminary talks were postponed.

Four opposition parties — Nepali Congress, CPN-UML, Samyukta Janamorcha, and Nepal Majdoor Kishan Party — refused to join the government's proposed committee for talks, calling the government illegal.
Maoists allegedly abducted 27 civilians from Taplejung, Tanahu, and Sarlahi districts.
Government and Maoist leaders agreed to hold peace talks on 27 April.
The Home Secretary and US Ambassador signed a joint agreement on countering terrorism.
First Round of 2003 Peace Talks

Maoists submitted a 35-point agenda. Former Speaker Daman Dhungana and human rights activist Padma Ratna Tuladhar were appointed as facilitators from the Maoists' side, while former Minister Shailendra Kumar Upadhaya and former Chief Secretary Karna Dhoj Adhikari were nominated from the government side.
The United States included Maoist insurgents in its list of other terrorist organizations.
Peace talk facilitators met Prime Minister Chand and Maoist chief negotiator Bhattarai separately to discuss the future course of talks.
Maoist chief negotiator Bhattarai criticized the US designation of Maoists as a terrorist organization.
Maoists allegedly abducted three government officials at Makalu.
Maoist insurgents allegedly abducted three journalists at Mehalamudi.
The RNA warned Maoists would pay a heavy price if they withdrew from peace talks. The US Ambassador stated the Maoists could be removed from the terrorist list if they terminated violence.
The three journalists abducted from Mehalamudi on 4 May escaped from Maoist captivity and reached Kalikot.
Second Round of Talks
The second round of peace talks began in Kathmandu.
The government agreed to restrict Army movement within five kilometers of barracks in Maoist areas and to release three Maoist central committee members.
Maoist insurgents opened a contact office at Shanti Galli in Anamnagar, Kathmandu.
Maoist insurgents allegedly abducted 20 persons in Panchthar district.

Maoist chief negotiator Bhattarai put forth five demands including the release of central committee members and restriction on Army movement. Bhattarai also met the 11-party coalition supporting anti-King agitation.

Government negotiator Narayan Pun confirmed the decision to restrict security force movement taken at the second round of talks. The 11-party coalition decided to form an 11-member committee including Maoists to draft a common programme for peace talks.
Maoist insurgents allegedly abducted nine persons from the Tharu community in Kailali district, illustrating the targeting of indigenous communities.
Prime Minister Lokendra Bahadur Chand resigned.
King Gyanendra appointed Rashtriya Prajatantra Party leader Surya Bahadur Thapa as the new Prime Minister.
Maoists demanded the release of three central committee members.
Change in Government
Maoist leader Prachanda stated the new government had no fundamental difference from the previous one.
Maoists announced a peaceful movement and formed a nine-member committee for the success of peace talks and to oppose foreign intervention.
Maoist leader Ram Bahadur Thapa announced his party's readiness to give up arms if security forces reciprocated.

King Gyanendra announced a seven-member Council of Ministers headed by Prime Minister Surya Bahadur Thapa. A joint security patrol arrested 17 Maoists, including two women cadres, in Darchula district.

The government announced Finance Minister Prakash Chandra Lohini and Communications Minister Kamal Thapa as official negotiators for peace talks. Bhattarai alleged the King was undermining the constitution and warned Maoists may return to the forests if talks failed.
Maoist leader Mahara stated no third round of peace talks would be held unless previous agreements were implemented.
Kamal Thapa announced former Foreign Minister Shailendra Kumar Upadhaya and retired Chief Secretary Karna Dhoj as government facilitators for peace talks.
Two soldiers were killed and four others injured in an encounter with Maoists in Dang district.
Maoist-affiliated Kirat Workers' Party activists abducted the principal of a local school in Dhankuta district.
Army and Maoists exchanged fire in western Nepal. The Army reported around 300 Maoists were involved.
The government opened a coordination secretariat for peace talks in Kathmandu.
The government and Maoists accused each other of ceasefire violations.
Two Maoist insurgents were killed and five injured in a clash with security forces in Jajarkot district.
The Army accused Maoists of resuming arms training in remote districts and threatening people not to attend government health camps, directly impacting civilians' access to healthcare.
A Maoist insurgent was killed in an encounter with the Army at Kulung.
Maoist leader Prachanda sent 24-point demands to five opposition political parties.
Maoists abducted two political activists from Jumla district.
Maoist leader Prachanda asked the government to present its agenda for the third round of peace talks.
Maoist leader Krishna Bahadur Mahara stated that restrictions on Army movement would not impede peace talks.
Peace talks facilitator Padma Ratna Tuladhar announced that the government and insurgents had agreed to participate in the third round of talks.
Maoist leader Krishna Bahadur Mahara stated that the right to revolt and multi-party democracy would be key elements of their envisaged political setup.
Government negotiators and Maoists held an informal meeting at an undisclosed location in Kathmandu.
Maoists reiterated demands for the release of three central committee members and restrictions on Army deployment.
The Royal Nepal Army reiterated it had received no orders from the government on restricting its movement.
A Maoist platoon commander was arrested in Rautahat district.
Security forces destroyed a Maoist training camp in Panchthar district.
Negotiators from the government and Maoists met unofficially in Kathmandu.
Maoists abducted two Army personnel and three civilians from Makwanpur district.
Three Maoists were released from prison in Kathmandu.

Government spokesperson Kamal Thapa sent a letter to Bhattarai proposing a date for peace talks. Bhattarai stated that forming an interim government under Maoist leadership would be the prime agenda in the talks.
Security forces arrested Maoist contact office secretary Bharat Dhungana in Kathmandu.
Maoist high command held a meeting in Surkhet-Jajarkot to discuss government proposals.
Maoists closed their contact office in Kathmandu.
Maoists killed a retired police officer in Ilam district, targeting an ex-security force member living as a civilian.
The government assured safe passage for Maoist peace team members during talks, even if negotiations failed.
Maoist insurgents abducted six persons in Sankhuwasabha district.
50 armed Maoists attacked a police post at Sugauli Customs Office in Parsa district and seized a dozen weapons.
Security forces arrested seven members of the Maoist student wing ANNISU-R.
Seven Maoists, including two women insurgents, declared their decision to abandon the organization.
Maoist leader Bhattarai proposed direct talks with the King and asked the King to publicly authorize the government as his representative.
A woman Maoist insurgent was killed by security forces in Kalikot district.
Maoist leader Prachanda addressed the first national convention of the Kirat National Front in Panchthar, an ethnic insurgent group in eastern Nepal.
The government sent a letter to Maoists calling for a third round of peace talks.
Peace facilitators met to discuss the third round of peace talks.
Maoists sent a response letter to the government carrying five demands.
The government released three Maoist central committee members — Rabindra Shrestha, Bamdev Chhetri, and Mumaram Khanal — from prison.
Government spokesperson Kamal Thapa stated the Army would not act against Maoists except in self-defense.
Opposition parties welcomed the Maoist response to peace talks and demanded a fully authorized all-party government to participate in negotiations.

The government presented its agenda and agreed to hold a round table conference and form an interim government as demanded by the Maoists.

Security forces killed 16 Maoist insurgents in separate operations across the country.

Four security force personnel were killed and 11 others injured in a Maoist ambush in Makwanpur district. Defence Secretary Madan Prasad Aryal survived repeated assassination attempts by Maoists in Makwanpur.

The Maoist student wing ANNISU-R called an indefinite strike for the release of imprisoned leaders, leading to the closure of 93 schools in Baglung district and depriving hundreds of children of education.

12 insurgents, including the vice-chairman of a Maoist village government, surrendered at the district administration office in Okhaldhunga district.

The UN World Food Programme and German Technical Cooperation suspended their food-for-work programme in Bajura district following Maoist looting, directly cutting off humanitarian food assistance to civilians.

Maoists killed at least two soldiers and injured 10 others in an ambush in Khotang district.

The World Bank warned in its Country Assistance Strategy 2004–2007 that Nepal would drift into a failed state if the eight-year armed conflict was not resolved, highlighting the conflict's devastating impact on national development.

35 schools in Mugu district resumed functioning after an agreement between the Maoist student wing and school administrations, reflecting the widespread disruption to children's education caused by the conflict.
17 Maoist insurgents were killed in separate incidents across the country.
Security forces killed four insurgents, including the Maoist people's government chief, in Sankhuwasabha district.
Maoists killed the Mayor of Birgunj and Rashtriya Prajatantra Party member Gopal Giri, continuing the pattern of targeting elected officials.

King Gyanendra dismissed the government of Prime Minister Sher Bahadur Deuba, assumed direct executive power, and declared a state of emergency. Telephone and internet communications were cut and the Army was deployed into newsrooms. Hundreds of politicians and civil society activists were detained. The move drew widespread international condemnation. On the same day, 14 insurgent bodies were recovered from a clash site in Dhanusha district.

Maoists abducted a former British Gurkha soldier, Dan Bahadur Limbu, from Tehrathum district.
A Maoist insurgent was killed in an encounter in Gulmi district.
Maoists announced programmes to disrupt the municipal polls scheduled for 8 February 2006, including actions against candidates and election officials.
Two civilians were killed and two others injured in a landmine explosion in Taplejung district.
Two Maoists and a soldier were killed in an armed clash in Rolpa district.
A Maoist was shot dead by security forces during a search operation in Dang district.

Maoist chairman Prachanda announced the end of the four-month unilateral ceasefire. The RNA's Human Rights Report 2061 recorded 10,725 abductions and 72 killings by the Maoists in the preceding six months, along with 65 explosions, 40 cases of extortion and looting, and 30 cases of threats.
Keywords: Nepal Army, Maoist, Prachanda, abduction, killing, peace process, extortion/land

Detail: Devi Sunuwar, mother of Maina Sunuwar — the 15-year-old girl abducted, raped, and killed by Royal Nepal Army personnel in February 2004 — established the Maina Bal Bikas Samiti (Maina Child Development Committee) in her daughter's memory, working to defend human rights, support conflict-affected families and marginalized children, and advocate for truth and justice.

The Guru Luitel Study and Development Centre was established by the family of Guru Prasad Luitel, a schoolteacher and district president of the All Nepal National Teacher Organization in Okhaldhunga, who was kidnapped and killed by Maoist forces in 2003 at the age of 41. The Centre advocates for justice and preserves his memory, later coordinating with local municipalities to establish a Guru Luitel Memorial Park in Rampur village, where he was killed.
Armed conflict resumed following the end of the ceasefire.
A civilian was injured during a series of Maoist-triggered blasts in Pokhara, including one at the residence of a Deputy Superintendent of Police.
Three police personnel were killed and two injured in a Maoist attack on an Armed Police Force checkpoint at Ranjha Chowk in Nepalgunj, Banke district.
Keywords: APF, police, Maoist, Banke, Nepalgunj, killing, clash

Detail: A Maoist was killed in a clash with security forces in Rautahat district.
Maoists killed two children, aged two and five, from the same family by detonating a bomb inside a house in Dolpa district.
Maoists raided the Rastriya Banijya Bank's district branch in Surkhet district and looted over NR 3 million.
Seven police personnel were killed in a Maoist attack at Dhangadhi, headquarters of Kailali district. 12 Maoists were killed in two separate encounters in Syangja and Tanahun districts.

12 security force personnel were killed and eight persons injured in a series of Maoist attacks on police posts across the Kathmandu Valley. 16 insurgents and a soldier were killed during clashes in Syangja district.
Keywords: police, Maoist, Syangja, Kathmandu, killing, clash

Detail: One civilian was killed when a security patrol and Maoists exchanged fire in Banke district.
A Maoist was killed and two persons, including a civilian, were injured in a shootout between insurgents and security forces in Dang district.

Maoists shot and injured two police personnel at a post in Mahendranagar Bazaar, Kanchanpur district. Over 150 persons, including leaders of the seven-party alliance, human rights activists, and student leaders, were arrested to prevent a planned opposition rally in Kathmandu.

In a nationwide crackdown ahead of royal municipal elections, security forces arrested CMDP leaders including Krishna Pahadi, Dr Devendra Raj Panday, and others (with Amnesty later naming Dr Mathura Prasad Shrestha and journalist Shyam Shrestha among detained peace activists), alongside scores of political leaders — over 100 under the Public Security Act that morning per OHCHR-Nepal reporting. Amnesty designated key CMDP detainees prisoners of conscience.
Keywords: CMDP, arbitrary detention, Public Security Act, Krishna Pahadi, Devendra Raj Panday, OHCHR-Nepal, civil society, Kathmandu
Organizations: Citizens’ Movement for Democracy and Peace; OHCHR-Nepal (monitoring); Amnesty International (advocacy)

Detail: Six police personnel were killed and four others injured in simultaneous Maoist attacks on security checkpoints and the customs office in Nepalgunj, Banke district.
Keywords: police, Maoist, Banke, Nepalgunj, killing, clash

Detail: The government issued three-month house arrest orders against Nepali Congress president Girija Prasad Koirala, CPN-UML general secretary Madhav Kumar Nepal, and Nepal Workers' and Peasants' Party chief Narayan Man Bijukche.
17 Maoists, six security force personnel, and two civilians were killed in a clash in Makwanpur district.
Three insurgents were killed in encounters in Palpa and Tehrathum districts.
Suspected Maoists shot dead Bijaylal Das, president of the Nepal Sadbhavana Party, at Janakpurdham in Dhanusha district, continuing the pattern of targeting political party leaders.
The RNA claimed at least 25 Maoists were killed in Palpa district.
Two security force personnel, one Maoist, and a civilian were killed in simultaneous Maoist attacks in Nepalgunj, Banke district.
Five insurgents were killed when a bomb they were carrying accidentally exploded in Siraha district.
At least 11 insurgents and two soldiers were killed in overnight clashes in Bhojpur district.
Two Maoists were killed in a clash with security forces in Khotang district. A woman was killed and another injured in crossfire between security forces and Maoists in Nepalgunj district.
At least 11 soldiers were killed in Tansen, headquarters of Palpa district, during overnight clashes with Maoist insurgents.
King Gyanendra addressed the nation, asserting improvements in security and governance over the past year, and refused to give up his direct rule as demanded by the seven-party opposition alliance.
An elected ward chairman of Biratnagar municipality, Triveni Majhi, was seriously wounded in a suspected Maoist attack in which civilian Dipak Gurung was killed.
At least three persons, including two Maoists, were killed in an explosion in Morang district.
An APF officer was killed and four others injured in a Maoist bomb explosion on the Mahendranagar-Dhangadhi Highway in far-western Nepal.
At least five persons were killed when Maoists attacked an RNA base camp and the Panauti municipality office in Kavrepalanchowk district.
Keywords: Nepal Army, Maoist, Panauti, Kavrepalanchowk, killing, clash

Detail: Five security force personnel and a Maoist section commander were killed in a Maoist attack on a patrol team in Udayapur district.
Municipal elections were held with an average voter turnout of only 20 percent, reflecting widespread public rejection of the royal government's electoral process.
Maoists and mainstream parties boycotted the polls.
Maoists killed a police officer and a civilian, bombed 12 government buildings, and destroyed a local bank in Dhankuta.
16 security force personnel, four Maoists, and a civilian were killed in clashes on the Sidhhartha Highway in Nawalparasi district.
A woman was killed in a landmine explosion in Rupandehi district.
Former Prime Ministers Sher Bahadur Deuba and minister Prakash Man Singh were released from RCCC custody.
Three RNA soldiers were killed in a clash with Maoists on the Nawalparasi-Palpa border.
Keywords: Nepal Army, Maoist, Nawalparasi, killing, clash

Detail: One civilian was killed in a Maoist IED blast in Parsa district.
Three Maoists, including a woman cadre, were killed, and a child nearby was injured, when a bomb they were carrying accidentally exploded in Makwanpur district.
The government extended the house arrest of CPN-UML General Secretary Madhav Kumar Nepal by two months.
Maoists shot dead Nepali Congress activist Bindeshwore Yadav in Dhanusha district.
16 Maoists were killed during a clash in Palpa district.
Three security force personnel and a civilian were killed in a Maoist attack in Kavrepalanchowk district.
Five persons were killed in a bomb blast in Mangalsen, headquarters of Achham district.
At least 29 persons — 18 Maoists and 11 security force personnel — were killed in a clash on the Arghakhanchi-Palpa border.

Maoists detonated pressure cooker bombs at four offices in Jhapa district, including a UN World Food Programme branch, the Land Revenue office, Nepal Telecom, and the Agriculture Development Bank. No casualties were reported.
One police officer was killed and over a dozen others injured when a large group of Maoists launched coordinated attacks on key government installations in Ilam Bazaar, headquarters of Ilam district.
At least nine persons were killed — two civilians, three soldiers, and four Maoists — in a Maoist attack in Ilam district.
Maoists freed all 103 prisoners, including 32 insurgents, from the district prison.
Four security force personnel were killed and five others injured in a Maoist bomb explosion at a temporary security post in Dang district.
At least five Maoists were killed in an encounter in Rautahat district.
Seven soldiers were killed during clashes with Maoists in the southern part of Ilam district.

Maoists imposed an indefinite blockade of Kathmandu and other major towns, ordering the closure of all roads to the capital. Vehicular movement was completely disrupted in Siraha, Saptari, Udaypur, Biratnagar, Dhankuta, Jhapa, Ilam, Chitwan, Pokhara, Butwal, Nepalgunj, and Mahendranagar.
Keywords: Maoist, Kathmandu, Siraha, Saptari, Biratnagar, Jhapa, Ilam, Chitwan, Pokhara, Nepalgunj

Detail: Maoist chairman Prachanda expelled two senior leaders, Ravindra Shrestha and Mani Thapa alias Anukul, from the organization.
One security force personnel and a Maoist insurgent were killed in an encounter in Jhapa district.

Maoists shot dead two civilians, Wakil Musalman and Murtara Dewan, in Nawalparasi district, accusing them of supplying arms to an anti-Maoist village committee. A 13-year-old child was killed in a bomb blast by suspected Maoists in Bara district.
Keywords: Maoist, Nawalparasi, Bara, killing, bombing, children

Detail: Representatives of the seven political parties and Maoists announced an agreement to launch a fresh joint agitation against King Gyanendra beginning 6 April, including a four-day general strike, civil disobedience, and a large public rally in Kathmandu on 8 April.
Maoists withdrew the blockade of Kathmandu and district headquarters.
13 soldiers were reportedly killed during a Maoist ambush in Kavre district.

Nine police personnel and three Maoists were killed when insurgents attacked the Birtamod police post in Jhapa district, injuring at least 22 police personnel. 20 Maoists were killed in a security operation in Dhading district.
Keywords: police, Maoist, Jhapa, Dhading, killing, clash

Detail: Two APF personnel and three Maoists were killed in a clash in Morang district.

The Supreme Court upheld a provision allowing the government to detain persons for up to a year without prosecution under the Terrorists and Disruptive Activities Ordinance, and upheld the terrorist designation of CPN-Maoist leaders.
Two police personnel were killed when Maoists attacked a ward police office in Janakpur municipality, Dhanusha district.
Keywords: police, Maoist, Janakpur, Dhanusha, killing, clash

Detail: Suspected Maoists detonated a bomb at the residence of an assistant minister in Kathmandu.
Two Maoists and a civilian were killed when troops launched an aerial attack near a school in Sindhupalchowk district.

The RNA disclosed that over 8,029 Maoists had been killed in security actions since the Army's deployment against them in November 2001, including 5,086 after the breakdown of the ceasefire in August 2003 and 401 since the Maoist unilateral truce of 3 September 2005. 635 Army personnel were killed since the breakdown of peace talks in August 2003.
Keywords: Nepal Army, Maoist, killing, peace process

Detail: Two security force personnel and one Maoist were killed during clashes at the Sarlahi-Rautahat border. Suspected Maoists shot dead a former police officer in Ghorahi Bazaar, Dang district.
Keywords: police, Maoist, Dang, Rautahat, killing, clash

Detail: Two police personnel were killed and two persons injured when Maoist insurgents attacked a police post in Rautahat district.
Jana Andolan IIMass nationwide protests force the restoration of Parliament.
Maoists announced a unilateral ceasefire within the Kathmandu Valley with effect from the evening of 3 April.
Two Maoists were killed in an encounter in Dailekh district.
Five police personnel and four Maoists were killed in clashes at Malangwa, headquarters of Sarlahi district.
Six security force personnel were killed when a Maoist IED exploded in Jhapa district.

The second mass people's movement began. Over 400 pro-democracy protesters and journalists were arrested in Kathmandu on the first day of a four-day nationwide general strike called by the seven-party alliance, while dozens of others were injured.

At least four Maoists and two civilians were killed after Maoists attacked security bases in Butwal and Kapilavastu districts. Protests continued across the country on the second day of the general strike. The district post office in Lalitpur was set ablaze and students at Tribhuvan University briefly held staff hostage.
Keywords: Maoist, The, Lalitpur, killing, clash, protest

Detail: The government imposed a curfew in the Kathmandu Valley. Local administrations in Surkhet, Butwal, and Chitwan also issued curfew orders.

Three persons were killed and over 26 protesters injured when security forces opened fire at anti-King demonstrators across the country. The seven-party alliance announced continuation of the general strike.
Maoists announced a nationwide campaign including defying curfew orders, capturing highways, and breaking royal statues. A 12-hour curfew was imposed in Pokhara.

70 demonstrators were injured when security forces fired rubber bullets at protesters in Dhangadhi, Kailali district. 35 persons were injured in security force action at Gongabu and Kalanki in Kathmandu. Daytime curfews were clamped in Bharatpur, Pokhara, Butwal, and Banepa.
A six-year-old child was killed in a Maoist IED blast in Kailali district. Over 350 anti-King protesters were injured in police action in Kathmandu.
Keywords: police, Maoist, Kailali, Kathmandu, killing, bombing, children, protest

Detail: At least 30 persons were injured in police action in Syangja. In Dipayal, at least 50 persons, including two children, were hurt in baton charges. In Sarlahi, 10 protesters were wounded. In Gaighat, over 30 demonstrators were injured. In Jhapa, at least 28 demonstrators were hurt.

The Federation of Nepali Journalists (FNJ) stated that at least 111 journalists had been arrested in the week after the seven-party general strike / People’s Movement began, with over a hundred injured while reporting, and demanded release of all detained media workers. CPJ later reported FNJ tallies exceeding 200 journalist detentions during the April movement.
Keywords: FNJ, Federation of Nepali Journalists, press freedom, journalists arrested, Jana Andolan II, civil society, Kathmandu
Organizations: Federation of Nepali Journalists (FNJ); Committee to Protect Journalists (reporting)

Detail: A Maoist insurgent was killed during a search operation in Khotang district. King Gyanendra called upon all political parties to join a dialogue on the occasion of the Nepali New Year.
Leaders of the seven-party alliance rejected the King's offer for dialogue.

Maoist chairman Prachanda described the King's address as showing feudal stubbornness. Security force personnel arrested more than 100 demonstrators, including 53 women and 14 journalists, from a rally in Baglung district.

Maoists killed one APF personnel in Jhapa district. In Rupandehi district, 100 protesters were wounded when soldiers opened fire at approximately 25,000 agitators. At least six protesters were injured in police shooting at Balkhu in Kathmandu. King Gyanendra met US, Chinese, and Indian Ambassadors separately at the royal palace.
Keywords: APF, police, Maoist, Jhapa, In Rupandehi, Rupandehi, Kathmandu, killing, protest

Detail: Maoists shot dead a traffic police inspector in Rautahat district. One anti-King protester was killed and several others injured when security forces opened fire at demonstrators in Bara district. In Kathmandu, police action at Chabahil-Chuchepati left 62 injured. In Kalaiya, at least 24 agitators were injured. In Birgunj, over a dozen activists were injured. In Itahari, 24 demonstrators were injured. In Nepalgunj, 20 demonstrators were injured in police action.
Keywords: police, Maoist, Rautahat, Bara, Kathmandu, Birgunj, Nepalgunj, killing, protest

Detail: At least 36 agitators were injured when security forces opened fire in Pokhara.
Four anti-King protesters were killed and over a hundred injured when security forces opened fire at demonstrators in Jhapa district.

King Gyanendra, in a televised address, announced he would hand over executive power to the people and asked the seven-party alliance to name a new Prime Minister. The SPA rejected the offer as inadequate.
Maoist spokesperson Krishna Mahara stated his party would not accept anything less than a Constituent Assembly.

More than 200 pro-democracy activists defying curfew orders were wounded when security forces opened fire at different locations in Kathmandu. In Pokhara, nearly 100,000 people joined the SPA-led demonstration.

Five Maoists, a security force personnel, and a civilian were killed in Maoist attacks on security bases in Sindhupalchowk district. 20 anti-King protesters were injured in police action in Kathmandu. Over 100,000 people assembled at Gongabu Chowk in defiance of the curfew.
Keywords: police, Maoist, Sindhupalchowk, Kathmandu, killing, clash, protest

Detail: King Gyanendra, in a televised address, restored the House of Representatives dissolved on 22 May 2002, marking the end of the second mass movement. The seven-party alliance welcomed the proclamation and withdrew the indefinite general strike. The CPN-Maoist rejected the royal proclamation, stating the reinstatement of the House of Representatives was not in line with the 12-point pact.

The seven-party alliance chose Nepali Congress president Girija Prasad Koirala to head the all-party government. The Chief of Army Staff stated the RNA was positive about merging Maoist troops with the national army.
Organizations: Nepali Congress, Royal Nepal Army, Nepal Army

Detail: The CPN-Maoist announced a unilateral ceasefire for three months with immediate effect. One police officer was killed and another injured in clashes in Nuwakot district.
Keywords: CPN-Maoist, police, Maoist, Nuwakot, killing, clash, peace process

Detail: King Gyanendra appointed Girija Prasad Koirala as Prime Minister.
The reinstated House of Representatives registered a proposal to hold constituent assembly elections. 11 RNA soldiers were abducted by Maoists from Dhankuta district.
Keywords: Nepal Army, Maoist, Dhankuta, abduction, elections

Detail: Eight soldiers were killed and nine others injured in a landmine explosion within the RNA barracks at Tamghas, headquarters of Gulmi district.
The reinstated House of Representatives unanimously passed a proposal for constituent assembly elections.
Nine RNA soldiers abducted from Dhankuta district were released in the presence of a human rights activist.
The government announced a ceasefire reciprocating the Maoist truce, and invited the Maoists for talks.
The government revoked the February 2006 municipal elections and cancelled appointments made by the royal government to District Development Committees and regional and zonal administration posts.
Maoist chairman Prachanda confirmed his party would sit for talks with the government and forwarded a draft code of conduct for both sides.
The government formed a five-member judicial committee under former Supreme Court judge Krishna Jung Rayamajhi to investigate the royal regime's suppression of the April mass movement.
The cabinet annulled all appointments made by governments since 4 October 2002 and recalled Nepal's ambassadors to 12 countries.
A group of Maoists abducted five APF personnel from Nawalparasi district.
Maoists released the five APF personnel abducted from Nawalparasi district on 9 May.
Two senior Maoist leaders, Matrika Yadav and Suresh Ale Magar, were freed from Nakkhu prison pursuant to court orders.
Security forces arrested five former royal cabinet ministers, including former Home Minister Kamal Thapa, Foreign Minister Ramesh Nath Pandey, and three others.
The government suspended three security chiefs including Nepal Police Chief Shyam Bhakta Thapa and APF Chief Shahbir Thapa.
Maoists beat to death a former insurgent, Prem Bahadur Thokar, in Kathmandu.
Maoists made public their roadmap for dialogue with the seven-party alliance government.
Two persons, including a minor, were injured when a Maoist-left socket bomb exploded in Tanahun district.
The House of Representatives passed a proposal depriving the King of his role as Supreme Commander-in-Chief of the RNA and declared itself supreme, significantly reducing the monarchy's powers.
Parliament Curbs Royal PowersThe monarchy's political authority is substantially reduced, and the Army is placed under civilian control.
At least 12 private banks were asked by the Maoists to donate NR 2.5 million each.
Maoists killed the two sons of Nepali Congress Rautahat district leader Jogendra Sahani, whom they had abducted the previous day.
Keywords: Nepali Congress, Maoist, Congress Rautahat, Rautahat, abduction, killing

Detail: Maoist negotiating team led by Krishna Bahadur Mahara held discussions with seven-party alliance leaders. The cabinet formed a three-member team headed by Home Minister Krishna Prasad Sitaula to hold negotiations with the Maoists.

Representatives of the government and the Maoists met at Gokarna, Kathmandu, and held the first round of formal peace talks. A 25-point Ceasefire Code of Conduct was announced to pave the way for constituent assembly elections.

Maoist leader Baburam Bhattarai reiterated demands for dissolution of the House of Representatives, formation of an interim government, and replacement of the existing constitution with an interim constitution.
The House of Representatives constituted a 21-member high-level parliamentary monitoring committee to oversee the peace process and implementation of the code of conduct.

A group affiliated to a Maoist Retaliation Committee killed a three-year-old boy, said to be the son of a Maoist cadre, in Kapilvastu district. The killing of a toddler illustrated the cycle of retaliatory violence engulfing civilian communities in the post-ceasefire period.
An estimated 200,000 Maoist cadres, supporters, and members of the public attended a mass meeting organized by the Maoists at Tundikhel in Kathmandu.
The UN Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights in Nepal raised concern over a series of abductions and killings of civilians in the central region allegedly by the Maoists.
The government decided to withdraw all cases filed under the Terrorist and Disruptive Activities Ordinance as a concession to the Maoists.
The government freed 240 Maoists detained in jails across the country.

The government and Maoists held the second round of peace talks in Kathmandu. A 31-member Ceasefire and Code of Conduct National Monitoring Committee was constituted, headed by human rights activist Dr. Devendra Raj Pandey. A report titled 'A Decade of Disaster' by the Community Study and Welfare Centre, released in Kathmandu, documented 13,190 conflict deaths between 1996 and 2005, including 446 children and 173 teachers.
A student abducted by Maoists from Sindhupalchowk district on 9 June was found dead.

Summit-level talks between the ruling seven-party alliance and the Maoists concluded in Kathmandu with an eight-point agreement, including commitments to frame an interim constitution, form an interim government, announce the date for constituent assembly elections, dissolve the revived House of Representatives and Maoist people's governments, and request UN monitoring of both armed forces.
Maoist chairman Prachanda made his first public appearance in Kathmandu.

Maoists were reported to have collected over NR 20 million annually in tax on yarsagumba trade in Darchula district, illustrating the systematic nature of Maoist taxation of civilian economic activity.
Maoists abducted former mayor of Tansen municipality, Dhata Nanda Bhattarai, from his home in Tansen.

A group of around 15 persons lynched two Maoists, Bhagirathi Kurmi and Keshav Bhattarai, in Kapilavastu district, reflecting growing civilian anger and the danger of vigilante violence in the post-ceasefire environment.

The high-level judicial commission probing suppression of the 2006 people's movement summoned former RNA chief Satchit Shumsher Rana, former law minister Niranjan Thapa, and two former senior police officials to record statements, alleging they had played key roles in provoking the King against democracy and suppressing protesters.
Deputy Prime Minister K.P. Sharma Oli called on the Maoists to immediately stop arbitrary extortion from civilians, stating that Maoist people's courts and extortion had terrorized the public.

Maoist chief Prachanda directed all district committees to stop running people's courts in major cities and to accept only voluntary public donations, while acknowledging the Maoists needed funds for their militia pending the formation of an interim government.
The government wrote to the United Nations formally seeking the UN's role in facilitating arms management in Nepal.
Maoists subjected six civilians from Banke district to severe physical punishment, holding them in custody on charges of murder and robbery.

Senior Maoist leaders and political party representatives held talks in Kathmandu and agreed to convert the existing House of Representatives into an interim parliament by inducting additional members.
Maoists extended the ceasefire for a further three months.
A UN assessment mission led by Staffan de Mistura met Maoist leaders and government negotiators in Kathmandu, focusing on decommissioning of arms.
The Janatantrik Terai Mukti Morcha shot and wounded two Maoist cadres in Siraha district.
Maoist spokesperson Krishna Bahadur Mahara stated the Maoist army would stay in camps under UN monitoring until constituent assembly elections but their arms would not be decommissioned.
Maoists abducted a CPN-UML member from Kirtipur municipality on the charge of tearing a Maoist pamphlet.
A group of Maoists abducted Nepali Congress activist Dipo Yadav from Dhanusha district.
The government and Maoists reached a five-point agreement seeking UN assistance in the entire peace process and creating a free and fair atmosphere for constituent assembly elections.
Chief Maoist negotiator Krishna Bahadur Mahara stated that the People's Liberation Army would be confined to cantonment areas until constituent assembly elections but would not decommission its arms.
Maoist insurgents abducted two Indian citizens from Mahendranagar.
Maoists stalled all NGO activities in Salyan district.
Over a dozen people were injured when Maoists attacked a protest rally organized against them by former cadres and displaced persons in Kalaiya, Bara district.

The Interim Constitution Drafting Committee submitted the draft interim constitution to the peace negotiating teams of the government and Maoists. In Dailekh, a Maoist village government chief attacked and injured a CPN-UML cadre and school management committee chairman.
A pregnant woman from Saptari district died in Maoist custody, three days after being taken away by insurgents.
Maoists abducted three girls from Bardiya district.
Maoists released an RNA soldier abducted from Itahari the previous day.
Maoists abducted five civilians affiliated with the Rolpa Drinking Water Project.
A Maoist cadre was killed after a clash between locals and Maoists escalated in Bara district.
Maoists attacked and injured a Nepali Congress activist in Arghakhanchi district for not paying donations to the organization.
Keywords: Nepali Congress, Maoist, Arghakhanchi, clash, extortion/land

Detail: Civilians in Siraha district blocked the Mahendra Highway for over five hours protesting a Maoist assault on a local trader the previous day, reflecting growing civilian resistance to post-ceasefire Maoist violence.

The UN Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights in Nepal publicly released a document detailing major concerns about human rights abuses committed by CPN-Maoist cadres since the 26 April ceasefire declaration.
Scheduled summit talks between the seven-party alliance and Maoists were deferred.
A civilian died in Maoist custody due to torture in Parsa district.
Three children were killed and five persons wounded when a bomb exploded in Kailali district.
At least one Maoist insurgent was killed in a clash between Maoists and the splinter Janatantrik Terai Mukti Morcha in Saptari district.
A civilian held in Maoist custody died mysteriously in Jhapa district.

Maoists disclosed that around 50,000 hectares of land were under their control across Nepal and stated seized land would not be returned to its lawful owners before a political settlement was reached.
Maoists extended the ongoing ceasefire by a further three months.

Commitments on Truth, Justice and DisappearancesThe CPA commits the state to investigate disappearances, establish truth-seeking mechanisms, provide relief to victims, and address conflict-era human rights violations.

After over 14 hours of negotiations, the seven-party alliance government and the Maoists reached a six-point agreement to end the decade-long conflict and restore lasting peace, agreeing to sign a peace accord by 16 November and confine all Maoist insurgents to seven cantonment areas by 21 November.
Maoists forced school children in Itahari, eastern Nepal, to participate in a victory rally celebrating the peace talks.
A bomb suspected to have been left by Maoists killed three children in Tehrathum district.
Maoists abducted four persons, including a bank manager, from Sunsari district.
Insurgents seized 11 kattahs of land from a poor farmer in Sarlahi at gunpoint and registered it in the name of a Maoist cadre, forcing the victim to thumbprint the transfer documents.

The high-level commission probing the suppression of the April 2006 people's movement found King Gyanendra and around 170 others, including ministers, security officials, and regional administrators, guilty of oppressing the movement — the first time in Nepal's history that a commission had found a King guilty.
The National Human Rights Commission's Biratnagar regional office found Maoists recruiting youths in Udaypur district for the People's Liberation Army.
Organizations: National Human Rights Commission of Nepal, PLA

Detail: Maoists kidnapped more than a dozen school children from Morang district.
Maoists forcibly recruited hotel, restaurant, furniture, and transport workers in Pokhara, promising them permanent jobs and salaries.
Maoists threatened journalists Ambar Khadka and Suman Puri with action if they reported on the Maoists' forced recruitment drive, directly targeting press freedom.

Maoists abducted more than 100 children and youths from Sunsari district for recruitment into the People's Liberation Army. Child clubs in Sunsari staged a protest before the Maoists' district contact office demanding a halt to child conscription. The US embassy in Kathmandu denounced the recruitment of children into Maoist armed ranks. The High Level Probe Commission submitted its 1,184-page report to Prime Minister Koirala, indicting 202 high-ranking officials of the royal government, though stopping short of recommending action against King Gyanendra himself.
Keywords: Maoist, Sunsari, Kathmandu, abduction, children, protest

Detail: Two commissioners refused to sign the report.

Prime Minister Koirala and Maoist chairman Prachanda signed the Comprehensive Peace Accord (CPA), formally ending the decade-long armed conflict in Nepal. The ten-point CPA included provisions on human rights, civil and political rights, arms and army management, and socio-economic transformation. The CPA committed both parties to investigate serious human rights violations and crimes against humanity committed during the conflict.
Comprehensive Peace Agreement (CPA)The Government of Nepal and Maoists formally end the decade-long armed conflict.

A Maoist resistance group in Nawalparasi publicly burned a dozen weapons — eight guns, one khukuri, one spear, and one sickle — in the presence of human rights commission representatives, political party members, journalists, and others, following the peace agreement.

Maoist leader Baburam Bhattarai accused the government of delaying the promulgation of the interim constitution and formation of the interim parliament and cabinet. Thousands of students from 22 schools in Sunsari district were barred from appearing in their second-term examinations when the Maoist student wing ANNISU-R padlocked an examination centre.
Maoists tortured three civilians in Sunsari district, including breaking the leg of a rickshaw-puller and abducting and torturing a student, Arjun Giri, before releasing him.

The government and Maoists signed the Agreement on Monitoring of the Management of Arms and Armies, under which the People's Liberation Army would be confined to cantonment areas under UN monitoring pending constituent assembly elections.
Senior Maoist leaders Chandra Prakash Gajurel and Mohan Baidhya were released from custody in West Bengal, India, after a court in Jalpaiguri ordered their release.
The UN Security Council unanimously adopted a proposal to assist Nepal's peace process in response to the government's request.
UNMIN Begins OperationsThe United Nations Mission in Nepal begins monitoring arms management and supporting the peace process.

The Maoist Victims Association staged a rally in Kathmandu demanding representation in the soon-to-be-formed interim parliament and fulfillment of their 10-point demands including rehabilitation, compensation, and accountability for perpetrators.

Maoist cadres kept a team of political leaders and human rights activists in confinement for four hours in Dang district, violating commitments to allow political parties to freely organize in villages.
Maoists were reported to be engaged in extortion across the country, violating the Ceasefire Code of Conduct.
Insurgents demanded 30 percent of community forest income in Gulmi district as tax.
Maoists announced the revival of their people's government in Sankhuwasabha district.

The National Human Rights Commission reported that 11 persons had been killed by security forces and 15 by Maoist insurgents since the 26 April ceasefire, with resistance groups killing five more and five others dying in accidental explosions — documenting the continuing loss of life even after the formal peace declaration.
Organizations: National Human Rights Commission of Nepal

Detail: Leaders of the seven-party alliance and Maoists signed the interim constitution.
Maoists took six teenagers from Siraha district to recruit them into the People's Liberation Army, offering NR 3,600 monthly salary and rations.
Six Maoists and two security force personnel were injured when Maoists clashed with police near a security base camp in Mahottari district.
