Maoists called a strike and staged demonstrations against the government's decision to nominate ambassadors and NHRC members. Thousands of PLA members carrying arms left their camps to join the demonstrations.
Organizations: National Human Rights Commission of Nepal, PLA

Detail: A group of 50 Maoists seized belongings of police officials at a newly restored police post in Banke district and looted food grains and cash.

Over 1,000 Maoists barged into the Rampur Agriculture Campus in Chitwan and thrashed Nepal Students' Union activists, injuring 49. Over two dozen people, including policemen and civilians, were injured when Maoist PLA combatants attacked an all-party meeting in Udaypur district.
Maoists forced district authorities in Phidim, Panchthar district, to remove re-established rural police posts.
Ten persons including Maoists, police, and locals were injured in Banke district when Maoists attempted to remove a re-established police post.
Five police personnel were injured in a Maoist attack on unarmed police at a recently re-established area police office in Nawalparasi district.
Maoists padlocked municipality offices of Damak, Bhadrapur, and Mechinagar, and VDC offices of Korobari and Juropani in Jhapa district.
Maoists padlocked the VDC offices of Dharampur and Topgachhi in Jhapa district.

Maina Sunuwar's mother, Devi Sunuwar, filed a case at the Supreme Court seeking justice for the abduction, rape, and killing of her 15-year-old daughter by Royal Nepal Army personnel in February 2004.
Keywords: Nepal Army, Supreme Court, abduction, killing
Organizations: Royal Nepal Army, Nepal Army, Supreme Court of Nepal

Detail: The Conflict Victims Committee in Bardiya was formally registered as an official organization. Established during the civil war to organize victims of both Maoist and state violence — particularly families of the disappeared — the CVC helped victims submit petitions to the government and NHRC, met with international human rights organizations, and organized rallies for justice.
Organizations: National Human Rights Commission of Nepal

Detail: Interim Relief Program IntroducedThe Government begins formulating Interim Relief Guidelines to provide interim relief (mostly economic compensation) to families of those killed, disappeared, displaced, and otherwise affected by the conflict. The torture and conflict related sexual violence were not included.
Keywords: killing, transitional justice, CRSV exclusion, torture survivors, Interim Relief Programme

Detail: The US Ambassador to Nepal, James F. Moriarty, stated the US government would not remove the terrorist designation from the Maoists as they had not yet proved they had given up violence.
Maoists were reported to be extracting taxes from construction materials supply, rural roads, and other internal resources of Kaski District Development Committee.
Around 11 UN arms monitors arrived in Nepal to begin monitoring the management of arms and armies from 7 January.

A meeting of the Maoists' Ilam District Committee decided to give VDC secretaries limited assignments such as distributing citizenship certificates and updating voters' lists, reflecting continued Maoist control over civilian administration.

Top leaders of the seven-party alliance and the CPN-Maoist agreed to promulgate the interim constitution and form the interim legislature on 15 January, formally opening the doors for Maoists to join the political mainstream.

Six women cadres of the People's Liberation Army reportedly fled from the Chulachuli-based headquarters in Ilam district due to harsh camp conditions, irregular salary payments, and poor camp management.
Maoists turned back police personnel from different villages in Rukum and Humla districts and obstructed police from reaching posts in Jajarkot district.
Maoists continued collecting NR 100 taxes from tourists visiting the Annapurna region.
Maoists threw away police preparatory goods at Bhotechaur VDC in Dang district and Chautara in Sindhupalchowk district and pressured police personnel to leave.
Two reinstated police posts in Bardiya district were displaced after Maoist attacks. The Home Minister stated Maoist arms would be locked in containers by 29 January.
Maoists assaulted and abducted two persons, Devendra Mishra and his son Manish, in Kapilvastu district.
Maoists padlocked the house of a schoolteacher in Bhojpur district after he refused to pay an amount equivalent to 12 days' salary.
Maoists padlocked the office of the Khandbari micro-hydropower project in Sankhuwasabha district after the campuses running it refused to pay 25 percent of the project's profits to the Maoists.

The Interim Constitution of Nepal 2063 came into effect, establishing Nepal as a federal democratic republic and setting the terms for the election of a Constituent Assembly. All 83 Maoist representatives, along with other Members of Parliament, were sworn in, marking Maoist entry into the mainstream legislature. The Interim Constitution replaced the Constitution of 1990.

Interim Constitution PromulgatedThe Interim Constitution commits the state to establish a Truth and Reconciliation Commission and requires the status of disappeared persons to be made public within 60 days.
Maoists stopped police teams in Parbat district who were heading to inner villages to provide security to government teams distributing citizenship certificates.

A day after promulgation of the Interim Constitution, Madhesi Janaadhikar Forum (MJF) activists led by Upendra Yadav burned copies of the Interim Constitution at Maitighar Mandala, Kathmandu, protesting the omission of federalism and proportional representation for Madhesis and other marginalised communities — widely cited as the immediate spark of the first Madhes movement.
Keywords: Madhes movement, MJF, Interim Constitution, Maitighar, federalism, proportional representation, Upendra Yadav, Kathmandu

Detail: The CPN-Maoist elected Krishna Bahadur Mahara as party leader in the interim legislature.
Maoists decided to dissolve all of their people's governments, people's courts, and communes across the country.

Ramesh Kumar Mahato (often reported as ~16–17), an MJF protester, was killed in Lahan, Siraha District, during Madhes movement protests (accounts attribute the shooting to Maoist cadres/escorts of a Maoist leader). His death is widely commemorated as the first martyrdom of the Madhes movement and intensified the uprising across the Tarai.
Keywords: Maoist, Siraha, killing, clash, Ramesh Mahato, Lahan, Madhes martyr, Madhes Sacrifice Day

Detail: Around 500 Maoists stormed the area police post at Patbhar in Bardiya district, injuring three police personnel and chasing them away.
Maoist-affiliated hotel and restaurant workers padlocked nine hotels and resorts in Dhulikhel, Kavre district.
Despite Prachanda's directive to dissolve people's courts, a Maoist kangaroo court in Kailali district fined a local person NR 115,000.

The UN verification team temporarily halted registration of Maoist combatants in Chitwan district after refusing to register apparent underage recruits who appeared to be between 12 and 15 years old. The team was pressured to register them as 18-year-olds.
A group of Maoists abducted three locals — Purna Bahadur Oli, Mok Bahadur Oli, and Durga Bahadur Oli — from their residences in Banke district.
The UN arms monitoring team completed registration of all Maoist arms and troops at the cantonment site at Shaktikhor in Chitwan district and handed the keys of arms containers to the Maoists.
Maoist leader Prachanda called for the immediate abolition of the monarchy, accusing King Gyanendra of trying to undermine the peace deal.

Maoists seized voters' lists and other documents from VDC offices in Dolakha and Dhading districts, forcing officials to enlist their cadres' names regardless of actual residency. The Kathmandu-based Industrial Security Group, comprising embassies of France, Germany, India, the UK, the US, and the European Commission, urged Maoists to cease violence, abductions, and extortion.
Keywords: Maoist, Dolakha, Kathmandu, abduction, extortion/land, elections

Detail: Maoist insurgents attacked Rashtriya Prajatantra Party leaders at Besisahar in Lamjung district, injuring 20 RPP workers including the district president.
Maoists abducted school students in Dhading to participate in a central-level Maoist meeting in Kathmandu.
ANNISU-R students vandalized a statue of the late King Mahendra in Kanchanpur district.

Maoists interfered in citizenship certificate distribution in Rupandehi district, pressuring staff to prioritize their party cadres. The Finance Minister revealed that the government had released NR 350 million to the Maoists for PLA upkeep without receiving any accounting of expenses.
Maoists were reported to be collecting NR 1,000 from truck and bus drivers and NR 500 from taxi drivers at various points in Panchthar district.
Maoists abducted family members of a civilian in Kathmandu.
Three persons, including two Maoists, were injured in a clash over citizenship certificate distribution in Sunsari district.
Maoists seized a house belonging to a member of the royal family in Nepalgunj, Banke district.
Maoists declared plans to collect NR 3 million from civilians in Nawalparasi district within five days.

A UN report documented the recruitment of 155 children across all five regions of Nepal by Maoists after the ceasefire of April 2006. 40 percent of recruits were girls; most were enrolled in schools at the time of their recruitment.
At least 15 persons were injured in a clash between Maoists and MJF activists in Rupandehi district.
Ten persons — six Maoist cadres and four civilians — were injured in a clash between Maoists and civilians in Kanchanpur district.
An MJF activist, Jille Ram Yadav, who was injured in a clash with Maoists in Bardiya district, died of his injuries.
Maoists entered Gaighat Bazaar, headquarters of Udaypur district, armed with AK-47 rifles and other sophisticated weapons.
Maoists assaulted Nepali Congress leaders and activists in Lamjung district.
Four civilians were injured when three Maoists opened fire inside a civilian residence in Saptari district.

An armed group of Maoists abducted five local residents from Jhapa district. A US State Department report indicated that Maoists had directed farmers in certain areas to increase cannabis production and were levying a tax on cannabis output, linking the insurgent organization to narcotics cultivation.

Maoist chairman Prachanda expressed commitment to returning public property seized during the conflict. The Nepali Congress called on the government not to include Maoists in an interim government unless they fully implemented all agreements, gave up violence, extortion, and abductions, and returned seized property.
Keywords: Nepali Congress, Maoist, Prachanda, abduction, extortion/land

Detail: A Maoist area in-charge detonated a hand bomb in Dailekh district in alleged retaliation against local youths.
JTMM-Jwala Singh cadres and Maoists clashed inside a bus in Sunsari district; the bus was torched by JTMM cadres.
A Maoist cadre was killed in a clash between MJF activists and Maoists in Sunsari district.

Prachanda disclosed at a mass gathering in Baglung that thousands of PLA combatants and weapons remained outside the cantonments as they could not meet UN standards, and that they still had armed technical capacity to launch simultaneous attacks at multiple locations on a single night.
Maoist cadres seized 13 Army trucks for two and a half hours in Nawalparasi district, suspecting they were carrying weapons in violation of the ceasefire code.

60-Day Commitment to Reveal Disappearances Not FulfilledDespite the Interim Constitution's commitment to make public the status of disappeared persons within 60 days, thousands of families continue to await answers regarding the fate of their relatives.
Young Communist League cadres abducted a civilian in Kavre district.

Maoists abducted and assaulted Hotel Woodland operator Hari Shrestha in Kathmandu after he refused to pay NR 2 million as demanded. He was released after signing an agreement to pay NR 10 million and provide 10 free rooms to the Maoists.
Five Maoists, including a lawmaker and a platoon commander, were arrested by the Nepal Army for entering Bardiya National Park with illegal arms.
YCL cadres captured 25 ropanis of land and four houses belonging to former Army Chief Sachchit Shumsher Rana in Gorkha district and hoisted their party flag.

At least 28 persons, including five women, were killed and over 40 injured at Gaur in Rautahat district when Maoists and MJF activists clashed — one of the deadliest post-ceasefire incidents of political violence.
Keywords: MJF, Maoist, Rautahat, killing, clash, peace process

Detail: Thousands of PLA soldiers left camps across multiple districts in protest against the killing of their cadres by MJF. Prachanda demanded the government outlaw the MJF.
Suspected Maoists killed Madhav Prasad Verma, a former VDC chairman in Banke district, and looted property worth around NR 200,000 from his home.
Three persons were injured in a Maoist-MJF clash in Rupandehi district.
An eight-party agreement was reached on sharing ministerial portfolios in the Interim Government, with the Maoists securing five ministries.
Maina Sunuwar Exhumation
Ministry of Peace and Reconstruction Established

An Interim Government including the Maoists was formed under Prime Minister Girija Prasad Koirala, with five CPN-Maoist ministers sworn in. Leaders agreed to hold Constituent Assembly polls on 20 June.
A Maoist area committee member was shot dead in Rautahat district by unidentified assailants.
One Maoist was killed in a clash between Maoists and members of other political parties in Kalikot district.
One Maoist and one MJF member were injured in a clash in Sunsari district.
The Maoist-affiliated trade union padlocked the offices of The Himalayan Times and Annapurna Post in Kathmandu in an industrial dispute, directly suppressing press operations.
Maoists captured the Kavre VDC office in Kavrepalanchowk district and set up a party office there.
The CPN-Maoist was registered as a political party at the Election Commission.
YCL and pro-Maoist union cadres in Biratnagar assaulted a leading businessman.
Maoists grabbed four bighas of land belonging to three locals in Sunsari district.
The Election Commission stated it was not possible to hold Constituent Assembly elections by 20 June.
At least 50 persons were injured when Maoists and locals clashed in Ramechhap district following a Maoist assault on a youth.
The UN Mission in Nepal completed the registration and storage of Nepal Army weapons at Chhauni Barracks in Kathmandu.

Maoists threatened to kill civilian Mukti Bahadur Swar in Bardiya district. Large numbers of PLA cadres came out of cantonment sites in several districts to protest the Election Commission's announcement that the 20 June deadline could not be met.
Keywords: PLA, Maoist, Bardiya, killing, demobilisation, elections, protest

Detail: The government and Maoists agreed to reduce the number of PLA combatants in cantonments from 30,000 to 17,000 and reduce the number of PLA camps to seven.
Police arrested seven YCL cadres in Kathmandu after they broke into a woman's residence and attempted to rob her valuables.
Prime Minister Koirala expressed commitment to returning property seized during the decade-long Maoist insurgency.
Senior Maoist leader Baburam Bhattarai threatened a third wave of indefinite agitation if a republic was not announced by the third week of May.

The Maoist-led Ministry of Information and Communications directed state-owned newspapers to give prominence to pro-Maoist news and suppress critical coverage — a direct attack on press freedom from within government.

The UN Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights in Nepal stated that Maoist insurgents were not complying with commitments to allow internally displaced persons to return safely and retrieve seized property.
Around 500 Maoists attacked a police post in Banke district, detaining a sub-inspector for 14 hours and assaulting police constables.
Three APF personnel were injured in a clash between YCL activists and APF personnel in Bardiya district.
Maoists assaulted two civilians in Kailali district.
UN Mission chief Ian Martin revealed that the second-phase PLA registration was delayed due to Maoist conditions on cantonment improvements, remuneration, and the future of the Maoist army.
The Ministry of Peace and Reconstruction formed a working group to draft a bill to establish a Truth Commission.
YCL cadres vandalized the house of Radio Nepal correspondent Yuvaraj Adhikari.
Maoists captured six ropanis of private land in Kavrepalanchowk district and destroyed crops.

Maoists padlocked Siraha municipality office. Senior Maoist leader Mohan Baidhya stated that properties seized during the conflict could not be returned, and the number of combatants would not be reduced.
Reports indicated that tree felling in Bardiya district had intensified since Maoists took over the Forest Ministry in the interim government.

YCL cadres clashed with police in Morang district, injuring many locals. In Phidim district, around 15 YCL cadres assaulted two men going abroad for employment and robbed them of NR 70,000 cash and two tolas of gold.
Keywords: YCL, police, Morang, In Phidim, clash

Detail: A Maoist-affiliated Tharu group shut down five western districts protesting against the Bardiya-Sanoshree incident.
Maoists set ablaze the offices of the Nepal Electricity Authority and Land Revenue at Gulariya in Bardiya district.
Nine people, including two political leaders, activists, and businessmen, were displaced from Bardiya district due to YCL threats.
Police filed criminal charges against 38 YCL cadres for burning the government offices at Gulariya.
YCL activists assaulted the Assistant Chief District Officer of Kailali and padlocked several district government offices.
YCL cadres killed an elderly man, Bir Bahadur Kalakheti, in Sankhuwasabha district.
At least 50 persons — 40 Maoists and 10 police — were injured in clashes in Dang district.

YCL cadres ransacked the Small Farmers' Cooperatives office in Bardiya district and looted all documents. Bajura district Maoists announced they would recapture land and properties previously returned to owners.
Maoists obstructed the district administration and land revenue office in Sankhuwasabha district.
At least 20 Maoists and eight police personnel were injured in clashes in Nepalgunj, Banke district.
Maoist chairman Prachanda announced the Central Committee had decided to return all seized lands to facilitate the peace and political process.
Two JTMM-Goit faction cadres were killed by the Jwala Singh faction in Rautahat district.

Maoist-affiliated All Nepal Women's Association-Revolutionary activists vandalized the Kanchanpur District Administration Office, injuring 18 activists when police intervened and reportedly misbehaving with the Chief District Officer.
ANNISU-R activists vandalized statues of late King Mahendra at Kalimati Chowk in Kathmandu, and statues of late Kings Birendra and Mahendra in Pokhara, Nepalgunj, and Surkhet.
YCL cadres abducted eight persons from Rupandehi district.
Maoists abducted three youths from Chitwan district.
YCL cadres assaulted a doctor at the Primary Health Centre in Saptari district for arriving late to work.
Eight persons were injured in a Maoist-police clash in Kanchanpur district.
Maoists seized weapons from police in Sindhupalchowk district.
Maoists vandalized a statue of King Prithvi Narayan Shah in Gorkha district.
YCL cadres severely assaulted a civilian in Parbat district, breaking his hands and legs.
YCL cadres smeared the face of a civilian and padlocked his house in Bardiya district.
YCL cadres assaulted a former police officer in Kathmandu.
Maoists captured 58 bighas of land belonging to four Nepali Congress-Democratic leaders in Kailali district.
Maoist insurgents abducted the principal of Janasewa Secondary School in Siraha district.
Maoists in Banke district announced they would not obey central or district leadership directives on returning seized property.
YCL cadres hurled stones at the vehicle of US Ambassador James F. Moriarty in Jhapa district.
At least 15 persons were injured when Maoists and Nepali Congress (Democratic) workers clashed in Humla district.
Maoists forced a reinstated police post in Baitadi district to close, driving out 13 police officers.
20 people were injured in a clash between YCL cadres and students in Bhairahawa district.
Maoists injured six Dalit civilians, including some women, in Siraha district following a dispute with locals, demonstrating the gendered and caste-based dimensions of Maoist violence.
Maoists assaulted journalist Shambhu Singh Karki, a Broadcasting Association of Nepal central member, in retaliation for news coverage he had aired.
Nine persons, including a child, were killed when three bombs exploded simultaneously in a house in Palpa district, believed to have been left behind by Maoists.
A bomb also exploded at the CPN-Maoist party office in Kathmandu.
Around 400 Maoists, mostly YCL cadres, seized over 60 bighas of land in Bardiya district. 14 persons were injured when they clashed with local youth club members who resisted the seizure.
An eight-party meeting decided to hold Constituent Assembly elections by the third week of November 2007.

In response to over 80 habeas corpus petitions submitted by relatives of the disappeared, the Supreme Court ordered the government to immediately investigate all allegations of enforced disappearances through a commission of inquiry, pass a law criminalizing enforced disappearances, punish those responsible, and provide reparations to families of the disappeared — a landmark ruling for victims of conflict-era enforced disappearances.
YCL cadres attacked a vehicle carrying Nepali Congress leaders in Nuwakot district.
Three YCL cadres abducted a businessman from his office in Kathmandu.
Maoists assaulted villagers in Rolpa district. The Madhesi National Liberation Front announced a month-long agitation demanding an autonomous Madhes region.
JTMM-Goit faction cadres shot dead a Maoist area committee member in Bara district.

JTMM-Jwala Singh faction cadres abducted and shot dead a YCL district coordinator in Rautahat district. The same faction captured land belonging to former Chief Justice Keshav Prasad Upadhyaya in Siraha district.
Keywords: YCL, JTMM-Jwala, Rautahat, Siraha, abduction, killing, extortion/land

Detail: Unidentified assailants killed a Nepali Congress member in Mahottari district.
JTMM-Jwala Singh cadres abducted an Agriculture Development Bank employee in Siraha district.
Around 150 YCL cadres took over a civilian's house and burned important documents in Sunsari district.
YCL activists seized land in Gorkha district, claiming it had been illegally acquired under the royal regime.
YCL activists set ablaze seven vehicles in Kapilvastu district for defying their call for a general strike.
A central Maoist leader was abducted and killed by JTMM-Goit cadres in Saptari district.
MJF activists abducted and killed two central YCL members in Rupandehi district.
Four people were injured in clashes between Maoists and Nepali Congress-Democratic cadres in Ramechhap district.
JTMM-Jwala Singh cadres shot dead a Maoist-affiliated Madheshi Liberation Front district vice-chairman in Bara district.
Keywords: JTMM-Jwala, Maoist, Liberation Front, Bara, killing

Detail: A group of JTMM-Jwala Singh cadres set ablaze the home of a former Maoist people's government chief in Bara district.
The body of Nepali Congress-Democratic Humla district member Netra Bahadur Shahi, abducted by Maoists on 10 March, was found at a riverbank, confirming his killing during captivity.
Keywords: Nepali Congress, Maoist, Democratic Humla, abduction, killing

Detail: Police raided the YCL office in Nepalgunj and rescued the Regional Health Director, Dr. Piyush Bahadur Rajendra, who had been abducted by the YCL.
Maoists torched four cargo vehicles in Saptari district for defying a three-day strike. A Council of Ministers meeting fixed 22 November as the date for Constituent Assembly elections.
JTMM-Jwala Singh cadres abducted and shot dead the Maoist area secretary in Rautahat district.
The first draft of the Truth and Reconciliation Commission Bill was circulated and faced immediate backlash over amnesty provisions, including from Amnesty International and OHCHR-Nepal.
Organizations: Amnesty International, OHCHR-Nepal, Truth and Reconciliation Commission

Detail: Nepal Peace Trust Fund EstablishedThe NPTF is created as the government's principal mechanism for financing peace process implementation, rehabilitation, reconstruction, and peacebuilding activities.
JTMM-Jwala Singh cadres abducted a lawyer in Sunsari district.
JTMM-J cadres shot dead a government employee in Dhanusha district.
MJF padlocked the District Development Committee office in Mahottari district indefinitely.
Nine persons were injured after YCL cadres attacked a monarchist rally in Kathmandu, obstructing supporters of King Gyanendra from reaching the royal palace.
YCL cadres vandalized the offices of two political parties in Dhankuta district.
Maoists forced out police from a recently established police post in Kaski district.
Maoists assaulted a VDC secretary in Ramechhap district for not paying a demanded NR 50,000 donation.
YCL cadres subjected a civilian to severe assault during interrogation in Kanchanpur district.
Around 15 YCL cadres assaulted three locals in Nawalparasi district without provocation.

Maoist-affiliated groups captured 1,100 ropanis of land belonging to former Prime Minister Surya Bahadur Thapa in Dhankuta district, citing his attendance at the King's birthday celebration. The second phase PLA verification came to an indefinite halt as Maoists refused to continue without a government commitment on integrating registered combatants into national security forces.
JTMM-Jwala Singh cadres abducted and killed two members of a family in Saptari district.

A Maoist insurgent was killed by JTMM-Goit cadres in Siraha district. Over 12 persons were injured when YCL cadres who had arrived to settle a local dispute turned on both parties and assaulted them in Sindhupalchowk district.
Keywords: YCL, JTMM-Goit, Maoist, Siraha, Sindhupalchowk, killing

Detail: YCL cadres vandalized an RPP office in Baitadi district.
JTMM-J rejected the government's ultimatum to come to the negotiating table within 15 days.
JTMM-J cadres killed the VDC secretary of Govindapur in Siraha district, who had been abducted on 15 July.
JTMM-Goit cadres shot dead a local Maoist leader in Dhanusha district.
Seven Maoist combatants fled from a PLA camp in Morang district with their weapons.
JTMM-J cadres abducted and shot dead a civilian in Bara district.

30 persons, including six police personnel, were injured in a clash between Maoists and police in Dolakha district, where Maoists vandalized the District Administration Office and assaulted the Chief District Officer.
JTMM-Goit cadres abducted and shot dead a person in Bara district. Madhesi Liberation Tigers abducted a civilian in Saptari district and shot him dead.
The Supreme Court issued a decision directing the government to provide compensation to 83 families of people who were subjected to state-enforced disappearance.
Maoists assaulted police in Humla district, protesting the arrest of a Maoist cadre for killing a Nepali Congress-Democratic activist.
Keywords: Nepali Congress, police, Maoist, Humla, killing, protest

Detail: An inquiry report blaming King Gyanendra for the violent crackdown on the 2006 pro-democracy protests was presented to Parliament. The report found the royal cabinet had misused power and authority and was responsible for loss of life, property, and human rights violations during the crackdown.
JTMM-J cadres abducted a civilian in Sunsari district.
JTMM-J cadres killed a local businessman in Saptari district, two days after abducting him.
JTMM-J cadres opened fire on two persons in Bara district; one person died of his injuries in hospital.

YCL and CPN-Maoist cadres assaulted a Nepali Congress-Democratic leader in Kavre district. The Maoists' fifth plenum endorsed Prachanda's political report, making proportional representation and declaration of a republic preconditions for Constituent Assembly elections.
Keywords: YCL, CPN-Maoist, Nepali Congress, Maoist, Prachanda, Kavre, elections

Detail: The Government of Nepal talks team concluded an agreement with the Nepal Federation of Indigenous Nationalities (NEFIN) and the Indigenous Nationalities Joint Struggle Committee, including commitments on indigenous representation, formation of a State Restructuring Commission considering ethnicity/language/region, and related inclusion measures amid post-conflict state restructuring demands.
Keywords: NEFIN, Adivasi Janajati, indigenous nationalities, State Restructuring Commission, agreement, inclusion, federalism
Organizations: Government of Nepal; Nepal Federation of Indigenous Nationalities (NEFIN); Indigenous Nationalities Joint Struggle Committee

Detail: A group of 23 Maoists attacked three police officers at a post in Nuwakot district and looted all their weapons.
Around 25 journalists were assaulted by Maoists at Gorkhapatra Corporation in Kathmandu as they picketed demanding the reinstatement of 49 dismissed colleagues.

Maoist trade union workers disrupted distribution of The Himalayan Times and Annapurna Post and obstructed their printing in retaliation for front-page coverage of a court summons against their leaders.
The Joint Monitoring Coordination Committee agreed to resume the second stage of PLA verification from 14 August.
Around 12 YCL cadres attempted to abduct a journalist in Kathmandu and threatened to kill him.
Two JTMM-J cadres were killed in a clash with villagers in Parsa district.
Maoists barred Nepal Electricity Authority clients from paying electricity bills in Sindhupalchowk district.
JTMM-Jwala Singh warned his group would foil Constituent Assembly elections and prevent Terai residents from voting, threatening armed struggle against the polls.
Suspected JTMM-J cadres abducted and shot dead a Nepali Congress activist in Birgunj district.
Keywords: JTMM-J, Nepali Congress, Birgunj, abduction, killing

Detail: Maoist chairman Prachanda proposed postponing the Constituent Assembly election to mid-April 2008, citing an atmosphere of pressure.
Baburam Bhattarai warned the party could walk out of the government if constituent assembly elections could not be held without first declaring a republic.

YCL cadres seized three rifles and 115 rounds of ammunition from police on the East-West Highway in Siraha district, vandalized a police vehicle, injured four police personnel, and obstructed vehicular movement demanding release of arrested comrades.
The JTMM-J Bara district commander was shot dead by police in an encounter. A large cache of arms and explosives was recovered.
Around 300 Maoists disrupted a CPN-UML election awareness campaign in Kalikot district.

The Government of Nepal and the Madhesi People’s Rights Forum (MJF) signed an agreement addressing Madhesi and other marginalised groups’ demands — including inclusion, federal restructuring language, and related commitments — as part of ending the first Madhes movement’s phase of agitation, while MJF continued to press republican and electoral-system agendas ahead of CA elections.
Keywords: MJF, Madhes, 22-point agreement, federalism, inclusion, Government of Nepal, Upendra Yadav
Organizations: Government of Nepal; Madhesi People’s Rights Forum

Detail: Six Maoists and two villagers were injured in clashes in Parbat district after Maoists abducted and assaulted a Nepali Congress supporter.
Keywords: Nepali Congress, Maoist, Parbat, abduction, clash

Detail: YCL cadres barred APF personnel from visiting Kalikot district to inspect a proposed polling centre.
Two persons were killed and 25 others injured in serial bomb blasts in three busy market areas in Kathmandu. Terai-based groups claimed responsibility.
JTMM-Goit cadres shot dead a youth in Rautahat district. A schoolgirl, Sandhya Khadka, who was injured in the 2 September Kathmandu blasts, died of her injuries on 4 September.
Maoists intervened in a press conference in Parbat district, assaulting a journalist and a civil servant, and vandalizing the local Chamber of Commerce and Industry office.
A crude bomb exploded in Birgunj district, claimed by the JTMM-Jwala Singh faction.
Two bombs were recovered and defused from a school in the same area.

Maoists declared they would resume confiscating land from landlords for distribution to the landless, violating their earlier agreement to return seized properties. A Madheshi Mukti Tigers strike caused complete disruption of normal life in Siraha, Bara, Sarlahi, and Udaypur districts.
CPN-Maoist chairman Prachanda directed party cadres to be ready for another revolution if the government did not lay the foundation for constituent assembly polls.
JTMM-J cadres abducted and killed a school headmaster in Siraha district. Madhesi Mukti Tigers shot dead a civilian in Saptari district.
JTMM-J cadres shot dead a brick kiln employee in Dhanusha district.
MJF chairman Mohit Khan was shot dead by unidentified extremists in Kapilavastu district, triggering mob violence in which four persons were killed across the district.

Three civilians were killed in mob violence in Kapilavastu and Rupandehi districts following the killing of Mohit Khan. One civilian was killed and another injured when JTMM-J cadres hurled a hand grenade at a passenger bus in Bara district.
JTMM-J cadres abducted a VDC secretary in Siraha district for failure to pay taxes.
Three civilians were killed in fresh mob violence in Kapilvastu district.
The government appointed a three-member commission to investigate the violence.
Police arrested several JTMM-J cadres with weapons in Saptari district.

Child Workers in Nepal Concerned Centre reported at least 20 children from Kapilvastu district remained missing and at least 100 had been displaced following the September violence. The CPN-Maoist and the CPN-Marxist-Leninist-Maoist united to form the second largest party in the interim parliament.
Maoists assaulted and injured 30 CPN-UML cadres campaigning for Constituent Assembly elections in Dhading district.
Seven CPN-UML cadres were specifically injured with iron rods, sticks, and sharp weapons in Dhading.
JTMM-J activists killed a civilian in Rautahat district.
Maoists resumed collecting tourism taxes from foreigners visiting Dhaulagiri peak and upper Dolpa, charging 15 US dollars per tourist.

Maoists abducted Birendra Shah, the Bara correspondent of Nepal FM, from near Dagiya Basti in Bara district. He was murdered by his captors the same day, shot dead by two Maoist cadres on orders from the Bara district committee member and area in-charge, according to an internal Maoist inquiry report made public on 5 November.

Around 500 combatants in the PLA's 7th Division in Kailali district were found to be underage — below 18 years — by UN Mission monitors during the second stage verification, documenting the systematic use of child soldiers by the Maoists.
JTMM-Goit cadres shot dead a VDC secretary in Bara district.
Maoists demanded donations from government offices, VDCs, educational institutions, and vehicle owners across districts.
United Janatantrik Terai Mukti Morcha cadres abducted and killed a schoolteacher in Mahottari district.

The UN Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights raised grave concerns about Maoist violations of rights to physical integrity, liberty, and security, pointing to violence, abduction, and intimidation by Maoist cadres and affiliated organizations.

A UNESCO report revealed that 22,000 students and 10,000 teachers were abducted between 2002 and 2006 during Nepal's insurgency, while 734 teachers and 1,730 students were arrested or tortured during that period — documenting the devastating scale of conflict-related targeting of education.

YCL cadres abducted six persons, including doctors and directors of Nobel Medical College in Biratnagar, and tortured them for 14 hours. In Sarlahi district, 63 VDC secretaries resigned citing extortion and threats by armed groups and government indifference. Civil servants and teachers in Siraha district shut down all government offices and educational institutions for 11 days demanding security guarantees.
Keywords: YCL, In Sarlahi, Siraha, Biratnagar, abduction, extortion/land

Detail: Maoists captured three houses and land belonging to former minister Kamal Thapa.
YCL cadres abducted three passengers in Nuwakot district, assaulting them and looting their phones and NR 25,000.
CPN-Maoist announced the formation of teams to mobilize funds from contractors, hotels, and business companies in multiple regions.
Maoists seized around 95 bighas of land in Morang district from multiple owners.

Maoists in Morang district decided to revive kangaroo courts and parallel government structures amid rising tension with the government. 91 VDC secretaries in Bara district tendered collective resignation citing the government's failure to guarantee security for civil servants in the Terai.

Four Maoists and villagers were injured in clashes in Ramechhap district. All 76 VDC secretaries in Mahottari district left their VDCs after receiving money demands from armed groups and death threats.
Maoists attacked and seriously injured a Nepali Congress leader and VDC treasurer in Okhaldhunga district.

Senior Maoist leader C.P. Gajurel warned his party would not participate in Constituent Assembly polls unless monarchy was abolished beforehand. Senior Central Committee member Mohan Baidhya admitted that YCL's criminal activities — extortion, killings, and kidnappings — were defaming the party and contrary to Central Committee decisions.
Senior Maoist leader Baburam Bhattarai warned his party would return to war if demands for a fully proportional electoral system and republic declaration were not met.

An eight-party agreement fixed Constituent Assembly elections for March-April 2008 and agreed to incorporate democratic republic provisions into the interim constitution, to be implemented by the first CA sitting.
The seven-party alliance signed a 22-point deal agreeing to declare Nepal a federal democratic republic through parliament.

Nepal was declared a federal democratic republic through the passage of the third constitutional amendment, with all responsibilities of head of state transferred to the Prime Minister pending the CA election.

The CPN-Maoist rejoined the interim cabinet after three and a half months in opposition, with five Maoist nominees including Pampha Bhusal, Krishna Bahadur Mahara, Dev Gurung, Hisila Yami, and Matrika Yadav sworn in as ministers.
Seven CPN-UML student activists and a former VDC secretary were injured when YCL cadres attacked them during a programme in Kavre district.

Implementation of the Interim Relief Programme began, providing some financial relief to over 100,000 conflict victims, though not connected to any state acknowledgement of human rights violations. Many categories of victims — including survivors of rape, torture, and serious injury — were ineligible for benefits, leaving a significant portion of those harmed during the conflict without remedy. Contemporary documentation later noted that conflict-related sexual violence and torture survivors were largely excluded from Interim Relief Programme benefits that went primarily to families of those killed or disappeared (Human Rights Watch, Silenced and Forgotten, 2014; later addressed by Supreme Court orders in 2023).
Keywords: CRSV exclusion, torture survivors, Interim Relief Programme
Organizations: Human Rights Watch, Supreme Court of Nepal

Detail: The Supreme Court referred the Maina Sunuwar case to Kavre District Court, which ordered the District Police to open a criminal investigation into the abduction, rape, and killing of the 15-year-old girl by Royal Nepal Army personnel in February 2004.
Keywords: Nepal Army, police, Supreme Court, Kavre, abduction, killing
Organizations: Royal Nepal Army, Nepal Army, Supreme Court of Nepal

Detail: Growing Calls for Truth and AccountabilityVictims' groups and civil society intensify demands for investigation of disappearances, conflict-era killings, torture, sexual violence, and other serious violations.

The Terai-Madhesh Democratic Party submitted an 11-point demand to Prime Minister Koirala, including constitutional guarantee of autonomy with right to self-determination for the Terai-Madhesh region, recognition of the 42 people killed during the 2007 Madhesh agitation as martyrs, compensation to the injured, and proportional recruitment of Madheshi people into the Nepal Army.
JTMM-Jwala Singh cadres shot dead civilian Hari Prasad Chaulagain in Mahottari district.
YCL cadres assaulted local traders in Baitadi district for organizing a vehicle strike in protest against YCL violence.

YCL cadres assaulted and injured a former VDC chairman and a CPN-UML activist in Kaski district. The Chief of Army Staff, Rookmangud Katawal, stated the Nepal Army would not accept any political ideology or political influence through the proposed PLA integration.
Keywords: YCL, PLA, CPN-UML, Nepal Army, Kaski, demobilisation

Detail: Cadres of the Prithvi Singh faction of the JTMM detonated three bombs in Birgunj, Parsa district.
Police arrested a JTMM-J leader in Lalitpur and recovered a revolver.
Security forces arrested two JTMM-J cadres in Bara district and recovered firearms. A cabinet meeting fixed 10 April 2008 as the date for Constituent Assembly elections.
A senior DDC officer in Kapilvastu district was abducted by armed JTMM cadres.
YCL cadres seized over a tonne of ginger from a farm in Panchthar district when the farmer refused to pay a demanded donation.
JTMM-J cadres shot dead journalist Pushpa Shrestha in front of a school in Birgunj, Parsa district — a direct attack on press freedom. The JTMM-J Parsa district in-charge claimed responsibility.
Keywords: JTMM-J, Parsa, Birgunj, killing, clash, press

Detail: Eight persons were injured when a bomb exploded near Bhotahiti in Kathmandu minutes after a seven-party election rally concluded. INSEC found that the Maoists were continuing to operate labour camps in Salyan, Rukum, Pyuthan, and Jajarkot districts, with detainees sentenced by kangaroo courts performing forced labour without pay.
Maoists were reported to be running a kangaroo court in Dhangadhi municipality, Kailali district, in violation of the peace agreement.
Security forces arrested two JTMM-J cadres with a pistol in Rautahat district.
JTMM-J cadres abducted and shot dead government clerk Purna Prasad Dhakal in Banke district; his bullet-ridden body was found three kilometers from where he was abducted.
YCL cadres abducted three Nepali Congress activists in Siraha district.
The Madhesh Mukti Tigers detonated seven bombs in Rajbiraj, Saptari district, ahead of a ministerial visit, causing no casualties.

YCL cadres killed the three Nepali Congress activists — Satya Narayan Yadav, Neem Chandra Thakur, and Ram Ikbaal Yadav — abducted on 20 January. Their bodies were found buried on the bank of the Kamala River in Siraha district.
Keywords: YCL, Nepali Congress, Siraha, abduction, killing

Detail: Demonstrators showed black flags to Nepali Congress leaders in Rajbiraj; one policeman and six demonstrators were hurt in the ensuing riot.
Two bombs were exploded at the venue, with JTMM-J claiming responsibility.
Bombs were detonated in Janakpur ahead of a seven-party meeting and in Inaruwa, Sunsari district, near a Nepali Congress gathering. No casualties were reported.
Maoists detained a Nepali Congress activist in Rukum district for one hour for organizing a party meeting.
JTMM-J cadres exploded a petrol bomb at the CPN-Maoist district office in Dhanusha district.
JTMM-J cadres shot dead a youth in Dhanusha district, accusing him of spying.
YCL cadres captured the house of a civilian in Sankhuwasabha district after he refused to pay a demanded donation.
YCL cadres clashed with police in Panchthar district and seized a policeman's weapon.
CPN-Maoist cadres surrounded the Rautahat District Administration Office demanding release of a detained colleague facing murder charges.

Around 54 persons, including the Chief District Officer of Parsa district, were injured in an explosion outside Narayani Stadium in Birgunj where the seven-party alliance was holding its final electoral assembly. The Madhesh Mukti Tigers claimed responsibility.
JTMM-J cadres shot dead a community forest project guard, Karna Bahadur Biswokarma, while he was on duty in Sarlahi district.
An eight-year-old girl was injured in a bomb blast in Sunsari district near a venue where Nepali Congress leader Sher Bahadur Deuba was addressing a mass meeting.
YCL cadres set ablaze Indian vehicles and imposed a ban on Indian vehicles in Jhapa, Morang, and Sunsari districts protesting the detention of YCL cadres by Indian border security.
More than a dozen bomb explosions rocked Rajbiraj, Saptari district, near a Nepali Congress election rally, injuring around a dozen persons including two policemen.
20 persons, including eight policemen, were injured in clashes between United Madhesi Front cadres and police in Banke district. Major Terai districts were paralyzed by the UMF strike.
YCL cadres assaulted the District Education Officer of Saptari in his office.
JTMM-G published a list of 37 persons in Sunsari district and threatened physical action against them, including civil servants, teachers, and entrepreneurs.
JTMM-J cadres detonated six bombs at the District Education Office and other locations in Mahottari district.
Maoists and Nepali Congress activists clashed in Darchula district when Maoists tried to disrupt an NC election campaign.
Keywords: Nepali Congress, Maoist, Darchula, clash, elections

Detail: Several bombs were detonated near a Nepali Congress mass meeting in Sarlahi district.
Police raided the central YCL office in Kathmandu reportedly searching for concealed weapons.
Two JTMM-J cadres were killed by police in Saptari district.
YCL cadres set ablaze a revenue collection post of the Rautahat District Development Committee.
Around 100 YCL cadres disrupted a Nepali Congress programme in Tanahun district and assaulted former minister and NC leader Govinda Raj Joshi.
Around 3,000 Maoist insurgents attacked the Latinath police post in Darchula district.
JTMM-J cadres abducted a rural health worker in Siraha district.
Two persons were injured when JTMM-J cadres detonated a pressure cooker bomb at the District Election Office in Nepalgunj, Banke district.
The Bara-Parsa district coordinator of JTMM-Goit, Binod Mahato, was shot dead by an unidentified group in Bihar, India.
At least 20 persons were injured when JTMM-J cadres attacked a wedding house in Rautahat district.
Three of four abducted girls were released; property including gold ornaments was looted.

Around 60 persons were injured on the ninth day of the indefinite United Democratic Madhesh Front strike across six Terai districts. Curfew was imposed in multiple district headquarters. Over 100 people were arrested and 30 buses vandalized.
60 persons, including five policemen and four journalists, were injured in clashes between UMDF activists and police in Rautahat and Dhanusha districts.
Four Maoists were injured in a clash with CPN-UML cadres in Arghakhanchi district. An APF head constable was abducted by JTMM-J cadres in Kapilvastu district.
Keywords: JTMM-J, CPN-UML, APF, Maoist, Arghakhanchi, Kapilvastu, abduction, clash

Detail: JTMM-J cadres abducted a civilian in Mahottari district, accusing him of tilling land seized by the group.
21 persons were injured in clashes across the Terai. Agitators set ablaze the Election Commission office in Bara district, injuring four persons.
JTMM-J cadres shot dead APF Head Constable Sukraraj Majhi Chaudhary in Sunsari district.

The government and the UMDF reached a consensus on the key demand of One Madhesh One Pradesh, to be decided through the Constituent Assembly, and agreed to recognize those killed in the Madhesh movement as martyrs and provide their families with compensation.
One person, Jagadesh Pashwan, was killed in police firing in Nawalparasi district on the 14th day of the UMDF strike.
YCL cadres assaulted a schoolteacher in Gorkha district.
One person, Mohammad Biskut Miya, was killed and six others injured when police opened fire at curfew-violating protesters in Sunsari district.
The government and the UMDF signed an eight-point agreement ending the indefinite Terai strike.
JTMM-G killed Nepali Congress leader Gokarna Kandel near his home in Rupandehi district. The Terai Mukti Tigers abducted two police constables from Mahottari district.
Keywords: JTMM-G, Nepali Congress, police, Rupandehi, Mahottari, Terai, abduction, killing

Detail: A writ petition was filed to initiate a criminal investigation into Agni Sapkota, senior Maoist leader, over his alleged involvement in the abduction and killing of civilian Arjun Lama in Kavrepalanchok district on 29 April 2005 during the armed conflict — a case that became emblematic of conflict-era enforced disappearance and extrajudicial execution.
Keywords: Maoist, Kavrepalanchok, abduction, killing, transitional justice

Detail: Madhesh Mukti Tigers cadres shot dead Nepali Congress member Uday Yadav in Dhanusha district.
Akhil Terai Mukti Morcha cadres set ablaze a vehicle belonging to Kantipur daily in Saptari district.
Suspected Maoists abducted the CPN-UML candidate in Manang district.

YCL cadres obstructed Rashtriya Janashakti Party workers from campaigning in Dhankuta district, seizing NR 130,000 in cash and the citizenship certificate of former Prime Minister Surya Bahadur Thapa.
JTMM-J cadres shot dead a civilian in Bara district.
Maoists attacked a CPN-UML election campaign meeting in Ramechhap district, injuring 12 persons including the UML's candidate.
Maoists abducted two RPP workers in Chitwan district.
Maoists severely assaulted a Nepali Congress activist in Gorkha district.
YCL cadres misbehaved with Nepali Congress leaders on campaign in Surkhet district.
Maoists assaulted two Nepal Workers and Peasants Party cadres in Jumla district and filed false cases against them.
YCL cadres attacked a CPN-UML meeting in Dhading district, injuring four activists.
Maoists assaulted two Nepali Congress activists and picketed the home of a Nepali Congress candidate in Gorkha district, assaulting his son and another activist.
CPN-Maoist cadres assaulted a CPN-UML activist in his home in Bardiya district.
Maoists ambushed a Nepali Congress election procession in Okhaldhunga district, injuring an NC cadre.
At least 10 persons were injured in clashes between Nepali Congress and MJF activists in Sunsari district.
Maoists attacked CPN-UML supporters returning from an election rally in Chitwan district.

Two CPN-Maoist cadres were shot dead by unidentified persons in Rolpa district. A CA election candidate from NPF in Banke constituency, Kamal Prasad Adhikari, was shot dead by JTMM-J cadres who had been pressing him to withdraw his candidacy — a direct attack on the electoral process.
Keywords: JTMM-J, CPN-Maoist, Maoist, Rolpa, Banke, killing, clash, elections

Detail: A Maoist area committee member was shot dead in Kapilvastu district.
Maoist cadres vandalized vehicles belonging to Nepali Congress candidates in the district in protest.
YCL cadres attacked the vehicle of former Deputy Prime Minister and CPN-UML leader K.P. Sharma Oli in Jhapa district, smashing its windowpanes.
Police arrested three PLA cadres in Rolpa district and seized an AK-47 and INSAS rifle.

A Democracy and Election Alliance report documented around 170 incidents of election-related violence across the country in the preceding three months, in which 20 persons were killed, 623 injured, and 24 abducted, with the majority of incidents attributed to armed Terai outfits and Maoists.
Two persons were killed and two others injured when unidentified assailants lobbed a bomb inside a mosque in Biratnagar.
A group called National Defence Army claimed responsibility.
Two persons of a family were killed when a bomb left behind by Maoists exploded inside a house in Jajarkot district.
YCL cadres threatened villagers in Nawalparasi district with eviction if they did not vote for the Maoists.
Four persons, including a child, were injured in a bomb blast in Birgunj by the Madhesh Mukti Tigers.
Maoists abducted 10 CPN-UML cadres on election campaign in Jajarkot district.
10 Nepali Congress cadres, including the party's candidate from Rasuwa, were injured when around 200 YCL cadres attacked them.
Maoists abducted six Nepali Congress cadres from Dadeldhura district.
Six policemen were injured when YCL cadres pelted stones at them in Rasuwa district.
Five persons were injured in a bomb blast in Birgunj, Parsa district.
Three CPN-UML activists and three RPP leaders were injured in YCL attacks on their election programmes in Chitwan district.
A CPN-UML district committee member was injured in an attack by 65 Maoists in Dolpa district.
YCL cadres attacked a Nepali Congress team in Nawalparasi district, injuring two policemen and six NC cadres.
Five CPN-UML activists, a poll monitor, and a Nepali Congress activist were injured in Maoist attacks in Ramechhap district.
Keywords: Nepali Congress, CPN-UML, Maoist, Ramechhap, clash, elections

Detail: Unidentified assailants abducted and killed a Rastriya Janashakti Party activist in Bhirgaun VDC.

At least 10 persons, including two children, were injured when a bomb exploded in Parsa district during a Nepali Congress rally. Suspected JTMM-J cadres abducted an election official overseeing a polling centre in Mahottari district.
Keywords: JTMM-J, Nepali Congress, Parsa, Mahottari, abduction, bombing, children, elections

Detail: Seven Maoists were killed in police firing during a clash between Maoists and Nepali Congress workers in Dang district. A CPN-UML candidate for Surkhet-1, Rishi Prasad Sharma, was killed by a bullet during the clash.
Keywords: Nepali Congress, CPN-UML, police, Maoist, Dang, Surkhet, killing, clash

Detail: Police arrested 31 YCL cadres with weapons, including a pistol, knives, and iron rods, in Rupandehi district.

The Constituent Assembly elections were held with approximately 60 percent voter turnout. One CPN-UML activist, Rishiraj Subedi, was killed by unidentified persons in Kaski district on polling day. The first Constituent Assembly election marked a major milestone in Nepal's transitional period; major political parties publicly committed to a transitional justice process, and the CA later drafted a transitional justice bill and conducted 19 sub-committee discussions before its dissolution, after which the bill lapsed.
Seven persons were injured when Maoists clashed with security forces at Gaur.
Around 25 Maoists attacked and injured Finance Minister Ram Sharan Mahat in Nuwakot district.
Seven other persons, including two Nepali Congress supporters, a police inspector, and four children, were also injured.
YCL cadres set ablaze a Nepali Congress leader's house in Khotang district.
At least 22 Nepali Congress workers were displaced from their villages in Rukum district following post-election Maoist threats.
The first meeting of the Constituent Assembly declared Nepal a Federal Democratic Republic and formally abolished the monarchy.
Armed Madhesh Mukti Tigers cadres shot and injured a businessman in Birgunj, Parsa district.
The CPN-Maoist threatened to quit the government if not allowed to form the next government by 5 June.
YCL cadres attacked and injured two civilians in Tanahun district.
At least 20 persons were injured when Maoist cadres clashed with CPN-UML-backed cooperative members in Ramechhap district.
A Maoist kangaroo court issued a summons to a civilian in Dang district.
Two ATMF cadres were killed in a police encounter in Bara district.

Most adult male members of around 50 families in Kalikot district fled to the district headquarters after Maoists threatened to kill them following a dispute over an inter-caste marriage between Dalits and Brahmins — illustrating how caste-related tensions intersected with post-conflict Maoist coercion.

Maoist cadres in Dadeldhura district blocked the drinking water supply to over five villages because their residents had not voted for the Maoists in the Constituent Assembly elections, punishing civilians collectively for their electoral choices.
Former King Gyanendra Shah left the Narayanhiti Palace.
JTMM-J cadres abducted and shot dead a Surya Nepal employee in Bara district.
Govinda Prasad Pandey, convenor of the Bardiya Civil Society Network and former mayor of Gulariya Municipality, was shot dead by unidentified assailants inside his home in Bardiya district.
An explosion at the International Organization for Migration office in Damak destroyed part of the building.
JTMM-J claimed responsibility. The IOM had been involved in resettling Bhutanese refugees.
JTMM cadres shot dead a local businessman in Mahottari district after abducting him; a second abducted businessman remained missing.
YCL cadres allegedly shot and injured a 22-year-old CPN-UML member in Baitadi district.
An unidentified group shot dead a civilian in Sarlahi district.

An YCL cadre was abducted and subsequently killed by an unidentified group in retaliation for his involvement in an abduction and extortion drive. The Kirant Janabadi Workers Party set ablaze the furniture and documents of three VDCs in Bhojpur district.
A nine-year-old girl, Rajani Sahani, was killed and her two sisters and father were injured when two bombs exploded inside their home in Sarlahi district.
Unidentified assailants abducted and killed a local Nepali Congress leader, Pashupati Rana, in Mahottari district.
A group claiming affiliation with JTMM claimed responsibility.

The Agriculture Development Bank's eastern regional office in Morang district reported failure to collect NR 1.5 billion in farmer loans after Maoists persuaded small farmers not to repay, disrupting rural financial systems.

Conflict Victims’ Society for Justice (CVSJ-Nepal) was formally registered with the District Administration Office, Kathmandu (and with the Social Welfare Council on 24 September 2008), consolidating conflict victims — including survivors and families of the disappeared and killed — into a national-level victim organisation that later partnered with Advocacy Forum on justice advocacy.
Keywords: CVSJ, Conflict Victims Society for Justice, survivor organisation, victim association, Kathmandu, district-to-national organising
Organizations: Conflict Victims’ Society for Justice (CVSJ-Nepal); District Administration Office Kathmandu; Social Welfare Council

Detail: Sharma et al. v. Nepal Submitted to the UN Human Rights CommitteeThe family of a conflict-era disappearance victim submits one of the first Nepal conflict-related communications to the UN Human Rights Committee after failing to obtain justice through domestic mechanisms.

Ashok Kumar Yadav of Motipur killed in a bomb blast at Belahath, Dang District. An Indian national, Bimal Gupta of Bihar, was injured in a bomb blast in front of Kathmandu Mall at Sundhara, Kathmandu; a pamphlet of Ranabir Sena, an underground outfit, was found at the explosion site.
First Truth and Reconciliation Commission Bill IntroducedThe Government introduces the first draft legislation to establish a Truth and Reconciliation Commission.
Amnesty Debate BeginsProposed amnesty provisions for conflict-era violations generate strong criticism from victims' groups, human rights organizations, and international actors.

Ram Bhandari founded the National Network of Families of Disappeared and Missing Nepal (NEFAD), growing out of a small family organization established in 2006, to amplify the demands of families of the disappeared across Nepal.
Supreme Court issued a stay order asking the Government not to implement its decision to withdraw 349 cases, noting that criminal cases related to law and order were included in the withdrawal list.

Police arrested two persons in connection with a blast near the main entrance of Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu. Ranabir Sena claimed responsibility, stating the blast was a warning to the Government and the CPN-Maoist.
CPN-Maoist cadres attacked the Bhandaris (aides of the Pashupati priests) and other devotees in the Pashupatinath temple premises, Kathmandu, injuring at least 10 persons.
YCL cadres attacked CPN-UML cadre Bibek Devkota from Jitpur VDC, Nuwakot; doctors were forced to amputate his left leg.

Security guard Bhawanath Pudasaini was abducted from his workplace at Basudeva Industries Pvt. Ltd, Banjhariya-7, Bara District, and shot dead. Tabaresh, District in-charge of the JTMM-J, claimed responsibility.
Journalist Uma Singh, a woman reporter based in Janakpur, was killed by unidentified assailants who forcibly entered her apartment in Rajoula and killed her with sharp weapons.

Three years earlier, her father and elder brother had been abducted by persons her family accused of being CPN-Maoist cadres. Separately, one person identified as Pachhu Hajara was shot dead at Raghunathpur-6, Rautahat District.
ATMM cadres shot dead Rajkumar Kamati, former chairman of Sirauwa Pachuware VDC, Siraha District, accusing him of acting as a police informant. ATMM District in-charge Biplov claimed responsibility.
YCL in-charge Babar Khan and other cadres abducted a 16-year-old girl, Bahida Khatoon, a CPN-UML supporter, from her residence, and also robbed NR 25,000 and valuables.
MRJP-R shot dead two youths, Ram Udgar Muchi and Ramesh, residents of Phulkaha Katti-5, Siraha. District Commander Arjun claimed responsibility.

Police arrested Unified CPN-Maoist cadre Shrawan Yadav, Siraha-5 regional committee member, on charges of murdering journalist Uma Singh. Another accused, Nemlal Paswan, described as 'army commander' of the Terai Ekata Parishad, was arrested a day earlier from Saghar, Dhanusha District.
Keywords: CPN-Maoist, Unified CPN-Maoist, police, Maoist, Dhanusha, Siraha, Terai, killing, press

Detail: Police constable Awadesh Kumar Jha injured when unidentified armed gang attacked a temporary Police Post at Padampokhari VDC, Makawanpur District.

ATMM cadres abducted two persons, Bik Narayan Yadav and Shankar Yadav, residents of Lohojhara-2, from Bhardaha Chowk, Saptari District, citing their alleged affiliation with another Terai armed group.

Two persons killed and one woman injured in a bomb blast at a marketplace in Rautahat's Katahariya VDC. The dead were identified as Jayanarayan Mahato (died on the spot) and Hari Raya (died the following day). Terai Army vice-president Mister Shahansha claimed responsibility.
JTMM-Rajan central committee member Manoj Mukti threatened to kill Jitendra Khadga, correspondent with Kantipur newspaper, by telephone.

Three high-intensity bombs detonated in a series at Rajbiraj, headquarters of Saptari District, Terai. A minor, Pooja Das, was injured by splinters in the second explosion. Property estimated at NR 400,000 destroyed.
Five persons, including two minors, injured when a bomb planted at Maisthan, Birgunj, exploded. Bhagat Singh, Parsa District in-charge of Madheshi Mukti Tigers, claimed responsibility.
Unidentified armed group attacked a Police Post at Syaulibang, Pyuthan District, killing one policeman identified as Suman G.C. and looting all 10 weapons including five 3-knot-3 rifles.
Police suspected the Mongolian Mukti Morcha.
Police shot dead the Eastern area commander of the ATMM, Lalan Kumar Yadav alias Bikrant, in Saptari District.
Three other cadres were arrested. Bikrant had claimed responsibility for killing a worker at Surya Nepal Private Limited in June 2008.

Shakti Bahadur Basnet, personal secretary of Prime Minister Prachanda and a Unified CPN-Maoist politburo member, sustained bullet injury when an unidentified gang opened fire on him at Koteshwor, Kathmandu. The Mongolian Mukti Morcha (MMM) claimed responsibility for the earlier Syaulibang Police Post attack.
Keywords: CPN-Maoist, Unified CPN-Maoist, police, Maoist, Prachanda, Kathmandu, clash

Detail: Three YCL cadres were attacked and one, Ramesh Shrestha, was abducted from the YCL office in Okhaldhunga District.
Nepali Congress leader Krishna Bahadur Balami of Okharpauwa injured in an attack by YCL cadres in Nuwakot.
Bomb exploded at the UNHCR office in Nepalgunj. Pamphlets of a previously unheard group, Bhisan Himali Bag, were found at the site; security sources suspected Hindu extremist involvement.
Unidentified group detonated a pressure cooker bomb at the Nepali Congress district office in Hasanpur, Dhangadhi.

Narendra Khati, supervisor at the Janakpur cigarette factory, shot dead in Janakpur. A person claiming to be a JTMM-J cadre claimed responsibility. Separately, unidentified gunmen shot dead Gambhir Saud, a resident of Sripur VDC-4, and injured his son Prem at Dhangadi, Kailali District.
An unidentified group vandalised and set ablaze the Pahupatinagar VDC office in Bardiya District.
Radio journalist Gyanendra Raj Mishra sustained bullet injury when an unidentified gang opened fire near his office at Ward 4, Birgunj municipality.

One security personnel was hacked to death and another was seriously injured by Tharu demonstrators in Sauraha region, Chitwan District, following the killing of two Tharu agitators in police firing a day earlier.

PLA cadres from Jit Smriti Brigade indiscriminately attacked a rally of local residents of Kalyan VDC-3, Surkhet District, who were protesting ongoing PLA raids in the village. The attack was described as reprisal following an assault on a Maoist soldier by locals during the Holi festival on 11 March.
Keywords: PLA, Maoist, Kalyan, Surkhet, clash, protest

Detail: Pressure cooker bomb exploded at the Nepali Congress office, Nepalgunj-13, Banke District.
JTMM-J's Bhagat Singh claimed responsibility. A second bomb damaged the shutters of the Unified CPN-Maoist office on Surkhet Road, Nepalgunj.

Detail: Seven persons injured when a bomb exploded in front of Maistahan Temple, Birgunj, Parsa District. Over 90% of locals in Kanchanpur, Bara District, fled their homes after approximately 300 persons claiming to be Unified CPN-Maoist cadres looted and vandalised over two dozen houses.

Detail: CPN-UML cadre Brija Mohan Yadav shot dead and another injured at Jhatikaiya, Dhanusha District.
Unidentified gang detonated a powerful pressure cooker bomb at Sukauli VDC office, Nawalparasi District, completely destroying the building.
One person killed and another injured when a bomb exploded at the Transport Management Office in Nepalgunj. The deceased died while attempting to detonate the device.
YCL established planned checkpoints at two bordering areas of Rolpa District to screen persons entering the district.

Two persons, including a 12-year-old child, injured when JTMM-Prithvi Singh cadres detonated a bomb at the office of Sahara Savings and Cooperatives in Malangawa, Sarlahi District, over non-payment of extortion demands.
Police shot dead two persons in Birgunj, claiming they were involved in bomb blasts, extortion and shootings.
Four persons were injured while making a bomb in the same town.

Unidentified gunman shot dead Sanjaya Kumar Gupta in Birgunj, Parsa District. Separately, unidentified gunmen on a motorcycle shot dead Prachanda Thaiba, a Youth Force (CPN-UML youth wing) cadre, at Butwal-9 Deepnagar, Rupandehi District. ATMM District in-charge Rakesh Bidrohi claimed responsibility.

Detail: Five persons injured when a powerful socket bomb exploded at Garuda Bazaar, Rautahat District.
JTMM-J commander Barud Singh claimed responsibility.

Anuj Thapa Magar (male, seventh grade student, also a Youth Force cadre) killed and two others injured when a gang of five stabbed them in front of Namuna Higher Secondary School, Biratnagar, Morang District. Eyewitnesses claimed the assailants were YCL-affiliated.
Keywords: YCL, Youth Force, Morang, Biratnagar, killing

Detail: Unified CPN-Maoist women cadres assaulted Nanda Bhandari, a government lawyer, on the premises of Surkhet District court.

Nepali Congress cadre Prem Bahadur Kandel killed by an unidentified group in Thaparek VDC, Nuwakot District. Over a dozen people, including two policemen, were injured in clashes between Unified CPN-Maoist and CPN-Maoist (Matrika Yadav faction) cadres in Biratnagar; local administration imposed prohibitory orders.
