Detail: Santosh Shah, CPN-ML candidate for Dhanusha constituency-5, abducted from Binahi by the Terai Rastriya Mukti Sena on the eve of the Constituent Assembly by-election.

JTMM-J cadre Parasuram Kori shot dead by Police in an encounter at Shivapur village, Banke District. His mother, Buduni Kori, stated he was innocent and had been forcibly taken by JTMM-J three days earlier.

MRJP-R cadres shot dead Chatthu Yadav, district in-charge of Madheshi Mukti Tigers and a resident of Ayodhyanagar, at Mahanaur-3 VDC, Siraha District. The MRJP-R stated Yadav had been involved in extortion.

Three persons killed by an unidentified gang in Mabu VDC area, Ilam District. The deceased were identified as Moti Bahadur Gurung of Mabu VDC-7, Gunj Bahadur Gurung, and Purna Kumari Gurung; bodies were found at Moti Bahadur's house.

Two children, Hom Bahadur B.K. and Bam Bahadur B.K. (both 11 years old), killed in a stray bomb explosion in a forest in Gulmi District. The children had gone to herd cattle and were playing with what they believed was a toy.
A UN report confirmed that Prime Minister Prachanda's commitment to remove all disqualified child combatants from the PLA cantonments by end of February 2009 had not been implemented.
A new UN report stated that commitments to remove disqualified child combatants from Maoist cantonments remained unimplemented eight months after the Maoist-led Government's initial commitment.

Agitating Tharu activists set ablaze seven Village Development Committee offices in Kailali District (Sadhepani, Balia, Bhajani, Joshipur, Thapapur, Dododhara and Ramshikarjhala). All documents and furniture were destroyed.

TJSC activists set ablaze eight VDC offices in Dang District's Deukhuri valley (Gobardiha, Gangaparspur, Gadhawa, Lalmatiya, Sishaniya, Sonapur, Bela and Rajpur), destroying all furniture and documents.

National Human Rights Commission directed the Home Ministry to clarify why it had recommended withdrawal of 238 court cases against alleged perpetrators of the September 2007 Kapilvastu carnage, described by the NHRC as one of the gravest incidents of human rights violation after the 2006 peace deal.
Organizations: National Human Rights Commission of Nepal

Detail: Prime Minister Prachanda ResignsPrime Minister Pushpa Kamal Dahal (Prachanda) resigns following a dispute over the dismissal of the Army Chief, triggering a political crisis and contributing to delays in key peace process and transitional justice commitments.

The Maoist-led Government removed Chief of Army Staff General Rookmangud Katawal, triggering a constitutional crisis. President Ram Baran Yadav directed Katawal to continue in post in his capacity as Commander-in-Chief, overturning the cabinet decision. The CPN-UML subsequently withdrew from the coalition Government.

Prime Minister Pushpa Kamal Dahal resigned following the President's reinstatement of army chief Katawal. The Unified CPN-Maoist announced it would agitate in parliament and the streets until its decision to dismiss Katawal was implemented.

Tekbir Budha, chairman of the armed outfit Mongolian Revenge Group (MRG), shot dead at Gam VDC, Rolpa District, by six masked gunmen. Separately, the Maoist district committee in Ramechhap issued a warning to Nepali Congress and CPN-UML members to leave the District by 9 May or face 'physical action'.
Keywords: Nepali Congress, CPN-UML, Maoist, Gam, Rolpa, killing

Detail: UN Mission in Nepal (UNMIN) chief Karin Landgren warned that the political crisis threatened gains made in the peace process.
YCL District notice in Siraha threatened 'physical action' against those supporting the President's reinstatement of the army chief.

YCL cadres also distributed pamphlets warning of 'punishment' in Banke and Bardiya Districts. Separately, Education Minister Renu Kumari Yadav (MJF) was reported to have issued death threats to Avenues Television journalist Baidha Nath Yadav of Saptari.
Keywords: YCL, MJF, Banke, Bardiya, Saptari, press

Detail: A senior Maoist leader, Central Secretariat member Top Bahadur Rayamajhi, publicly called on party cadres to chase NC and CPN-UML activists from villages and take 'people's action' against those supporting the President's move, warning of the resumption of armed struggle if the party was 'forced'.

Maoists attacked NC leader Basanta Raj Bhatt (approximately 60 knife-wielding cadres), looting NR 27,000, and assaulted CPN-UML member Gopal Silwal, NC cadres Krishna Paudel and teacher Keshav Paudel in Banke District.
Jiva Nath Chaudhary, junior clerk at the District Development Committee in Dhanusha District, shot and wounded by unidentified gunmen.

Two other DDC officials also sustained bullet injuries. The NHRC expressed serious concern over organised Maoist attacks on leaders and cadres of opposing parties in at least 13 districts, including Sankhuwasabha, Bhojpur, Jhapa, Saptari, Panchthar, Morang, Dhankuta, Dolakha, Ramechhap, Kailali, Bardiya, Khotang and Taplejung.
Keywords: Maoist, NHRC, Jhapa, Saptari, Morang, Dolakha, Kailali, Bardiya, clash
Organizations: National Human Rights Commission of Nepal

Detail: Two persons, Suresh Singh of Tenuwapatti-9 and Ram Narayan Singh of Sitapur, Siraha District, sustained bullet injuries in an attack by unidentified gunmen in Lahan. Madhesh Rastra Janatantrik-Revolutionary claimed responsibility.

Yam Bahadur Roka killed and his son Ramesh Roka seriously injured when a stray bomb exploded at Bhingri VDC, Pyuthan District. Separately, 30 persons were injured when a cylinder bomb exploded on a passenger train heading from Jayanagar to Janakpur, near Parabaha station, Dhanusha District. The Terai Rastriya Mukti Sena claimed responsibility. Unified CPN-Maoist cadres clashed with Nepali Congress activists at Bariyaarpur-4, Bara District, leaving more than a dozen injured; at least eight were in critical condition.
Keywords: CPN-Maoist, Unified CPN-Maoist, Nepali Congress, Maoist, Bhingri, Pyuthan, Dhanusha, Bara, Janakpur, Terai, killing, bombing

Detail: Nepali Congress activist Uma Kant Hamal killed in Jumla. He was abducted from his house at midnight by approximately 25 persons; his body was found in a jungle the following morning. NC accused YCL cadres of responsibility.

Two persons killed and 13 others wounded when a bomb exploded inside a Catholic church in Dhobighat, Lalitpur District. The deceased were identified as Alicy Joshi (Indian national) and Deepa Paitri. A leaflet of the Defence Army was found at the site.

Teacher Menuka Kumari Sah abducted and shot dead by JTMM-Prithvi (Prithvi Singh faction) cadres near Itiyahi at Bhulahibharwaliya VDC, Bara District. District military commander Dewa claimed responsibility.
Buddha Laxmi Joseph (female, 45) died in hospital from injuries sustained in the 23 May church bomb blast in Lalitpur, raising the death toll to three.
Maoists assaulted Nepali Congress District president Mukti Prasad Nyaupane at Badalkot, Kalikot, as he was travelling to the district headquarters.

Rajan Bohora, a 10-year-old boy, killed and two others (Mohan Bohora and Amar Bohora) injured when a bomb exploded in the premises of Mahadev Higher Secondary School, Kapalseri VDC, Bajhang District. The children had accidentally picked up the stray bomb from the debris of a house damaged by Maoists during the insurgency. Separately, a woman was arrested in connection with the 23 May church bombing in Lalitpur; Police identified her as Sita Shrestha Thapa (27), who admitted placing the pressure cooker bomb.
Keywords: police, Maoist, Kapalseri, Bajhang, Lalitpur, killing, bombing, children

Detail: Special Court issued clean chits to Unified CPN-Maoist Chairman Pushpa Kamal Dahal, senior leader Baburam Bhattarai, and over a dozen Maoists on charges of treason related to the Bandipur Police Post attack of 26 January 2001, citing insufficient Government evidence.
Keywords: CPN-Maoist, Unified CPN-Maoist, police, Maoist, clash

Detail: Ladai Shah, a Maoist from Pataura VDC, Rautahat District, died in Kathmandu from injuries sustained when CPN-UML cadres attacked him following the arrest of two YCL cadres who had shown black flags to Prime Minister Nepal on 1 June.
Keywords: YCL, CPN-UML, Maoist, Pataura, Rautahat, Kathmandu, clash

Detail: Police seized a cache of bombs and guns hidden in a rice mill at Indrapur VDC, Banke District; two pistols, two guns, and a socket bomb recovered. The Janatantrik Madhesh Mukti Tiger, a Terai outfit, was believed responsible.
Prakash B.K., a civilian man, died in a landmine explosion at Lamahi, Dang District, after accidentally stepping on a mine planted by the Nepal Army near Arjunkhola.
Indian national Narendra Kumar Sharma, from Ghaziabad, Uttar Pradesh, seriously injured when a socket bomb he was carrying exploded at Radhakrishna Chowk, Gulariya, Bardiya District.
A group of journalists including Federation of Nepalese Journalists general secretary Ramji Dahal attacked by ANNISU-R cadres in Nepalgunj; vehicle damaged.

Unified CPN-Maoist cadres clashed with police and vandalised government offices during nationwide sit-in protests. Several persons, including a Maoist CA member, were injured at Singha Durbar. Cameras of photojournalists were damaged. Violence also erupted in Kavre, Bardiya, Darchula, Mahottari, Ramechhap, Ilam, Morang and Baitadi, injuring at least 50 people; police used tear gas in Baitadi and Bardiya. The Dhading local development officer was also assaulted.
Keywords: CPN-Maoist, Unified CPN-Maoist, police, Maoist, Kavre, Bardiya, Mahottari, Ilam, Morang, clash, protest

Detail: MRJP cadres shot dead CPN-UML activist Ram Swagarath Kapadi at his home in Kharihani VDC-5, Dhanusha District. MRJP District in-charge Ganesh claimed responsibility.

Police arrested Bhairav Yadav alias Mister Sahansa, vice-chairman of Terai Army, and Birendra Yadav (Sarlahi District in-charge of JTMM-Prithvi), from Sarlahi District. They were linked to extortion, kidnapping and murder in Rautahat and Sarlahi, and to bomb explosions in Kathmandu.
Keywords: JTMM-Prithvi, police, Sarlahi, Terai, Rautahat, Kathmandu, killing, bombing, extortion/land

Detail: Twelve people were injured in a clash between a local Madhesi community and YCL cadres at Khairapur, Gulariya Municipality-2, Bardiya District.

Ministry of Peace and Reconstruction began the discharge process of 4,008 disqualified PLA combatants — including 2,975 identified as minors at the time of the May 2006 ceasefire — from the cantonment at Hattikhor, Nawalparasi. Process was later halted due to lack of Maoist cooperation.
Keywords: PLA, Maoist, Nawalparasi, demobilisation, peace process, children
Organizations: Ministry of Peace and Reconstruction, PLA

Detail: Police shot dead Prashuram Yadav, Siraha District in-charge of the Madheshi Mukti Tiger, while he was being transferred in custody. According to police, he attempted to flee.
Unified CPN-Maoist CA member Prem Tamang and Tamang People's organisation leader Kumar Blon assaulted by locals at Balaju, Kathmandu, while allegedly attempting to disrupt traffic.
Akash Tyagi, 'military commander' of the Terai Madhesh Rastra Mukti Sena (TMRMS), killed in an exchange of fire with police at Bhrampura Police Station, Janakpur.
YCL central leader Laxman Yadav shot dead in Bishrampur VDC, Rautahat District. The Terai Janatantrik Mukti Morcha-Arun claimed responsibility.

Eleven persons injured when YCL cadres attacked an RPP-N signature campaign at Chipledhunga, Kaski District; four policemen, six RPP-N activists including District chairman Devijung Gurung, and YCL District chairman Sushil Devkota were among the injured. Separately, four Terai armed groups — MMT, MVK, Terai Samyukta Janatantrik Party and JTMM-Rajan — warned of intensified armed struggle if Government did not resume peace talks.
Keywords: YCL, JTMM-Rajan, MMT, Kaski, Terai, clash, peace process

Detail: YCL cadres led by chairman Rohit physically assaulted and smeared black soot on the face of Industrial Area Management Limited General Manager Giriraj Mani Bhandari at a press conference in Balaju, Kathmandu; IAML staff members were also injured while trying to protect him. Separately, approximately 406 sets of gelatin, 584 detonators and 30 rolls of safety fuse were seized by Armed Police Force from Gaddachauki Customs, Mahendranagar, Kanchanpur, along the India-Nepal border.

PLA fighters of First Division Cantonment (Ilam) abducted two CPN-Maoist (Matrika Yadav faction) District leaders, Santa Rai (Jhapa chairman) and Sharan Rai (security branch coordinator), from Damak, Jhapa District; both were former PLA combatants who had defected. Separately, police arrested two JTMM-Rajan Mukti cadres — including an Indian national, Mithilesh Kumar Yadav — at Nagdhunga, Kathmandu, with three grenades, two socket bombs and two hand grenades.
Keywords: PLA, JTMM-Rajan, CPN-Maoist, police, Maoist, Jhapa, Ilam, Kathmandu, abduction, bombing, demobilisation

Detail: Approximately 200 PLA combatants of the Bahubiryodha Brigade, Sahajpur, Kailali District, left their cantonment and assaulted 36 local civilians at Shantipur, Nigali VDC-1. Victims stated they were threatened with reprisals if they reported the incident to police or media.
Bomb exploded at the Nepali Congress central office at Sanepa, Kathmandu, damaging windows. Pamphlets of the Nepal Defence Army, an underground outfit, were found inside.
Police shot dead Maoist cadre Lal Dhoj Limbu (Liban Village Committee secretary) and injured YCL cadre Lokesh Limbu when an unidentified gang opened fire at Goskhana Tole, Taplejung.

Police detained 19 PLA combatants, including an assistant brigade commander, with nine UNMIN-registered weapons at Jitpur, Kapilvastu District, while they were returning from Nepalgunj to the PLA Fourth Division cantonment. UNMIN described this as 'a serious violation of the Comprehensive Peace Agreement.'

Detail: Socket bomb exploded outside Vice President Paramananda Jha's residence at Gaurighat, Kathmandu, injuring one woman. The Kirat Janabadi Workers Party claimed responsibility, stating Jha was targeted for taking his oath of office in Hindi.

Police arrested Ram Prasad Mainali, chairman of the Nepal Defence Army (NDA), an armed religious extremist group, from Jhapa District, and the NDA's Morang District commander, Tribhuvan Yadav alias 'Police', from Morang. The NDA claimed the May 2009 Assumption Church bombing in Jawalakhel in which four people were killed and 15 injured.
Police seized a pistol with bullets, a revolver, pipe bombs, sutali bombs and pamphlets.
Three persons killed and five others injured in a bomb explosion at Malakheti VDC, Kailali District. The bomb exploded at the home of Harka Bhadaur Mahata.

Government and Unified CPN-Maoist reached an agreement to resume discharge of 4,008 disqualified PLA combatants — most of them minors — after a two-month stalemate during which Maoists had refused to cooperate with the Ministry of Peace and Reconstruction's July mission to the camps.

Detail: At least 15 Unified CPN-Maoist cadres and two policemen injured as Maoists attempted to disrupt the convocation ceremony of Purwanchal University in Biratnagar, attended by Prime Minister Madhav Nepal.

APF arrested two JTMM-G cadres — Satyendra Pandey (21) and Ramprabesh Pandit (17, a minor) — at Parsa, with a bomb they were planning to detonate at Apex Pharmaceuticals in Birgunj. A police constable was injured when the bomb went off during confiscation.

Nepali Congress Tarun Dal cadre Chandra Prakash Hanggam killed on the Mechi Highway, Ilam-Godak section, Taplejung District, when approximately half a dozen assailants attacked him on a motorcycle. His pillion rider Patanwa was seriously injured.

Detail: Nepali Congress alleged Unified CPN-Maoist involvement.

Detail: PLA 'commander' Narendra Tamrakar arrested in Dadeldhura District on charges of abducting a girl, Kalawati Tamrakar (18 years old), from Ajayameru VDC-7 in broad daylight with six other men. Kalawati was recovered and returned to her family. The other six perpetrators were at large.

Unified CPN-Maoist-called nationwide general strike brought life to a standstill across the country, protesting the killing of three people by police in action against squatters in the Kailali-based Dudhejhadi forest on 4 December.
Keywords: CPN-Maoist, Unified CPN-Maoist, police, Maoist, Kailali, killing, protest

Maoist students set ablaze the campus chief's office of Mahendra Bindeshowri Multiple Campus in Rajbiraj.
Maoists vandalised government offices and vehicles in Gorkha, Butwal and other districts.
At least 17 strike enforcers arrested for vandalism and arson.

At least 22 Tarun Dal (Nepali Congress youth wing) activists injured when Unified CPN-Maoist cadres attacked their microbus at Harmatari Chowk, Gorkha District. Cadres pelted stones and vandalised the vehicle, and police intervened to prevent the activists from being burned alive inside. Detail: Omkar Gosain, 'Baguada region commander' of the Terai Janatantrik Mukti Tigers (TJMT), killed in an exchange of fire with Armed Police Force in a forest in Banke District. Separately, the Matrika Yadav-led CPN-Maoist announced formation of a military wing in eastern Nepal, the Namsam Memorial Battalion, comprising approximately 650 combatants who had defected from the Unified CPN-Maoist.

Detail: Reports indicated that Unified CPN-Maoist cadres in Dang District were selling land seized during the insurgency. Landowners were prevented from selling their own land without paying the party. Cadres were reported to be submitting 20-25% of proceeds to the party.
Keywords: CPN-Maoist, Unified CPN-Maoist, Maoist, Dang, extortion/land

Detail: Approximately 20 hectares belonging to 16 people had been sold in this manner.
The Committee for Social Justice (CSJ), established in Lamjung District in 2007 to organise and advocate for conflict victims, was formally registered.

ANNISU-R cadres (Unified CPN-Maoist student wing) attacked Nepali Congress's Nepal Student Union District member Rajkumar Dangi at Narayani Salyani conference hall near Mahendra Multiple Campus, Dang District.

Detail: CPN-Maoist activists injured when they clashed with Police at Sangam Chowk, Chitwan District.
Special Committee Advances Combatant ManagementEfforts continue to integrate and rehabilitate former Maoist combatants.

Unified CPN-Maoist called for Kailali District closure protesting against Nepal Army patrolling at Dudejhari. Background: five persons including a junior Police officer were killed in Kailali violence on 4 December 2009 after Police used force to evict Maoist-backed illegal squatters from Dudejhari forest.

Detail: First batch of 201 former child soldiers of the PLA — 155 minors and 46 recruited after the cut-off date — left the Second Division main cantonment at Dudhauli, beginning the formal discharge process. The Dudhauli camp held 372 disqualified combatants who had failed UNMIN verification in December 2007.

At least eight persons, six from Youth Force (CPN-UML) and two YCL cadres, were injured in a clash at Madirambeni VDC after the YCL attempted to seize maize belonging to local resident Ramalaya Guthi.
Keywords: YCL, CPN-UML, Youth Force, Madirambeni, clash

Detail: JTMM cadre Sanjeev shot dead the bodyguard of Parsa's Assistant Chief District Officer, identified as Anandaraj Khadka, and injured the officer Balbahadur Malla at the District headquarters in Birgunj.

Detail: Unified CPN-Maoist leader Rajesh Mandal (30), in charge of the Maoists' Bhojpura Rajya Samiti at Parsa area no. 2, shot dead in Bara District. A caller claiming to be a member of Terai Army claimed responsibility.

INSEC survey of Gorkha District found the UCPN-M topped human rights violation incidents for the year, involved in 11 of 16 documented incidents — including manhandling, threatening and displacing more than two dozen people.

WikiLeaks released a US Embassy New Delhi cable (dated 18 April 2006) stating the Indian Government believed the Nepalese Maoists sold arms to Indian Naxalites: 'The Naxalites have bought some arms from Nepalese Maoists.'

SJMM intensified an extortion drive in Itahari, Dharan, Hasposa, and Sunsari District, causing widespread fear among the business community and Government officials. Traders reported demands ranging from NPR 10,000 to NPR 100,000.
UNMIN Completes Its Mission

The Ministry of Peace and Reconstruction issued Interim Relief Directives, declaring a relief program of NPR 1 million and a rehabilitation program for family members of killed and disappeared persons, as well as for the injured and displaced.

Cadres of the Limbuwan State Council (LSC) assaulted CA member Mina Pun (RJP) and other party activists at Damak Chowk, Jhapa District, during a party programme. More than 100 LSC cadres chased Pun and her supporters and seized banners, pamphlets, and other materials.
MJF Nepal cadres assaulted a team of RJM activists led by senior leader Rashmiraj Nepali in Birgunj, Parsa District. RJM Chairman Chitra Bahadur KC condemned the attack as 'violent and undemocratic'.

Nepal Army bomb squad, aided by Police, defused a bomb planted at the Manamaiju VDC office in Kathmandu. Leaflets of a previously unknown outfit calling itself 'United Nations Morcha' were found at the scene.

Detail: Police reported that a group of former PLA combatants calling itself the People's Liberation Army Former Soldiers' Unity Organisation (PLAFSUG), largely comprising disqualified Maoist combatants, was operating an extortion, abduction, and robbery racket in Jhapa District. Mechi Zonal Police Chief Raviraj Shrestha said the authorities had established direct involvement of the group in multiple crimes over the previous two months.

Detail: JMMP cadres detonated a bomb at the house of local resident Shiva Puja Sah at Tegraha VDC-3, Rautahat District. JMMP 'central chairman' Bhagat Singh telephoned Police and claimed responsibility.

The Supreme Court stayed the Government's move to arrest and prosecute 21 UCPN-M cadres on murder charges relating to the insurgency period. A division bench directed that the named individuals not be arrested or detained pending further proceedings.
Organizations: Unified CPN-Maoist, Supreme Court of Nepal

Detail: Police arrested two persons — Pasang Moktan (33) of Parsa District and Dhan Bahadur Limbu (31) of Morang District — for the abduction of Khagendra Phuyal (28) of Jhapa District. Limbu was identified as an active YCL cadre. Phuyal had been abducted from Thamel, Kathmandu on 19 January.
Keywords: YCL, police, Parsa, Morang, Jhapa, Kathmandu, abduction

Detail: An unknown armed group shot and killed Rukshana Khatun (35), a female cadre of the UCPN-M Bhojpura State Committee, in Rautahat District.

UCPN-M cadres abducted six activists of the NC and CPN-UML in Udayapur District. The abducted were identified as NC activist Dik Bahadur Thapa (45), CPN-UML Lafa village committee chairman Kamal Rai (28), CPN-UML activists Parsuram Thapa (30), Kesar Rai (16), Karna Bahadur Rai (25), and his father Chunuklal Rai.
Ten students of Mahendra Higher Secondary School in Gorkha District were injured in an attack by YCL cadres.
An unidentified group shot and killed Paltu Mahato (49), a UCPN-M cadre, in Yagyabhumi VDC-4 in northern Dhanusha District.
Bhuwan Bahadur Karki (23), a CPN-UML cadre from Dulari, Morang District, was shot and killed by an unidentified assailant. His body was found near Budhikohola in Itahari, Sunsari District.

Sikendra Prasad Yadav (40), an Assistant Sub-Inspector of Police, was shot and killed by unidentified assailants in Bara District. Central leader of the JTMM-G, Jitendra Tiwari, telephoned local media to claim responsibility, calling the killing 'a warning to the State'.

A group of approximately ten discharged PLA combatants ransacked the Dhangadhi-based UNHCR office in Kailali District. The attackers said they acted because authorities had failed to rehabilitate them as promised.
Police arrested seven persons in connection with the incident.

A bomb detonated at Gauri Shanker Enterprises, a tractor shop owned by Biru Chawdhary, at Aspataal Road in Gulariya, Bardiya District, causing partial damage. An underground Tarai armed force claimed responsibility. No casualties were reported.

Nepal adopted its National Action Plan on Women, Peace and Security — the first country in South Asia to do so — based on UN Security Council Resolutions 1325 and 1820, emphasising the role of women in peace and security.

Madhav Thapa (40), a junior officer at the District Land Revenue Office in Bara, was shot and killed by an unidentified assailant. The Akhil Terai Mukti Morcha (ATMM) claimed responsibility, stating Thapa had been killed for financial irregularities at the office.

A UCPN-M cadre opened fire following an argument with a fellow cadre, Shyam Jarghamagar, at Gauri Puchchhar, Sindhuli District. The dispute was reported to have arisen from the internal 'two-line struggle' within the party.

Having exhausted domestic remedies, Yubraj Giri brought his case to the UN Human Rights Committee through Advocacy Forum Nepal and REDRESS. The Committee found in Yubraj Giri v. Nepal that Giri, a farmer arrested by the Royal Nepal Army in April 2004, had been wrongfully arrested and subjected to torture during 13 months of incommunicado detention, and that the anguish caused to his wife and two children constituted prohibited ill-treatment.
Organizations: Advocacy Forum-Nepal, Royal Nepal Army, Nepal Army

Detail: An explosion in a moving passenger bus injured at least 13 passengers near Bhediya Chowk in Rautahat District. The bus was travelling from the District headquarters to Chandranigahapur. The TJMP claimed responsibility, stating the bus was targeted for defying a bandh called on 23 February.
A bomb explosion carried out by the underground outfit Madhesh Mukti Samiti (MMS) damaged the Women Development Office in Gaur, Rautahat District. No casualties were reported.

An IED planted inside a passenger bus carrying approximately 40 passengers detonated at Milanchowk in Butwal, Rupandehi District, injuring over two dozen persons. One of the injured later died from his injuries on 28 March. No group claimed responsibility. On 26 March, seven persons had been similarly injured in Nepalgunj, Banke District in a comparable incident.

Nepal Army bomb disposal team neutralised a pressure cooker bomb planted at the Police office at Traffic Chowk in Biratnagar, Morang District. Brochures of the Janatantrik Madhesh Mukti Tigers were recovered from the site.
Keywords: Nepal Army, police, Morang, Biratnagar, bombing

Detail: The Ministry of Peace and Reconstruction revised data on the human cost of the decade-long armed conflict: 115,760 people were victims overall, of whom 17,000 were killed, 78,675 were displaced, approximately 1,600 disappeared, and 12,657 lost property.
Two cadres of JTMMT-R were shot and killed by unidentified assailants in Parsa District. The victims were identified as Raj Guru alias Chhote Lal Patel and Rabindra Patel of Chikani VDC.
Nepal Army reported that de-mining of minefields planted during the Maoist insurgency was nearing completion.

Four NA platoons, working with UNMAT, had cleared 45 of 53 minefields and planned to declare Nepal mine-free by mid-June. During the conflict, the NA had planted 53 minefields, and more than 300 IEDs had been planted collectively by the NA, Nepal Police, and Armed Police Force.
Four persons were injured when cadres of the underground ethnic outfit KJWP attacked Pangacha VDC in Bhojpur District.
Newly appointed Minister for Energy Gokarna Bista (CPN-UML) was attacked by unidentified assailants at Samakhushi Town Planning area, Kathmandu, sustaining injuries.

People of Jutpani VDC-3 in Chitwan blocked the East–West Highway at Ratnanagar for three hours after UCPN-M combatants from the Dinesh-Ramji Memorial Brigade attacked and injured six local residents in a dispute over the use of a football ground.
Police publicly identified three persons arrested in connection with the 27 March bus bombing in Butwal, Rupandehi District.
A bomb detonated at the Sagarmatha Transport Zonal Office in Siraha District. No casualties were reported.

A group of MJF-N cadres attacked the vehicle of party 'chairman' Upendra Yadav in Birgunj, Parsa District, after the party's Parsa District Committee was dissolved. Senior party leaders Renu Yadav and Hari Narayan Yadav were injured in the attack.
A member of the UCPN-M Nuwakot District Committee Secretariat was found to have been involved in the murder of three members of a family on 2 March at Newarpani, Bhadrutar-3, Nuwakot District.
Thirty-six VDC secretaries in Bhojpur District resigned en masse citing death threats from Bikas Kirati of the Shree Jung Force of the Kirat Janabadi Workers.

UN Deputy High Commissioner for Human Rights Kyung-Wha Kang called on Prime Minister Jhala Nath Khanal and urged 'gradual implementation' of the recommendations of the Universal Periodic Review held in January, and discussed a possible term extension of OHCHR-Nepal.

The ruling UCPN-M registered its proposed amendments to key clauses in the Truth and Reconciliation Bill, including provisions on action against human rights violators from the decade-long insurgency.

A Nepal Army squad disposed of a socket bomb planted at the house compound of Santaram Yadav, a resident of Hakui VDC-3, Rupandehi District. Pamphlets of the Janatantrik Madhesh Mukti Tigers were recovered from the site.

A study by DFHRI documented instances of extrajudicial killings in the Terai between 2008 and 2010. The report, based on inputs from the NHRC and OHCHR-Nepal, found that the State was implicated in 133 extrajudicial killings and armed groups in 129 cases during the period.
Organizations: OHCHR-Nepal, National Human Rights Commission of Nepal

Detail: NC activists attacked and injured six UCPN-M supporters at a school construction site in Dhyangphedi VDC-6, Nuwakot District. The UCPN-M District Committee alleged about 20 NC activists led by Sun Bahadur Tamang had carried out the attack.
At least 14 RPP activists were injured after UCPN-M cadres attacked them while they were attending a party workers' meeting at Madi, Chitwan District.

Anil Chamar alias Samrat, 'Western Regional Bureau Chief' of Madheshi Mukti Tigers (MMT), was killed by Police at Rohani Khola on the border of Nawalparasi and Rupandehi Districts, after he attacked a Police patrol team.
Keywords: police, MMT, Nawalparasi, Rupandehi, killing, clash

Detail: Three people were also injured in a bomb attack on a bus at Volti in Mahottari District.
Police Constable Ambika Pokharel was shot and wounded by unidentified assailants near the Aduwa Bridge in Birtamod, Jhapa District.
Bindeshwar Mahato, a UCPN-M cadre, was shot and killed by two motorcycle-borne assailants at Manaharwa Chok in Rampurbirta, Siraha District.

The UN Secretary-General's annual report on Children and Armed Conflict listed the UCPN-M among 52 armed forces globally that recruit or use children, kill or maim children, or commit sexual violence against children in armed conflict. This was the sixth consecutive year the Maoists appeared on the watch list. A total of 2,973 minors had been discharged from cantonments in 2010 under the tripartite action plan signed between the Maoists, the Government, and the UN in December 2009.
Dinesh Kumar Yadav (25) was injured when a bomb covered with black tape exploded at Lakkad-2, Janakpurdham, Dhanusha District, after he stepped on it.
A group of 60 UCPN-M cadres from the Chulachuli-based PLA First Division camp in Ilam attacked local people of Kamal Jhoda, injuring at least 12 persons.
A UCPN-M trade union cadre threatened to kill party Vice-chairman Baburam Bhattarai. The party's standing committee subsequently suspended Janak Bartaula for three months for making the threat.
The Ministry of Home Affairs was actively working to withdraw criminal cases against UCPN-M cadres, including serious charges dating from the insurgency period.
Organizations: Ministry of Home Affairs, Unified CPN-Maoist

Detail: A cadre of Terai Mukti Tigers, identified as Ashnarayan Saha Kalwar, sustained serious injury when an unidentified group opened fire at him along the By-pass road in Birgunj.
Police Constable Purna Shrestha was injured when an unidentified group detonated a socket bomb at Ganeshpur Police Station in Bardiya District, causing partial damage to the station.

Approximately 70 UCPN-M cadres abducted three CPN-UML cadres and a minor from Makwanpur District following a dispute over the relocation of a VDC office. The abducted were identified as Lalit Moktan, Tularam Moktan, Padmeshwor Shangtan, and Shangtan's 12-year-old daughter.
SFs arrested a teenager, Pawan Rai (14), at Kakadbhitta, Jhapa District, carrying 125 Orika explosives, a detonator, and wire.

Armed outfits planted IEDs at four locations in Sunsari and Udayapur Districts. In Sunsari, an IED was found at a savings and credit cooperative in Inaruwa, and another at the Revenue Investigation Office in Itahari — the latter claimed by the Janatantrik Terai Madhesh Mukti Party. In Udayapur's Dharan, the Khambuwan Mukti Morcha Samyukta planted an IED at the Inland Revenue Office and claimed another device at a crusher factory.

Bikram Saud (12) was killed and Babita Saud (5) was injured when an abandoned explosive device detonated at Bindabasini-7 in the far-western Achham District. The children had struck the device with a stone.
Bachha Yadav alias Shumsher Singh, District in-charge of JTMMM, was shot and killed by two unidentified assailants in Birgunj, Parsa District.
Sanjaya Lama, a cadre of the Youth Association Nepal (YAN), the youth wing of CPN-UML, was killed at Kabilas area in Chitwan District.

Police later arrested NC Tarun Dal district president Shiva Poudel and local leader Chandra Bahadur Lama in connection with the killing, establishing that Lama had opened fire during an argument over money being extracted from timber dealers.
A 'can bomb' planted by unidentified persons was recovered at the main gate of the house of businessman Devraj KC at Tulsipur Municipality-8, Dang District.
The whereabouts of 835 persons who disappeared during the decade-long Maoist insurgency remained unknown, according to OHCHR-Nepal and the National Human Rights Commission.
Organizations: OHCHR-Nepal, National Human Rights Commission of Nepal

Detail: At least one UCPN-M cadre was seriously injured and at least 11 others wounded in clashes between cadres loyal to party Chairman Prachanda and those loyal to Vice-chairman Mohan Baidya at Panchkhal, Kavre District. The clashes arose over the issue of handing the keys to PLA arms containers to the AISC, which the hardliner faction had opposed as 'suicidal'.
Keywords: PLA, UCPN-M, Baidya, Prachanda, Kavre, clash

Detail: Human rights organisations appealed to Prime Minister Baburam Bhattarai not to withdraw criminal cases filed during the armed conflict and different political movements, and not to offer general amnesty, in response to the four-point deal signed between the UCPN-M and the UDMF.
Organizations: United Democratic Madhesi Front, Unified CPN-Maoist

Detail: NHRC chairman Kedar Nath Upadhyaya wrote to Prime Minister Baburam Bhattarai asking him not to withdraw cases against those allegedly involved in crimes during various political movements.
Organizations: National Human Rights Commission of Nepal

Detail: A pressure cooker bomb detonated at the main gate of C Max Food, a Chinese-invested meat processing company in Narsingh VDC, Sunsari District. No casualties were reported. The Janatantrik Terai Madhesh Mukti Party (JTMMP) claimed responsibility.
CPN-UML-affiliated YAN central member Kamal Pathak sustained serious injuries when attacked by an unidentified group in the forest of Tikauli along the Ratnanagar–Bharatpur road section in Chitwan.

Police arrested seven cadres of ATMM-G, including Rameshwar Mandal alias Tufan Singh (27), on charges of extortion. Recovered items included a homemade bomb, bullets, leaflets, mobile phones, and diaries.
Police Head Constable Rahesh Raut Kurmi was shot and killed by a group of four assailants at Sanphulawa, Badaki Phulbariya VDC-8, Bara District.
Police said JTMMP cadres carried out the attack. One assailant was killed in the police response and another was arrested.
Om Jung Thapa (32), former Dailekh District chairperson of the CPN-UML-affiliated YAN, was injured when a group of locals led by YCL cadre Bam Bahadur KC attacked him at Chupra Bazar, Belpata VDC-6.
Nepal Army defused a socket bomb found at Ruiniwang of Majhing VDC-1 in Rolpa District. The bomb was uncovered during a landslide at the site.
A bomb detonated at the house of businessman Ramesh Thapa in Nepalgunj Municipality-1, Banke District. No damage was reported.
JTMMP faction chairman Bhagat Singh claimed responsibility.
An armed outfit detonated a socket bomb at the District Land Revenue Office in Gulariya Municipality-8, Bardiya District.
An unidentified group detonated a bomb at the residence of UCPN-M leader Raj Kumar Gaim in Bhardaha-1, Saptari District.
Two pressure cooker bombs were recovered from two different locations in Chatakpur, Kailali District.
Til Bahadur Pun, a boy from Kagate, Baluwatar VDC-8, Dailekh District, was seriously injured when he struck an abandoned socket bomb with a stone, causing an explosion.
Nepal Army defused two socket bombs found abandoned at Jaitpur, Hanku VDC-2, Jumla District.
Nepal Army defused a socket bomb planted near the District Forest Office in Dhanusha District. A pamphlet bearing the name of JTMMP 'military commander' Bhagat Singh was found at the site.
Two YCL cadres were injured in a clash between the Prachanda faction and the Mohan Baidya faction at the Prithvi Chowk-based YCL camp in Pokhara, Kaski District.
Keywords: YCL, Baidya, Prachanda, Kaski, Pokhara, clash

Detail: UCPN-M combatants of the Lokas Memorial Brigade in Kailali District assaulted four civilians from Pathariya VDC-2.

UCPN-M chairman Pushpa Kamal Dahal, NC president Sushil Koirala, CPN-UML chairman Jhala Nath Khanal, and UDMF representative Bijay Gachchhadar signed a seven-point agreement on the peace process. Under the agreement: 6,500 former Maoist combatants would be integrated into a new Directorate of the Nepal Army focused on development projects, forest and industrial security, and disaster rescue; those choosing rehabilitation would receive NPR 500,000 to 900,000 depending on rank; regrouping would begin within seven days and conclude by 23 November; and properties seized by the Maoists would be returned to their owners by 23 November, with the State compensating those who did not recover their property.
Keywords: UCPN-M, CPN-UML, Nepal Army, Maoist, UDMF, demobilisation, peace process
Organizations: United Democratic Madhesi Front, Unified CPN-Maoist, CPN-UML, Nepali Congress, Nepal Army

Detail: Seven-Point Agreement on Peace ProcessMajor political parties reach agreement on combatant integration, rehabilitation, and completion of the peace process.
A time bomb planted at the Land Revenue Office in Nepalgunj Municipality-13, Banke District, detonated, causing minor damage.

The Cabinet decided to recommend to President Ram Baran Yadav that a presidential pardon be granted to UCPN-M lawmaker Bal Krishna Dhungel, who had been convicted of murder and sentenced to life imprisonment by the Supreme Court for his involvement in the killing of Ujjan Shrestha of Okhaldhunga on 24 June 1998. Shrestha had been shot dead by the Maoists for allegedly spying on the party.
Keywords: UCPN-M, Maoist, Supreme Court, Okhaldhunga, killing
Organizations: Unified CPN-Maoist, Supreme Court of Nepal

Detail: OHCHR-Nepal expressed serious concern over a series of recent Government decisions to appoint, promote, or pardon public officials implicated in serious crimes and human rights abuses.
UCPN-M-affiliated All Nepal Peasants' Association (ANPA) declared that it would not return properties seized during the conflict.
SJMM cadres set ablaze two vehicles near Damechaur, Tasarpu VDC, Dhading District, for defying a bandh they had called.
The NC warned of protests if the Government did not withdraw its decision to recommend a presidential pardon for murder-convict lawmaker Bal Krishna Dhungel.
Nepal Army defused a bomb found near a bus park in Khalanga VDC-2. Kumar Ghaite Thapa, claiming to be 'chairperson' of underground outfit Janamukti Morcha Nepal, claimed responsibility.

Nepal Army defused a pressure cooker bomb planted at the house of Padam Yogi in Satbariya VDC-3. A pamphlet bearing the signature of JTMMP-Bhagat 'military commander' Bhagat Singh was found at the site.

The process of returning properties seized by the Maoists during the insurgency officially commenced with the handover of approximately 30 hectares of land owned by Binod Dhwoj Chand and family members at Rajapur VDC-7, Bardiya District.

One day after the UCPN-M returned land to its rightful owner Binod Dhwoj Chand in Bardiya, activists from the hardliner Mohan Baidya faction planted a party flag on the same land, declaring it recaptured.
UCPN-M Secretary CP Gajurel stated the party would not return seized land, calling the prior handover 'not an official party decision'.

An unidentified group detonated a socket bomb at the house of bank employee Chabbilal Pathak in Gulariya Municipality-4, Bardiya District. The 'Bardiya in-charge' of the Free Terai Madhesh Mukti Tiger, Ranbir Singh, claimed responsibility, stating Pathak had not supported the group.
An explosive device was found at the CPN-UML party office in Nepalgunj.
A bomb-disposal team safely neutralised it. A man identifying himself as a JTMM cadre telephoned journalists and claimed responsibility.

Five persons, including Sunsari District Superintendent of Police Raju Manandhar, were injured when a bomb planted by Khumbuwan Mukti Morcha (Samyukta) detonated at Itahari Chowk while Police were attempting to evacuate the area before defusing it.

The hardliner UCPN-M faction led by Mohan Baidya demanded the Dang local administration suspend the process of returning seized property in the District, insisting that land would not be returned without new pro-poor land-reform legislation.
OHCHR-Nepal's mandate expired after the Government of Nepal declined to renew it, leading to the closure of the mission.
Nepal Army bomb disposal unit defused two pressure cooker bombs near the East–West Highway in Kanchanpur District.
A time bomb exploded at the District Development Committee in Rautahat District, damaging window panes of the training hall. No casualties were reported.
JTMMM Rautahat in-charge Abhay Singh claimed responsibility.
Six local residents were injured when UCPN-M cadres attacked members of a Road Consumers' Committee at Khanayokharka, Thakre VDC-4, Dhading District.
JTMP cadres abducted Ramnandan Yadav (35), a farmer from Balawa VDC-6, Mahottari District, from his home.
UCPN-M cadres close to the Mohan Baidya hardliner faction seized two houses and approximately 22 hectares of land in Kapilvastu District in a fresh drive of property seizures.
Nepal Army bomb disposal team defused a socket bomb found at Mukti Chowk in Birtamod, Jhapa District.

Hundreds of disqualified former PLA combatants — 4,008 of whom had been discharged from cantonments without receiving any benefits — staged demonstrations against the UCPN-M leadership in Nepalgunj, Banke District.
Government Declines Renewal of OHCHR Nepal MandateOHCHR formally ends its field presence in Nepal after nearly seven years of monitoring conflict-era and post-conflict human rights issues.

UN Human Rights Committee Holds Nepal Responsible in Disappearance CasesThe UN Human Rights Committee issues landmark decisions on conflict-era disappearances, calling for investigations, reparations, and legal reforms, including criminalization of enforced disappearance.

NEFAD led the "Invisible No More" campaign aimed at generating solidarity and raising awareness about families of the disappeared in Nepal, including a photography project, memory gallery, fundraising and advocacy events, and a storytelling initiative.

Nepal Army bomb disposal team defused three explosive devices placed at Rajha Chowk along the Nepalgunj–Kohalpur road in Banke District. A flag and leaflet bearing the signature of "commander" Bharat Singh indicated the devices were planted by the Terai Janatantrik Madhesh Mukti Morcha (TJMMM).
Keywords: Nepal Army, Banke, Nepalgunj, Terai, bombing

Detail: Nepal Army defused a pressure cooker bomb found at Sangpang VDC-9 in Bhojpur District.
Nepal Army defused five bombs planted at Manpur, Banke, along the Nepalgunj–Gulariya road. Leaflets and flags of JTMMM-Bhagat Singh were recovered from the site.
Keywords: Nepal Army, Banke, Nepalgunj, Gulariya, bombing

Detail: Police arrested Dayaram Yadav (28) and Ram Das Yadav (26), both members of a JTMMM group, at Gadiyanpuruwa, Kamdi VDC-3, Banke District. A socket bomb, pistol and SLR ammunition, and electrical wire were recovered.

Nepal Army bomb disposal unit defused a time bomb at Chirauli Chok, Bhokraha VDC-9, Sunsari District. Pamphlets and flags of the Janatantrik Tarai Madhes Mukti Morcha (JTMMM) were recovered from the site.
Keywords: Nepal Army, Bhokraha, Sunsari, Tarai, Madhes, bombing

Detail: An IED planted inside a passenger bus by a militant outfit detonated in Tulsipur, Dang District. No casualties were reported.
JTMMM leaflets were found inside the bus.

Samyukta Madheshi Mukti Morcha (SMMM) detonated a bomb at a shop owned by Kul Prasad Kandel (35) at Radha Krishna Chowk, Gulariya Municipality-8, Bardiya District. Minor damage to the premises was reported; no casualties.

YCL cadres attacked two CPN-UML members, Jore Sunar (46) and Kalya Sunar (48), brothers from Odanku VDC, Kalikot District, with an iron rod, injuring both. The attackers included YCL District member Gante Luwar alias Akhanda and a cadre named Takka Singh.
Nepal Army bomb disposal team destroyed two pressure cooker bombs found on the Ghorahi–Tulsipur road in Dang District. Pamphlets of the underground outfit JTMMM were recovered from the scene.

A bomb explosion outside the Nepal Oil Corporation's central office at Babarmahal, Kathmandu — approximately 300 metres from Singha Durbar — killed three people and injured seven. The attack was attributed to Samyukta Jatiya Mukti Morcha-Bishwokranti (SJMM-B). The type of explosive used was consistent with devices used during the Maoist insurgency.
Keywords: Maoist, SJMM, Kathmandu, killing, bombing, clash

Detail: Kathmandu Police publicly identified six persons arrested in connection with the 27 February Babarmahal bombing that killed three and injured seven. The accused were identified as Bhim Bahadur Tamang, Nima Tamang, Buddhi Bahadur Gole, Prem Tamang, Suresh Lama, and Sagar Lama.
JTMMM detonated a pressure cooker bomb at the home of Prem Dangi, a transport entrepreneur, at Tikari, Tulsipur Municipality-8, Dang District. No casualties were reported.
Leaders of the three major parties discussed formation of the Truth and Reconciliation Commission and a Commission to Investigate Enforced Disappearances.
CPN-UML Chairman Jhala Nath Khanal said parties were near consensus on the enabling bills.

Radio Paschimanchal, an FM radio station belonging to the UCPN-M in Palpa District, was destroyed by an explosion carried out by an unidentified group. The third floor of the building was completely damaged. No casualties were reported. Detonator wire and bullets were recovered from the site.
An unidentified group detonated a socket bomb outside Pragati Higher Secondary School in Balaju, Kathmandu, at approximately 8 pm. Ground-floor window panes were damaged. No casualties were reported.

A group of approximately 100 UCPN-M cadres, led by Pyuthan member Man Bahadur Thapa and VDC secretary Gobardhan Thapa (50), looted 140 electricity poles intended for the electrification of Aglung VDC, Gulmi District. More than 20 villagers — including Radhika Malla (70), Manmaya Bishta (45), Mina Chand (40), and Bijay Chand (52) — were injured while attempting to stop the seizure.
YCL cadres armed with khukuris, spears, and batons surrounded village elders' homes and also assaulted police officers.
CPN-UML member Khum Bahadur GC (50), resident of Manmateriya VDC-9, Rupandehi District, was seriously injured when unidentified persons attacked him with an iron rod and batons near his home.
Three persons, including a PLA platoon commander, were arrested in Sunsari District for alleged involvement in arms dealing with an Indian national.
JTMMP detonated a bomb at the Naya Bus Park in Tulsipur Municipality-5, Dang District. One person sustained minor injuries.
Nepal Army defused a bomb near the Bypass Road in Ramgram Municipality, Nawalparasi District. A pamphlet of Madhesh Mukti Tiger (MMT) was recovered from the site.
Keywords: Nepal Army, MMT, Ramgram, Nawalparasi, bombing

Detail: Nepal Army bomb disposal team defused an IED at the Land Revenue Office in Bhashi, Bhimdatta Municipality-3, Kanchanpur District. No group claimed responsibility.

The three major parties — UCPN-M, NC, and CPN-UML — agreed to form a task force to prepare a proposal on the formation of the Truth and Reconciliation Commission and the Commission of Inquiry into Enforced Disappearances.
Organizations: Truth and Reconciliation Commission, Unified CPN-Maoist, CPN-UML, Nepali Congress

Detail: A bomb explosion damaged the Traffic Police office in Jaleshwar Municipal-5, Mahottari District, at 2:30 am. No casualties were reported. No group claimed responsibility.

Top leaders of political parties agreed to remove the list of non-pardonable crimes from the proposed TRC bill. Section 25 of the bill had listed murder in captivity, murder of unarmed persons, rape, torture, enforced disappearance, and abduction as crimes for which no amnesty could be granted. The decision was condemned by victims' groups and human rights organisations as a betrayal of victims.

The Supreme Court issued an interim order preventing the Government from implementing its decision to withdraw a murder case filed by Rupaiya Devi Kairin of Rautahat District. The case concerned the killing of Dev Sharan Mahato.
Cantonment Handover Begins
A pressure cooker bomb detonated at Duerali, Panchkanya VDC-5, Sunsari District, while a local resident, Narendra Rai, was removing a rope near the device. No casualties were reported.
At least two UCPN-M cadres were injured in a clash between rival party factions loyal to Chairman Pushpa Kamal Dahal and Senior Vice-chairman Mohan Baidya over local financial resources in Dhangadi.
A group calling itself Samyukta Jatiya Mukti Morcha (SJMM) planted an IED on the veranda of the home of Bara District NC Secretary Ram Prasad Chaudhary in Kalaiya, Bara District.
Nepal Army bomb disposal personnel were deployed.
Victims in Jajarkot District whose property was seized during the conflict reported they had not received compensation. The Peace Ministry stated that appeals had not followed due process.
The Supreme Court issued a mandatory order (writ of mandamus) to the Government and the Bara District Court directing them not to withdraw cases involving serious crimes, even of a political nature.
The three major political parties — UCPN-M, NC, and CPN-UML — agreed to merge the proposed separate commissions on Truth and Reconciliation and Enforced Disappearance into a single body.

JMMM detonated a bomb at the rented house of businessman Pawan Pokhrel in Kothiya, Gulariya VDC-10, Bardiya District, causing minor structural damage. JMMM in-charge Ranbir claimed responsibility, citing Pokhrel's refusal to pay NPR 100,000 as "donation" and alleged spying against the group.
A large quantity of bombs, bullets, and other ammunition was found buried near the Tila satellite cantonment in Gairigaun, Rolpa District, after local residents informed police.

At least five people were killed and approximately two dozen injured when an IED detonated at Ramanand Chowk in Janakpur, Dhanusha District. The bomb went off while activists from the Mithila Struggle Committee were holding a sit-in demanding the creation of an autonomous Mithila State. The JTMMM claimed responsibility.

One of the persons injured in the 30 April Janakpur bombing died of his injuries, bringing the confirmed death toll to five. The deceased was identified as Dipendra Das. The mastermind was later identified as Mukesh Choudhary alias Arjun Singh of the Tarai Students Liberation Front.

Supreme Court Justice Rana Bahadur Bam was shot and killed by unidentified assailants while travelling to work in Lalitpur District, Kathmandu. His bodyguard and a passenger in the vehicle were also wounded. A leaflet from a previously unknown group calling itself the Nepal Vad Party was found at the scene.
An IED detonated near Ananda Higher Secondary School in Jalbire, Sindhupalchowk District, where Finance Minister Barsha Man Pun was attending an UCPN-M programme. No casualties were reported.

Basanta Shahi, a cadre of the CPN-UML-aligned All Nepal Free Students Union (ANNFSU), was shot by unidentified persons in front of his home at Sohrakhutte, Kathmandu. His condition and the motive were not established.
Nepal Army inactivated a socket bomb found in a brick kiln at Kanthapur, Kalika VDC-6, Bardiya District.
Families of persons disappeared during the decade-long armed conflict reported they had been unable to receive interim relief due to delays in processing their applications.

Having exhausted domestic remedies, Dev Bahadur Maharjan — a teacher and farmer abducted from his home by the Royal Nepal Army in November 2003 and held illegally until January 2005 — brought his case to the UN Human Rights Committee through Advocacy Forum Nepal and REDRESS. The Committee found in Dev Bahadur Maharjan v. Nepal that he had been subjected to illegal detention, enforced disappearance, and torture, and that the anguish caused to his family constituted prohibited ill-treatment.
Organizations: Advocacy Forum-Nepal, Royal Nepal Army, Nepal Army

Detail: Students affiliated to ANNISU-R, the student wing of the Mohan Baidya-led CPN-Maoist, set ablaze a school bus belonging to Delhi Public School near Seutipul, Sunsari District. The school is located within BPKIHS grounds in Dharan.

Three students were critically injured in a clash between ANNFSU (CPN-UML-aligned) and ANNISU-Revolutionary (UCPN-Maoist-aligned) students at Khalnga Multiple Campus in Musikot, Rukum District. Those injured were ANNISU-Revolutionary Rukum District member Sushil Bista, Campus Unit chairman Sundar Sharma, and Campus Unit member Binod Oli, all of whom sustained deep head lacerations.
Keywords: CPN-UML, Maoist, Rukum, Revolutionary Rukum, clash

Detail: JTMM, led by Bhagat Singh, signed a four-point agreement with the Government at Pakali, Sunsari District, pledging to surrender all weapons within 20 days. As a gesture of commitment, the group immediately handed over seven pistols and one revolver to the District Administration Office.
The Government agreed to release the group's cadres from jail and withdraw cases filed against them.

Jaya Narayan Pasawan alias Barud Tyagi, JTMM "commander" for Mahottari, Sarlahi, and Dhanusha Districts, was killed in retaliatory police fire at Belaekdara along the Samasi–Jaleshwor road, Mahottari District.
Police Constable Surendra Chaudhary was injured in the encounter. A country-made pistol and two rounds of ammunition were recovered.
Rama Shankar Mandal, General Secretary of the Madheshi Janaadhikar Forum-affiliated Free Workers Union (FWU), was killed by unidentified assailants in Birgunj, Parsa District.

President Ram Baran Yadav signed an ordinance establishing a Commission on the Investigation of the Disappeared, Truth and Reconciliation. Human rights organisations and victims' groups had urged the President to return the ordinance, citing provisions allowing amnesty for perpetrators of serious violations as contrary to international law.

Amnesty International, Human Rights Watch, the International Commission of Jurists, and the Swiss Association against Impunity published an open letter urging President Yadav to return the transitional justice ordinance, citing provisions permitting amnesty for perpetrators of serious human rights violations as a violation of international law.
Organizations: Amnesty International, Human Rights Watch, International Commission of Jurists

Detail: The UN Resident and Humanitarian Coordinator stated that the transitional justice ordinance could "severely undermine access to justice for victims."
The JTMM group led by Bhagat Singh surrendered 63 homemade pistols and guns to the District Police Office in Sunsari, fulfilling the terms of the 5 August agreement with the Government.

The Ministry of Peace and Reconstruction reported that only 50 per cent of physical infrastructure damaged during the decade-long conflict had been reconstructed. Of 5,560 physical structures damaged, only 2,883 had been rebuilt.
The United States removed the UCPN-M from its global terrorist organisations list, stating the party had demonstrated a credible commitment to the peace and reconciliation process.
CPN-Maoist-Baidya cadres vandalized Janajagriti Higher Secondary School at Pithuwa, Chitwan District, for running classes in defiance of a shutdown they had imposed in the district.

The UN Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) released a comprehensive report documenting serious violations of international human rights law and international humanitarian law committed during the Nepal conflict, accompanied by a database of approximately 30,000 documents. The report archives records of up to 9,000 serious violations.
Maoist Combatant Integration and Rehabilitation CompletedA major milestone in implementing the Comprehensive Peace Agreement.
A socket bomb was found at the venue of a public meeting in Sunkuda, Bajhang District, where NC senior leader Sher Bahadur Deuba was scheduled to address the gathering.
UCPN-M Dhading District committee member Bijay Tamang was shot and killed by unidentified assailants in Gumdi VDC, Dhading District.
A former UCPN-M activist was murdered by unidentified assailants following his abduction from his home in Ratmate, Darkha VDC.
An IED detonated near Doorsanchar Chowk in Banepa, Kavre District. No casualties were reported.
The Government decided to withdraw criminal cases lodged against Maoist leaders and cadres during the decade-long insurgency, including cases of murder and abduction.
Ganga Maya and Nanda Prasad Adhikary began a hunger strike demanding justice for the killing of their son Krishna Prasad. Both were subsequently admitted to Bir Hospital as their health deteriorated.

Victims and Civil Society Submit Reform ProposalsVictims' groups, lawyers, human rights organizations, and civil society coalitions submit approximately fifteen rounds of recommendations and formal submissions calling for the proposed ordinance to comply with constitutional guarantees, victims' rights, and international human rights standards, while opposing provisions that could permit amnesty for serious violations.

An armed group of about 10 persons belonging to CPN-Maoist (Baidya) vandalized the corporate office of NDEX at Tinkune, Kathmandu, demanding the company pay a hefty amount as donation — a pattern of coercion of civilian populations and businesses.

Deputy Prime Minister Narayan Kaji Shrestha said the Government was ready to make necessary amendments to the TRC ordinance — currently pending at the Office of the President — for setting up transitional justice mechanisms.

Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Narayan Kaji Shrestha stated that the Government was in favour of forming a TRC to investigate conflict-era human rights violations, affirming Government commitment to punishing the guilty and ensuring justice to victims.
Mohan Baidya-led CPN-Maoist warned the party would take up arms if the state cannot assure the rights of the people, threatening resumption of people's war.

Prime Minister Baburam Bhattarai and UCPN-M Chairman Prachanda met ambassadors of major foreign missions on Nepal's failure to start the transitional justice process. Foreign representatives highlighted the country's failure to provide justice to conflict-era victims and pressed for earliest formation of a credible TRC.
Organizations: Truth and Reconciliation Commission, Unified CPN-Maoist

Detail: NHRC Spokesperson Gauri Pradhan warned that if Nepal failed to establish the TRC and CEIDP, international jurisdiction would become active — referencing the January 3 arrest of serving Colonel Kumar Lama in the United Kingdom.
Organizations: National Human Rights Commission of Nepal, Truth and Reconciliation Commission

Detail: Nine opposition parties, including CPN-UML and NC, organised a protest assembly against the murder of journalist Dekendra Thapa, killed during the Maoist insurgency approximately eight years earlier.
UCPN-M coordinator Ganga Karki warned of retaliation against journalists and human rights activists seeking justice in the Dekendra Thapa murder case.
CPN-Maoist (Baidya) central committee planned to revive the insurgency-era organizational command structure within the party, including centralizing power in a military-style command system.

CPN-Maoist (Baidya) demonstrated in Kathmandu demanding the release of cadres arrested in connection with the murder of journalist Dekendra Thapa. A speaker warned that if conflict-period cases were "rediscovered," the country would return to conflict.
Keywords: CPN-Maoist, Maoist, Baidya, Kathmandu, killing, press

Detail: Security forces defused three bombs allegedly planted by CPN-M Revolutionary at three separate locations in Butwal (Rupandehi), Biratnagar (Morang), and Bankatuwa (Banke). Leaflets of CPN-M Revolutionary were recovered from all sites.

UCPN-M Chairman Pushpa Kamal Dahal apologized for the Badarmude incident in Chitwan — one of the worst attacks on civilians during the Maoist insurgency — in which 39 passengers including three army personnel were killed and 72 injured in an ambush on June 6, 2005. A relief package of Rs. 6 million was announced for victims.

President Ram Baran Yadav signed a revised Truth, Reconciliation and Disappearance Ordinance. The ordinance granted the commission discretion to recommend amnesty for perpetrators, excluding some serious crimes such as rape, but not explicitly excluding gross violations including torture, extrajudicial killing, and enforced disappearance.

CPN-Maoist (Baidya) cadres systematically disrupted the voters' registration process in multiple districts including Jhapa, Tanahun, Baglung, Lalitpur, and Bhaktapur, looting election documents, smashing equipment, and threatening officials — targeting civilian electoral infrastructure.
Keywords: CPN-Maoist, Maoist, Baidya, Jhapa, Baglung, Lalitpur, Bhaktapur, elections

Detail: TRC Ordinance PromulgatedThe government adopts the Truth and Reconciliation Commission and Disappearance Commission Ordinance through executive action.

Four major political parties agreed to remove the amnesty provision from the TRC draft ordinance, following NC and CPN-UML objections to pardoning those involved in conflict-era human rights violations. The TRC ordinance was to be revised accordingly.
Organizations: Truth and Reconciliation Commission, CPN-UML, Nepali Congress

Detail: An ordinance was drafted to establish a commission for investigation, truth-finding, and reconciliation regarding disappeared persons — verified at the Supreme Court (Writ Petition) by Ram Bhandari and Raju Chapagain.

The ICJ urged the newly appointed head of the interim election Government, Khil Raj Regmi, to step down as Chief Justice to preserve judicial independence and the rule of law, and acknowledged the Supreme Court's prior strong commitment to upholding human rights in Nepal.
A group affiliated with CPN-Maoist (Baidya) vandalized the head office of Ncell, Nepal's largest private telecom company, in Kathmandu.

A group of seven conflict victim organizations, led by Ram Bhandari, filed a petition at the Supreme Court against the TRC ordinance, raising concerns over political amnesty, forced reconciliation without victim consent, and lack of victim participation.
Organizations: Truth and Reconciliation Commission, Supreme Court of Nepal

Detail: The Government formed a three-member committee headed by Home Minister Madhav Ghimire to negotiate with CPN-Maoist (Baidya) and other poll-opposing parties.
CPN-Maoist (Baidya) cadres chased away Election Commission officials in Kavre District; the party formally disrupted voters' registration across multiple districts.

CPN-Maoist (Baidya) cadres captured approximately 35 acres of private land belonging to Interim Election Council Chairman Khil Raj Regmi in Bardiya District, along with over 100 acres belonging to local landowners — continuing a pattern of forced land seizure.
Keywords: CPN-Maoist, Maoist, Baidya, Bardiya, extortion/land, elections

Detail: A nationwide general strike (bandh) called by the 33-party alliance led by CPN-Maoist (Baidya) crippled normal life across the country.

A bomb was planted near a mobile citizenship distribution camp at Mainaghat-based Saraswati School in Nawalparasi District, targeting civilians and officials. Anti-Government slogans were found at the site.
A Nepali national was arrested at Nepalgunj in Banke District with 30 detonators and 15 packets of explosives from the Nepal-India border.
1,606 illegal weapons were collected from districts in the far-west as part of a nationwide arms collection drive.
Two bombs were found at Mainaghat-based Saraswati School in Nawalparasi District, planted by an unidentified group targeting a mobile camp for citizenship distribution and voter registration.

Two Armed Police Force (APF) personnel were injured in a clash with CPN-Maoist (Baidya) in Mainatada village, Surkhet District. The clash occurred when APF intervened to stop Maoist activists from disrupting an integrated mobile service camp organised by the local administration.
Keywords: CPN-Maoist, APF, police, Maoist, Baidya, Surkhet, clash, demobilisation

Detail: CPN-Maoist (Baidya) cadres allegedly looted approximately five quintals of food supplies being transported to a mobile camp in Jima village, Mugu District, in an effort to obstruct the mobile camp's operation.
Baidya-led CPN-Maoist announced control over Surya Boarding Secondary School in Khandbari, Sankhuwasabha District — targeting civilian educational infrastructure.
UCPN-M cadres cut off the water supply mains to two VDCs in Sindhupalchok District, causing civilian hardship.
CPN-Maoist (Baidya) Secretary Dev Gurung warned that declaration of an election date would lead to "national liberation war or civil war."
CPN-Maoist (Baidya) cadres captured 16.8 bigha of land owned by UCPN-M local leaders in Fattepur Village, Banke District — continuing a pattern of forced land seizure.
Keywords: CPN-Maoist, UCPN-M, Maoist, Baidya, Banke, extortion/land

Detail: Two people, including a Nepal Army soldier, were shot by unidentified motorcycle-borne gunmen in Janakpur, Dhanusa District. The Janatantrik Terai Mukti Morcha (Rajan Mukti) claimed responsibility.
An IED was recovered near Interim Election Council Chairman Khil Raj Regmi's house in Palpa District.
Nepal Army personnel defused the pressure cooker bomb; pamphlets of CPN-Maoist-Revolutionary were found at the site.

UCPN-M launched a new donation drive in Bara, Parsa, and Rautahat Districts, sending sealed letters with audio CDs to approximately 24 chiefs of Government offices and large businesses, demanding between NPR 25,000 and NPR 100,000 — a pattern of coercion of civilian populations.
A Nepal Army bomb disposal squad defused a socket bomb recovered in Siraha District. The device was described as powerful and capable of causing large-scale casualties.
CPN-Maoist (Baidya) cadres seized 70 bigha of land belonging to a private individual in Rupandehi District.

Twelve armed Tarai outfits announced their unification under the banner of JTMM (Jaya Mukti faction) with an agenda to foil the upcoming CA elections, representing a significant convergence of armed groups.

Having exhausted domestic remedies, Shanta Sedhai brought her case to the UN Human Rights Committee through Advocacy Forum Nepal and REDRESS. The Committee found in Shanta Sedhai v. Nepal that Nepal was responsible for the enforced disappearance of Mukunda Sedhai — arrested by plain-clothes army personnel in December 2003 and never seen again — in violation of his right to life and freedom from torture, and that the anguish caused to his wife and two children constituted prohibited ill-treatment.

A faction of CPN-Maoist (Baidya) detonated an IED at the Panchayat Silver Jubilee Pillar in Hetauda town, Makwanpur District. No casualties were reported. Pamphlets and banners opposing the CA elections were recovered from the site.
Keywords: CPN-Maoist, Maoist, Baidya, Makwanpur, Hetauda, bombing, elections

Detail: MJF-N District Secretary Prakash Sah was shot and injured by an unidentified motorcycle-borne gang at the Mahottari District party office. The JTMM-R, an armed outfit operating in Madhesh, claimed responsibility.
A bomb exploded at the NC party office in Siraha District. The JTMM (East) claimed responsibility, citing the "hill-dominated regime's" exploitation of the Madhes.

CPN-Maoist (Baidya) leader (unnamed) stated the party had "trained youths in Dang, Banke, Bardiya, Kailali and Kanchanpur to disrupt the poll process," claiming they were "fully capable of challenging the security forces."
Keywords: CPN-Maoist, Maoist, Baidya, Dang, Banke, Bardiya, Kailali, elections

Detail: In a blatant violation of the election code of conduct, CPN-Maoist (Baidya) ordered businessman Krishna Bhagat Pradhan of Sankhuwasabha District not to sell any property and issued a warning demanding NPR 20 million — targeting civilian economic actors.

The Nepal Army Integration process concluded its final phase when 70 former Maoist combatants were commissioned as Lieutenants in the Nepal Army at the Nepal Military Academy, Bhaktapur — marking the formal end of combatant integration seven years after the Comprehensive Peace Agreement.
UCPN-M cadres attacked a Police constable deployed to provide security to an NC leader in Rukum District, snatching his pistol.
The ICRC released its updated report "Missing Persons in Nepal: Updated List 2013," stating that of 3,777 victims of forced disappearances, 1,360 people still remain unaccounted for.
UCPN-M Chairman Pushpa Kamal Dahal revealed that his party had ties with Sri Lanka's LTTE during the decade-long armed conflict in Nepal, and that the LTTE had also sought help from the Maoist side.

CPN-Maoist (Baidya) General Secretary Ram Bahadur Thapa directed the party's rank and file to be mentally prepared to take up weapons to disrupt the CA elections, stating the party would supply weapons to its cadres in every village.

CPN-Maoist (Baidya) conducted underground combat training for its cadres in Garayala village, western Rukum District — a weeklong residential training in which 36 cadres were trained in warfare skills.
Police arrested UCPN-M cadre Ram Prasad Adhikari in connection with the murder of Krishna Prasad Adhikari in 2004, who was killed by the Maoists on the "charge" of spying.
UCPN-M demanded all such conflict-era cases be resolved through the TRC.
Organizations: Truth and Reconciliation Commission, Unified CPN-Maoist

Detail: CPN-Maoist (Baidya) Vice Chairman CP Gajurel issued a public threat to CA election candidates: "If anyone files candidacy by disregarding our request, there is no guarantee that the candidate will return home," and directed cadres to ban candidates from entering villages — a direct threat to civilian participation in elections.
A bandh imposed by CPN-Maoist (Baidya) shut down the Kathmandu Valley, closing transport, markets, schools, and colleges.
Twelve persons were injured when an IED exploded at the District Survey Office of Sarlahi District. A pamphlet of Akhil Tarai Mukti Morcha (Goit faction) was recovered from the site.

CPN-Maoist (Baidya) launched a "donation campaign" in Rukum District, preparing a list of approximately 500 targets — Government and NGO staffers, entrepreneurs, businessmen, and contractors — and demanding donations between NPR 20,000 and NPR 200,000.

CPN-Maoist (Baidya) launched a massive nationwide campaign to collect funds for anti-election activities, sending threatening electronic messages, letters, and phone calls demanding donations from individuals, state-owned institutions, private companies, schools, banks, manpower agencies, and industries.
CPN-Maoist (Baidya) cadres captured electoral education materials in Thal Bazaar, Jajarkot District.

A bandh called by the Federated Limbuwan State Council (FLSC) hit nine eastern Districts — Jhapa, Ilam, Taplejung, Morang, Sunsari, Terhathum, Dhankuta, Panchthar, and Sankhuwasabha — targeting the CA election process.
Keywords: Jhapa, Ilam, Morang, Sunsari, elections, protest

Detail: Unidentified assailants on a motorcycle shot at CPN-UML FPTP candidate Mohammad Alaam in Bara District. He was hit on the head.
Police arrested Muneshwor Mandal, alias Manish, District Commander of the JTMM (Jwala Singh faction) in Saptari District, accused of involvement in four kidnapping cases, a murder, and bus arson.

CPN-Maoist (Baidya) delivered letters to candidates of NC, CPN-UML, UCPN-M, and others in Sunsari District, warning them not to participate in the CA elections — a pattern of intimidation of civilian candidates.
Keywords: CPN-Maoist, UCPN-M, CPN-UML, Maoist, Baidya, Sunsari, elections
Organizations: CPN-Maoist, Unified CPN-Maoist, CPN-UML, Nepali Congress

Detail: CPN-UML candidate Mohammad Alam, shot on October 4 in Bara District, succumbed to his injuries.
Ten persons were injured in a clash between NC and CPN-Maoist (Baidya) cadres at Bhiyee village, Mugu District.
UCPN-M cadres looted election publicity materials belonging to NC in Rukum District.
One person was injured in a clash between MPRF-D and NC cadres in Siraha District.
Seventeen persons were injured in a clash between TMDP and MPRF-D supporters in Godaita village, Sarlahi District, involving sharp weapons and spears.
Five MPRF-D and approximately twelve TMDP activists were injured.
Four NC activists and a schoolteacher were attacked by masked men in Bafikot village, Rukum District. NC alleged that the assailants were YCL (UCPN-M youth wing) cadres.
CPN-Maoist (Baidya) enforced a bandh in Bajura, Achham, and Doti Districts in the far west.
At least three persons were injured in clashes between NC and UCPN-M cadres during election campaigns in Radibazaar, Rukum District.

A team of 15–20 CPN-Maoist (Baidya) cadres looted and burned voters' education materials sent to three VDCs of Parbat District, also warning candidates to stop election publicity campaigns — targeting civilian electoral infrastructure.

CPN-Maoist (Baidya) cadres set ablaze a UCPN-M campaign jeep in Kaski District. Separately, a group sprinkled acid on a UCPN-M cadre's wife in Laharepauwa VDC, Rasuwa District, and made off with election materials.
Keywords: CPN-Maoist, UCPN-M, Maoist, Baidya, Kaski, Laharepauwa, Rasuwa, elections

Detail: Twelve people were injured when UCPN-M and CPN-UML cadres clashed in Swara VDC, Gorkha District.
CPN-Maoist (Baidya) cadres vandalized campaign vehicles used by CPN-UML Secretary Shanker Pokhrel in Dang District.
UCPN-M candidate Sancha Pal Maden and at least 15 others were injured; three, including Maden, were in serious condition.
A Nepal Army bomb disposal unit recovered and defused a bomb planted at a UCPN-M campaign office in Dharan municipality, Sunsari District.
Keywords: UCPN-M, Nepal Army, Dharan, Sunsari, bombing

Detail: A UCPN-M candidate's campaign jeep was set ablaze in Hetauda town, Makwanpur District.
Six persons were injured in a clash between NC and MJF-N cadres during an election publicity campaign in Mahottari District.
A bomb was found and defused at CPN-UML's contact office in Nawalparasi District.
Campaign vehicles belonging to an NC candidate (Dhankuta-2) and a CPN-UML candidate (Dang) were torched by unidentified persons.
CPN-Maoist (Baidya) cadres planted an IED to target UCPN-M Chairman Dahal's election program in Charikot town, Dolakha District.
Keywords: CPN-Maoist, UCPN-M, Maoist, Baidya, Dolakha, bombing, elections

Detail: Nepal Army bomb disposal team defused it.
A bomb exploded at a house in Ramjakot VDC, Tanahun District, where NC Vice-President and candidate Ram Chandra Paudel was staying. No casualties, but his vehicle was damaged.
Six persons were injured when CPN-UML and UCPN-M cadres clashed in Kotila VDC, Bajura District.
Multiple campaign vehicles belonging to UCPN-M candidates in Morang and Sunsari Districts were set ablaze by unidentified groups.
At least two bombs were found near Surkhet airport on the route taken by UCPN-M leader Baburam Bhattarai.
Nepal Army bomb disposal team defused them.
A CPN-Maoist (Baidya) bandh brought vehicular movement to a halt in the mountainous Far-western region Districts including Dadeldhura, Baitadi, Darchula, Doti, Achham, and Bajura.
Six Police constables were injured in a clash with YCL cadres (UCPN-M youth wing) in Dunai, Dolpa District. Forty-nine YCL cadres were arrested.
Three persons were injured in a clash between UCPN-M and NC cadres in Muru VDC, Rukum District.
An NC candidate's campaign vehicle was torched in Banepa town, Kavrepalanchok District by motorcycle-borne assailants who sprayed petrol.
An unidentified group planted a bomb at the site of a planned NC election meeting in Durgamandu VDC, Doti District.
Nepal Army defused it, delaying the meeting by two and a half hours.
A team of UCPN-M election campaigners was fired upon while returning from a campaign in Jaljala VDC, Sankhuwasabha District.
Police recovered an SLR rifle, 11 rounds, wires, and a bomb-making battery near the site.
Seven persons were injured in a clash between UCPN-M and NC cadres in Tikha VDC, Doti District.
A bomb was recovered near a campaign event for CPN-UML leader Subash Chandra Nembang in Illam District, near a school.
A nationwide bandh and a 10-day transport strike were called by the 33-party alliance led by CPN-Maoist (Baidya) to foil the November 19 CA election.
Five pressure cooker bombs were recovered at various locations in Siraha District, including three at Lahan and two at Golbazaar.
An IED was exploded at the under-construction UCPN-M party office in Dhankuta District.
At least six NC and CPN-UML cadres were injured in a clash between the two sides in Khotang District.
A minor, Abhisekh Lama, was injured when unidentified assailants hurled a petrol bomb at a microbus in Kumaripati, Lalitpur District, during the transport strike.
Police arrested a member of the ANTMM armed outfit in Saptari District. A socket bomb, pistol, and bullets were recovered.
Three UCPN-M cadres were attacked by CPN-Maoist (Baidya) cadres while they were sleeping at Dime VDC, Jajarkot District.
Keywords: CPN-Maoist, UCPN-M, Maoist, Baidya, Dime, Jajarkot, clash

Detail: Two passengers were injured when an unidentified group hurled petrol bombs at two vehicles carrying Indian tourists in Bandipur, Tanahun District.
Two tourist buses were torched in Lekhnath, Kaski District.
UCPN-M Chairman Dahal had a narrow escape when a roadside bomb was detonated as his vehicle passed through Kanchanpur District en route to an election rally in Belauri.
